description: Company Description Arista Networks is an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large data center, campus and routing environments. What sets us apart is our relentless pursuit of innovation. We leverage the latest advancements in cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and software-defined networking to provide our clients with a competitive edge in an increasingly interconnected world. Our solutions are designed to not only meet the current demands of the digital landscape but to also anticipate and adapt to future challenges. At Arista we value the diversity of thought and perspectives that each employee brings to the table. We believe that fostering an inclusive environment, where individuals from various backgrounds and experiences feel welcome, is essential for driving creativity and innovation. Our commitment to excellence has earned us several prestigious awards, such as Best Engineering Team, Best Company for Diversity, Compensation, and Work-Life Balance. At Arista, we take pride in our track record of success and strive to maintain the highest standards of quality and performance in everything we do. Job Description Who You’ll Work With The Commodity Manager is responsible to develop Arista’s commodity strategies for Thermal / Heat Sinks (experience with Front end Power Supplies is a plus) in order to drive time to market, continuity of supply and meet cost reduction initiatives. You'll work across the supply chain to support operations and will be collaborating closely with Engineering on sourcing strategies. The role will require the individual to be familiar with the complete range of strategic sourcing activities. This includes the analysis of spend, the formulation of and implementation of commodity strategies, the negotiation of contracts and the ongoing management of strategic supplier relationships. What You’ll Do Creates, implements, and maintains sourcing strategies for assigned commodities to support company requirements. Undertakes spend analysis, supplier assessment and supplier selection to agreed processes. Develops and implements commodity strategies in line with company and manufacturing initiatives to improve supply chain efficiencies and reduce the total cost of supply chain management. Builds cost models (TAC/should cost) to validate commodity strategies and to understand cost drivers. Coordinates all activities with Engineering, NPI, and suppliers to ensure the selection of parts with long lifetimes and solid supply availability. Working with the site supply chain leads, this individual will manage relationships with suppliers on behalf of Arista. Develops a robust commodity supply base which creates and sustains a competitive advantage for Arista, utilizing global markets, leveraging spend, and best in class technologies. Monitors/reports on priority projects and savings. Ensures that agreed strategic sourcing targets for cost reduction are met in the commodity portfolio. This includes responsibility for meeting improvement plan targets and year on year cost reductions. Provides support to NPI teams as required to meet target costs and establish program cost models. Negotiations and management of cost models for suppliers to include "hard" money (such as price, volume discounts, etc.) and "soft" money (such as expertise, technical backup, etc.) in the context of Total Acquisition Cost (TAC) and Total Opportunity Cost (TOC). Identification and delivery of opportunities for cost reduction. Provides input for annual and long-term savings targets. Trains/Mentors junior supply chain personnel on strategic sourcing process. Ensures appropriate performance measure (Technology, Quality, Cost and Delivery) of supply base and feedback of results. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Operations or Engineering required; Master’s degree preferred. Minimum 10 years’ experience in a networking environment (preferred), electronics or electrical, purchasing, commodity management and materials management positions. CPIM, CIRM, and/or C.P.M. desired. Excellent Program and Project Management Skills. Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing and Process Variation Reduction (Six Sigma) concepts and tool sets as they relate to materials management. Utilize strong team building abilities to lead cross-functional process improvement teams and lead change within the organization. Ability to coordinate cross-site, multi-functional objectives. Ability to interface and positively influence at all levels through excellent communication skills. Understanding of assigned commodities, materials, and manufacturing processes. Strong PC application skills. Including complement of Microsoft Office Software, with strong capabilities in Project and Access. Compensation Information The new hire base pay for this role has a salary range of $142,000 to $188,000. Arista offers different pay ranges based on work location, so that we can offer consistent and competitive pay appropriate to the market. The actual base pay offered will be based on a wide range of factors, including skills, qualifications, relevant experience, and work location. The pay range provided reflects base pay only and in addition certain roles may also be eligible for discretionary Arista bonuses and equity. Employees in Sales roles are eligible to participate in Arista’s Sales Incentive Plan, which pays commissions calculated as a percentage of eligible sales. US-based employees are also entitled to benefits including medical, dental, vision, wellbeing, tax savings and income protection. The recruiting team can share more details during the hiring process specific to the role and location Additional Information Arista Networks is an equal opportunity employer. Arista makes all hiring and employment-related decisions in a non-discriminatory manner without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin or any other factor determined to be unlawful under applicable federal, state, or law law. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

description: JOB SUMMARY The Senior Planner/Buyer, Contract Manufacturing is appointed to their position by the Supervisor, Contract Manufacturing Supply Chain. Review supplier capacities and supply risks; recommend tooling and capital investments and/or dual sourcing to protect continuity and support growth. Perform demand/supply and market analysis to assess short and long-term pricing trends, raw material availability, and industry capacity for liners and paper. Manage sourcing and trial data quality; cleanse and maintain data and deliver reporting/dashboards (trial results, material performance, cost comparisons) to enable decision-making. description: Career Area: Procurement Job Description: Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc. When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it. Employees in this position work directly with a specific group of suppliers in the Forgings Supply Chain and cross functional clients daily to help ensure uninterrupted availability of material through the Global Supply Chain to worldwide locations in direct response to our customers’ requirements. The Procurement Specialist have a direct impact on improving and sustaining supplier performance with impact to quality, cost, delivery, and ultimately to customer commitments and satisfaction. Responsibilities include day-to-day and strategic supplier management including, but not limited to: purchase order placement, follow-up, issue resolution, communication of demand and forecasts, preparing contracts, negotiating contract terms, providing solutions to a wide range of issues, managing supplier relationships and performance metrics, facilitating communications and mitigating risk that could impact Solar’s ability to meet customer commitments or business plan. This position acts with a sense of urgency and is diligent in providing timely support to internal clients and external customers. This individual operates in compliance with corporate and Supply Chain policies and procedures and continuously practices and demonstrates Safety and acts in adherence to Our Values in Action. A Procurement Specialist will manage relationships of moderately strategic to complex suppliers. This individual has no direct reports but works within a team structure typically including a Sourcing Specialist, Supply Chain Coordinator/Planner, Supplier Technical Engineer and reports directly to a Supply Chain Manager. There is an expectation to both participate and lead projects from conception to maturity that directly support organizational objectives. The work environment is office based with occasional visits to internal production areas as well as external supplier sites, which may involve domestic and/or international travel. The successful candidate will have demonstrated skills and competencies that include: Supply Chain Management – Ensures procurement processes meets audit, regulatory, and legal standards. Develops and maintain relationships with internal clients and supplier executives. Applies advanced Supply Chain knowledge to manage processes, establish policies, and develop value-adding strategies. Monitors and manages ownership of risk from financial, business continuation, and compliance perspectives. Supplier Management - Manages each relationship of moderately complex suppliers. Drives cost management through identifying and implementing opportunities for cost reduction, utilizes cost modeling techniques, and analyzing TCO to ensure the best overall value to Solar. Manages and maintains the supplier relationship at a day-to-day and strategic level. Day-to-day activities include purchase order issuance and maintenance, grief resolution, and business review meetings. Supplier Selection - Strategic activities include working with the Supply Chain Leadership and/or Sourcing Specialist to define the buyer-supplier relationship and the strategic direction (Hold, Grow, Consolidate, Exit). Supports NPI, global strategic sourcing, and supplier selection to ensure flexible capacity and consistent supply from qualified suppliers to support business objectives. Contract Management – Develops agreements that align with sourcing strategies and utilizes appropriate standard Solar contracts with legal review, as required. Identifies and balances key risks at all stages. Integral in tracking contract execution, leading contract teams, closing contracts, and enforcing any applicable rights beyond contract completion. Works closely with users defining supplier performance measurements and reporting frameworks. Leads commercial negotiations and is accountable for contract execution and maintenance (NDA’s, GP’s, PSAs, JDAs, etc). Negotiation – Creates negotiation strategies based on thorough knowledge of business requirements. Communicates negotiation strategies and parameters to negotiating team and defines roles. Able to ethically execute negotiation strategy for moderately critical and complex items displaying varied negotiation techniques to achieve best results. Identifies and resolves areas of risk. Cost Management – Applies business strategies to daily activities, contributes to make-buy decisions, identifies market opportunities, gaps and trends. Understands, applies and coaches others in building and analyzing Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) models. Purchasing Execution – Resolves highly complex purchasing related grief issues with minimal assistance. Manages PO’s from issuance through invoice, and support Supply Chain initiatives. Understands financial markets and is able to analyze cost/pricing models. Risk Management – Identifies and mitigates risk to the business. Executes risk mitigation strategies to avoid Supply Chain disruption. Initiates and promotes cross functional teaming in Supplier development, problem resolution, and continuous improvement efforts. Required Qualifications The position requires a Bachelor’s degree with 5-7 years of purchasing experience or equivalent experience in similar business role. Alternatively, the qualified candidate can have a Master’s Degree in Business, Engineering, Supply Chain or other related field with 3-5 years of purchasing experience or equivalent experience in similar business role. Experience with ERP software and proficient with MS Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Visio). Fluent in Business English in written and oral form. Preferred Qualifications Supply Chain Certification from a professional institution (ASCM, APICS, IIPMR, ISCEA, ISM, or comparable International Certification). Affiliation(s) with ISM, ASCM/APICS or comparable professional purchasing organizations. Demonstrated background(s) in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, Manufacturing, or related field. Individual Contributor Behavior consisting of customer commitment, priority setting, proactiveness, accountability and professional growth. 6-Sigma certification as a Blackbelt or Greenbelt with project and team leadership experience. Understanding and application of Lean Manufacturing principles. Strong Communication and Analytical Skill Sets. Proven Influencing and Interpersonal Skill Sets. Summary Pay Range: $112,704.00 - $169,056.00 Compensation and benefits offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, job level, market location, job-related knowledge, skills, individual performance and experience. Please note that salary is only one component of total compensation at Caterpillar. Benefits: Subject to plan eligibility, terms, and guidelines. This is a summary list of benefits. Visa Sponsorship is not available for this position. Posting Dates: October 9, 2026 - October 23, 2026 Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen. description: We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters. Ford’s Electric Vehicles, Digital and Design (EVDD) team is charged with delivering the company’s vision of a fully electric transportation future. EVDD is customer-obsessed, entrepreneurial, and data-driven and is dedicated to delivering industry-leading customer experience for electric vehicle buyers and owners. You’ll join an agile team of doers pioneering our EV future by working collaboratively, staying focused on only what matters, and delivering excellence day in and day out. Join us to make positive change by helping build a better world where every person is free to move and pursue their dreams. In this position... The global supply chain behind UEV must be as innovative as the platform itself. As Global Supply Manager, you’ll own the end-to-end sourcing strategy for critical vehicle spend. You’ll partner with engineering from concept through launch, using first-principles decision-making to deliver breakthrough outcomes. You will lead global supplier negotiations and structure commercial agreements that protect program timing without sacrificing cost leverage. You’ll also play a central role in one of the most complex challenges facing the industry today: designing a supply chain that is resilient to geopolitical risk and compliant with a rapidly evolving global trade and tariff environment. What you'll do... Own end-to-end sourcing strategy for critical spend areas across the UEV platform and follow-on advanced EV programs from sourcing strategy development through SOP, including supplier selection, contracting, and ongoing cost, quality, and delivery performance. Partner with engineering from concept through launch to align sourcing strategy with technical roadmaps, design freeze milestones, and prototype-to-production transitions. Structure commercial agreements that protect program timing without ceding cost leverage. Build first-principles should-cost models with cross-functional teams to drive a ground-up, physics-based part and system cost perspective. Use these models to set negotiation positions, evaluate quote submissions, and challenge supplier pricing line by line. Lead make-vs-buy analysis to ensure we have a best-in-class supply chain that delivers optimal value. Develop the supply base for resilience. Identify and qualify Tier 1 and Tier 2 partners across geographies; build dual-source and regional capacity strategies that address raw material scarcity, geopolitical risk, and an evolving global trade and tariff environment. Drive automation across the supply chain to deliver best-in-class supply chain efficiency. Partner with suppliers to identify opportunities for process automation and robotics. Shape the tools and processes the ADVEV supply chain runs on, including should-cost methodology, supplier and agreement management systems, and AI-enabled analytics that scale how Ford evaluates suppliers, parts, and agreements. You'll have... Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Business, Supply Chain, Operations Management or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. 5+ years of experience in supply chain management or commodity management. Experience bringing creative negotiation skills and out-of-the-box strategy. Strong relationship management skills with internal and external stakeholders. Even better, you may have... Master’s degree in Engineering, Business, Supply Chain, or related field, or MBA. Hands-on experience building and launching highly effective supply chains. Strong written and verbal communication skills. An eagerness to work cross-functionally in a dynamic environment where you are part of a high performing team. A systems approach to design and development with the desire and curiosity to strive for exceptional delivery execution and continuous improvement. Eagerness to expand into new commodity areas as the ADVEV portfolio grows. As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? description: Hunter Douglas is the world’s leading manufacturer of window coverings and a major manufacturer of architectural products. We are a brand that you know and trust. With more than 100 years of innovation, we’ve defined our industry with proprietary products that deliver revolutionary style and functionality and can be found in millions of homes and commercial buildings globally. We are searching for candidates that are driven, intelligent, creative, and entrepreneurial. By offering challenging and accelerated opportunities for growth, powered by a shared hunger for success, we create a space for your career to thrive. In return for your expertise, we are committed to providing competitive and robust total compensation and benefit packages to ensure you feel valued. Our dream is to become the fastest growing, most loved, window covering company in the world. What’s yours? Position Overview The Senior Sourcing Manager, Technology is a strategic procurement leader responsible for managing Hunter Douglas' global technology spend, including software, SaaS, cloud services, IT infrastructure, telecom, cybersecurity, and consulting services. This role partners closely with global IT leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to develop and execute sourcing strategies, negotiate enterprise agreements, optimize supplier performance, and deliver measurable cost savings. Directly impacting procurement MBOs, the position drives value creation, risk mitigation, supplier innovation, and operational efficiency across a global technology portfolio. What you'll do Develop and execute global category strategies and multi-year sourcing plans for technology spend categories in partnership with IT leadership. Lead end-to-end strategic sourcing activities, including spend analysis, market research, RFx management, supplier selection, negotiations, contracting, and implementation. Negotiate and manage enterprise agreements across software, SaaS, cloud, telecom, hardware, cybersecurity, and IT services categories. Deliver annual cost savings and total cost of ownership improvements through effective sourcing and supplier management initiatives. Collaborate with IT, Finance, Legal, and Information Security teams to ensure favorable commercial terms, risk management, and compliance. Establish and lead supplier relationship management programs, including business reviews, scorecards, performance monitoring, and risk assessments. Drive license optimization, demand management, supplier consolidation, and continuous improvement initiatives across global regions. Provide market intelligence, pricing benchmarks, vendor insights, and procurement support for major technology transformation projects. Who you are Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, Information Technology, Finance, or a related field required. Minimum of 8 years of procurement or strategic sourcing experience, including at least 5 years focused on technology categories. Demonstrated experience negotiating enterprise software, SaaS, cloud, telecom, and IT services agreements. Strong knowledge of technology licensing models, subscription pricing, cloud consumption, and contract management. Proven ability to develop and execute category strategies that deliver measurable business results and cost savings. Strong analytical and financial acumen, including total cost of ownership analysis, business case development, and supplier evaluations. Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills with the ability to work effectively across global and matrixed organizations. Excellent verbal, written, negotiation, and presentation skills. Proficiency with SAP or similar ERP systems, source-to-pay platforms, and advanced Excel reporting and analytics. CPSM, CIPS, MBA, or other relevant procurement certifications preferred; willingness to travel internationally up to 20%. What's in it for you Annual base salary range: $122k - $145k Bonus target range: 25-35% Generous benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life, disability A company culture that prioritizes internal development and professional growth Enjoy our Flexible Time Off (FTO) program designed to support work–life balance (excludes new hires in Illinois). 401(k) plan with a degree of employer matching Paid parental leave Wellness programs and product discounts Please note, all offers presented to candidates are carefully crafted to ensure market competitiveness, equity, and reflect the individual candidate’s education, experience, skills and potential. Hunter Douglas is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with applicable employment laws. EOE/M/F/Vet/Disabled are encouraged to apply. By submitting your application below, you are providing your prior consent to receive SMS messages to notify you of any updates to your application status and to engage in discussion throughout your application process. You can cancel the SMS service at any time. Just text “STOP” to any of our texts to unsubscribe. Message & data rates may apply. Message frequency may vary. If you have any questions regarding privacy, please read our privacy policy, https://www.hunterdouglas.com/privacy-policy or terms of use https://www.hunterdouglas.com/terms-of-use

description: Job Summary General Atomics (GA), and its affiliated companies, is one of the world’s leading resources for high-technology systems development ranging from the nuclear fuel cycle to remotely piloted aircraft, airborne sensors, and advanced electric, electronic, wireless and laser technologies. We have an exciting opportunity for a Senior Purchasing Manager! This position is responsible for managing the process of procuring material, parts, components, services, and equipment. Manages the activities of buyers and subcontract administrators to accomplish business objectives. Reviews and approves sizeable and complex purchase orders and subcontracts. Manages the development and interpretation of policies and procedures for the operation of the procurement department's activities and manages cost, schedule, and performance of subcontracts. Manages the coordination of purchasing activities with engineering and manufacturing departments. Typically accomplishes objectives through subordinate management and/or professional staff. May be responsible for decisions that have an extended and significant impact on outcomes across the company. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Review and approve complex, high dollar purchase orders and agreements. Negotiate and award purchase orders and subcontracts on behalf of the corporation. Establish and monitor compliance with purchasing policies and procedures in accordance with all acquisition, export and other applicable regulations, company policies and contractual requirements. Assign tasks, review work, and provide direction to staff while ensuring purchasing processes are met within established timelines. Manage proposal efforts by obtaining subcontractor and supplier quotes and proposals which may include subcontractor costs and pricing data. Analyze and negotiate subcontractor and supplier pricing when appropriate. Provide subcontractor and supplier pricing inputs to proposals/pricing departments. Manage production schedules by assisting in planning activities and monitoring buys. Manage the facilitation of pre-award surveys and supplier evaluations. Oversee various internal and external audits, including government and customer audits. Act as primary contact for purchasing activities and issues. May represent the company with customers, potential customers and suppliers. Keep abreast of best practices in supply chain and materials management. Manage the planning, attraction, selection, retention, and development of human resources to ensure the availability of the required management and professional talent. Maintain the strict confidentiality of sensitive information. Responsible for ensuring all laws, regulations and other applicable obligations are observed wherever and whenever business is conducted on behalf of the company. Responsible for ensuring work is accomplished in a safe manner in accordance with established operating procedures and practices. Additional Functions Other duties as assigned or required. We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals with diverse backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply. Job Qualifications Typically requires a Bachelor's degree in business administration or a related discipline and thirteen or more years of progressive experience interpreting, awarding and administering complex contractual agreements. May substitute equivalent experience in lieu of education. Must have demonstrated experience in the concepts, principles, and standard practices of supply chain management and purchasing and an extensive knowledge of contract construction, Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), FAR supplements, and the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC). Must be capable of coordinating inter-organizational activities and recommending creative solutions to complex issues. The ability to document, investigate, advise, interpret and explain complex issues or technical information to internal staff at all levels throughout the organization as well as external customers and suppliers is also required. Must have experience negotiating highly complex purchases and subcontracts and conducting briefings while having a detailed and comprehensive understanding of materials requirements planning. Able to work extended hours and travel as required. Job Type: Full-Time Salary Salary range: 130,500 - 228,375

description: Job Description Who We Are Creative Artists Agency (CAA) is the leading entertainment and sports agency, with global expertise in filmed and live entertainment, digital media, publishing, sponsorship sales and endorsements, media finance, consumer investing, fashion, trademark licensing, and philanthropy. Distinguished by its culture of collaboration and exceptional client service, CAA’s diverse workforce identifies, innovates, and amplifies opportunities for the people and organizations that shape culture and inspire the world. The trailblazer of the agency business, CAA was the first to build a sports business, create an investment bank, launch a venture fund, found technology start-up companies, establish a philanthropic arm, build a business in China, and form a brand marketing services division, among other innovations. Named Most Valuable Sports Agency by Forbes for eight consecutive years, CAA represents more than 2,000 of the world’s top athletes in football, baseball, basketball, hockey, soccer, in addition to coaches, on-air broadcasters, and sports personalities and works in the areas of broadcast rights, corporate marketing initiatives, social impact, and sports properties for sales and sponsorship opportunities. Founded in 1975, CAA is headquartered in Los Angeles, and has offices in New York, Nashville, Memphis, Chicago, Miami, London, Munich, Geneva, Stockholm, Shanghai, and Beijing, among other locations globally. The Role The Senior Manager, Procurement serves as a strategic business partner responsible for leading sourcing initiatives, supplier negotiations, contract lifecycle management, and procurement transformation activities across the organization. This role partners closely with business leaders and cross-functional teams to develop sourcing strategies, mitigate risk, optimize spend, and deliver measurable value. The Senior Manager will lead complex procurement initiatives from initial assessment and sourcing strategy through negotiation, contracting, implementation, and ongoing supplier management. The ideal candidate brings strong strategic sourcing expertise, financial and business acumen, exceptional negotiation skills, and the ability to influence stakeholders across the organization. Key Responsibilities Strategic Sourcing & Procurement Lead strategic sourcing initiatives across assigned categories, from initial business requirements and market assessment through supplier selection, negotiation, and contract execution. Develop sourcing strategies aligned with business priorities, operational requirements, and financial objectives. Partner with senior leaders and functional stakeholders to identify procurement opportunities, cost efficiencies, and areas for improved supplier performance. Provide procurement expertise and guidance throughout the contract lifecycle. Support procurement activities associated with acquisitions, integrations, and other enterprise transformation initiatives as needed. Negotiation & Contract Management Lead complex supplier negotiations focused on commercial terms, pricing, service levels, risk, and overall value. Partner with Legal, Finance, and business stakeholders to negotiate and execute agreements that appropriately balance business needs, cost, and risk. Identify opportunities to consolidate spend, improve commercial terms, and strengthen contractual protections. Manage contract renewals and key supplier milestones to ensure proactive decision-making and minimize business disruption. Supplier Management & Risk Develop and maintain effective supplier governance and performance management practices. Evaluate supplier performance, contractual compliance, financial risk, and business continuity considerations. Partner with internal stakeholders to address supplier performance issues and develop appropriate corrective action plans. Build strategic supplier relationships that support innovation, operational performance, and long-term value. Business Partnership & Transformation Serve as a trusted procurement advisor to business leaders across the organization. Partner cross-functionally with Legal, Finance, Technology, Operations, and other business functions to support enterprise priorities. Support integration of procurement processes, technologies, contracts, and supplier relationships across new or evolving business areas. Drive continuous improvement initiatives that increase procurement efficiency, scalability, and organizational effectiveness. Support adoption of procurement policies, processes, tools, and standards across the organization. Financial & Performance Management Develop and track savings, cost avoidance, value creation, and other procurement performance metrics. Utilize spend analytics, market intelligence, and financial analysis to inform sourcing and negotiation strategies. Develop business cases and financial models to evaluate sourcing alternatives and procurement opportunities. Provide clear reporting on sourcing initiatives, supplier performance, savings, risks, and key milestones. Innovation & Continuous Improvement Identify opportunities to leverage technology, automation, analytics, and emerging procurement capabilities. Benchmark procurement practices against industry standards and evolving market trends. Contribute to procurement transformation initiatives and the continued development of procurement capabilities across the organization. Mentor and develop team members and support a collaborative, high-performing procurement culture. Requirements Minimum of 8 years of procurement, strategic sourcing, supplier management, or related experience. Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Finance, or a related field required; Master's degree preferred. Professional certifications such as Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM) or Project Management Professional (PMP) preferred. Demonstrated experience leading complex sourcing initiatives and supplier negotiations. Strong knowledge of strategic sourcing, contract lifecycle management, supplier governance, risk management, and procurement best practices. Experience partnering with senior executives and cross-functional teams, including Legal, Finance, Technology, and Operations. Experience with enterprise procurement platforms and analytics tools; SAP experience preferred. Strong financial acumen with the ability to analyze spend, evaluate commercial models, and quantify procurement value. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple complex initiatives in a fast-paced, evolving environment. Exceptional negotiation, communication, leadership, and stakeholder management skills. Media & Entertainment industry experience strongly preferred. Key Competencies Strategic Thinking Business & Financial Acumen Negotiation & Influence Executive Presence Stakeholder Management Cross-Functional Collaboration Change Leadership Analytical & Data-Driven Decision Making Results Orientation Compensation The annual base salary range for this position is as follows: Los Angeles, CA - $140,000 - $180,000 New York, NY - $140,000- $180,000 This position is also eligible for benefits and a discretionary bonus. Ultimately, the salary may vary based upon factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, time in the role, business sector, and geographic location, among other criteria. description: At Rowan Digital Infrastructure, we are transforming data center delivery for speed and scale. Our mission is to deliver best-in-class data center solutions to hyperscale customers who share our commitment to sustainability, and to do so with an unwavering focus on efficiency, quality, and flexibility. Our data center solutions are tailored to our customers’ needs and delivered by our exceptional end-to-end team. Rowan is assembling a strategic portfolio of data center sites in Tier 1 markets across the United States at various stages of development, and we’re looking for incredible and passionate people to help us advance our company and our commitment to building a more sustainable future. Rowan is backed by Quinbrook, a leading investor in the energy transition, and Blackstone, the world’s largest alternative asset manager. Ready to join us in transforming the future of data centers and sustainability? Apply now to explore exciting career opportunities at Rowan Digital Infrastructure and be a part of our mission to revolutionize data center delivery. Role Summary Rowan Digital Infrastructure is seeking a Procurement Manager to support and streamline Power Systems equipment procurement for data center campus builds and help define a strategy to modularize solutions. This role serves as a key connector between the Procurement team and Rowan’s Engineering, Construction, and project management teams to ensure seamless delivery. You'll apply your skills in coordination, budgeting, and stakeholder alignment to manage procurement activities from planning through execution. This includes handling Requests for Proposals (RFPs), vendor relationships, contract reviews, payment terms, and delivery coordination. You will help bridge teams, driving efficiency in a fast-paced environment. Travel : Up to 25% to project locations and manufacturing facilities for expediting, site visits, RFP requirements, and initial delivery management. Location : Denver, CO (3 day hybrid in-office role) Compensation : $140k - 160k (Offers Bonus) Essential Responsibilities Manage the full procurement cycle for construction equipment, from needs identification to order finalization and timely delivery Build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers, manufacturers, and rental companies Negotiate contracts, terms, and pricing to secure optimal outcomes for Rowan Oversee the equipment procurement budget supplied by commercial and project management teams, ensuring purchases align with financial goals and arrive on schedule Track and analyze procurement costs, identifying opportunities for savings while maintaining quality Research and evaluate new suppliers for reliability, cost-effectiveness, and equipment quality Monitor vendor performance to ensure compliance with service levels and timelines Ensure all procurement activities adhere to legal, safety, and environmental standards Maintain detailed records of purchases, warranties, contracts, and repairs for audits Collaborate with project managers and construction teams to align on needs and deliver equipment on schedule Collaborate with Sr Director of Procurement in vendor selection Maintain detailed records for vendor relationships, onboarding qualified vendors and streamlining the process required for MSA and PO delivery Education, Skills, And Experience Bachelor’s degree in Business, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience) 8+ years of procurement, purchasing, supply chain, or construction procurement experience Proven procurement experience in construction for a mid-to-large-scale general contractor or similar organization Background in data center development or large-scale infrastructure projects Experience managing sizable projects or a portfolio of multiple initiatives Proficiency in Procore (or Bluebeam) and other construction management software Working knowledge of green building practices Excellent communication and collaboration skills Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving abilities Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment Preferred Experience Prior project management experience, with skills transferable to procurement (e.g., timeline oversight, risk mitigation) Familiarity with hyperscale data center procurement processes description: At Saputo, we bring good to the table by making high-quality products, investing in our people, and supporting communities around the world . As a top 10 global dairy processor, we value contributions that matter and strive to foster an inclusive, growth-driven work environment. Ready to bring your best? The Senior Procurement Manager, Warehouse & Operational Services is responsible for developing and executing sourcing strategies that support warehouse, distribution, supply chain, manufacturing, and operational equipment needs across Saputo USA, with opportunities to leverage North America scale where beneficial. This role leads supplier negotiations, supports operational requirements, and drives measurable value through lease optimization, maintenance cost control, supplier governance, asset utilization, lifecycle planning, standardization, capital planning, and total cost of ownership improvement across the network. This position partners closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Engineering, Safety, Finance, Legal, Procurement, and site leadership to translate business needs into sourcing strategies, supplier solutions, scopes of work, commercial requirements, contracts, and governance models that support day-to-day operational performance and long-term business priorities. The role requires senior-level ownership, influence, and business judgment, including cross-functional leadership, supplier accountability, program optimization, and recommendations to divisional leadership. How You Will Make Contributions That Matter Lead sourcing, lifecycle management, and governance of 3,500+ leased assets across 29 locations, including material handling equipment, fleet assets, maintenance services, and operational support solutions. Drive asset optimization through supplier strategies, standardization, replacement planning, redeployment, and total cost of ownership improvements. Analyze asset performance, utilization, and spend to identify cost savings, improve reliability, and support data-driven decision making. Partner with Operations, Supply Chain, and site leadership to align asset, warehouse, and equipment strategies with business objectives. Develop business cases, KPIs, reporting, and recommendations that support fleet optimization, capital planning, and enterprise value creation. Lead supplier relationships, governance, performance management, risk mitigation, and continuous improvement initiatives across warehouse, fleet, leasing, equipment, and operational service categories. Develop and execute category and sourcing strategies, including supplier selection, negotiations, contracting, and implementation activities. Partner with internal stakeholders to align supplier and sourcing strategies with operational requirements and enterprise priorities. Partner with Finance and Operations to support budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, spend management, and contract compliance. Develop financial analyses and investment recommendations while monitoring performance against savings, cost, and value creation targets. Identify and implement technology, analytics, and supplier innovation opportunities that improve operational performance, visibility, and asset utilization. Lead cross-functional initiatives and provide guidance to project teams to support operational improvement and network optimization. You are best suited for the role if you… Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Finance, Operations, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 10+ years of experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, supply chain, operations, logistics, warehousing, asset management, fleet management, category management, or a related function. Experience leading enterprise-wide initiatives involving suppliers, operations, financial stakeholders, and cross-functional project teams. Direct experience supporting warehouse, logistics, distribution, manufacturing, fleet, or operational service environments. Experience leading RFx events, supplier negotiations, contract development, supplier governance, and cross-functional sourcing projects. Experience developing business cases, cost models, total cost of ownership analysis, financial recommendations, or capital planning support. Strong analytical, financial, communication, project management, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills. Ability to influence senior stakeholders, make sound recommendations, lead through ambiguity, and manage competing priorities independently. We support and care for our employees by providing them with… Development opportunities that enhance you career fulfillment. Meaningful compensation & benefits that help you care for your family. Opportunities to contribute to your community and enhance the lives of others through Saputo products. Salary range: $107,305 - $140,895 Salary offers will vary commensurate with experience, education, skills and training. Hybrid office: Dallas - 3 days in office, 2 days remote Milwaukee - 4 days in office, 1 day remote In the USA, Saputo ranks among the top three cheese producers and is one of the top producers of extended shelf-life and cultured dairy products, with a portfolio of well-loved brands such as Stella, Frigo Cheese, Montchevre, Stella, and Treasure Cave. We also boast a strong foodservice presence, partnering with reputable chain restaurants and broadline distributors. description: NorthMark Strategies is a leading investment firm, combining capital, innovation, and engineering to drive long-term value. From operating complex businesses to backing breakthrough technologies, our mission is to build enduring businesses. Our team combines intelligent risk-taking, operational excellence, exceptional talent, and world-class computing capacity to create shareholder value. Our company offers a dynamic environment where individuals have the freedom to lead companies toward bold achievements by embracing innovation, leveraging technology, and fostering differentiated business strategies. Our values are Integrity, Ability, and Energy, and the company aims to hire individuals who possess those qualities. At NorthMark Strategies, we believe the future isn’t something to hope for, it’s something to build. We don’t just invest, we create. Bringing together strategic insight and technical horsepower to deliver outcomes that endure. The Position We are seeking a Procurement Associate for Mechanical Equipment who will be responsible for buying the mechanical, electrical, and plumbing equipment for our OFCI data center construction program. The Procurement Associate – Mechanical Equipment executes the purchasing that keeps that model running: issuing and administering purchase orders for major mechanical equipment, expediting long-lead deliveries, and coordinating daily with our third-party EPC partner so equipment arrives on site in line with the construction schedule. This is a hands-on execution role working under Grey Space category leads. It suits a buyer with 4–6 years of direct procurement experience who knows mechanical equipment — chillers, cooling towers, air handling, pumps — and can run a disciplined PO book in a fast-moving construction environment. Responsibilities Execute and administer purchase orders for owner-furnished mechanical equipment, including chillers, cooling towers, CRAH/fan wall units, pumps, piping and valve packages, VFDs, and related systems. Support category leads through sourcing events: prepare RFQ documentation, build bid tabulations, and manage supplier communications through award. Expedite long-lead equipment; track production milestones, ship dates, and delivery status against construction schedule milestones, and escalate slippage risk early. Coordinate OFCI delivery logistics with the third-party EPC and site teams, covering freight arrangements, delivery sequencing, offloading and laydown requirements, and receiving documentation. Manage the full PO lifecycle in the ERP: change orders, milestone payment tracking, invoice discrepancy resolution, and closeout. Track vendor submittals, drawing approvals, and factory witness test / factory acceptance test (FAT) schedules; keep documentation moving between vendors, engineering, and the EPC. Support over/short/damage (OS&D) and warranty claims with vendors and freight carriers through resolution. Maintain supplier records, pricing history, and lead-time intelligence for the mechanical category; contribute to supplier scorecards and status reporting. Requirements 4–6 years of direct procurement experience with hands-on buying responsibility (PO execution and administration) for capital equipment, engineered systems, or construction materials. Demonstrated buying experience in the mechanical discipline: chillers, cooling towers, air handling units, pumps, HVAC packages, or comparable engineered mechanical equipment. Working knowledge of the full procure-to-pay cycle and ERP-based purchasing. Experience managing long-lead equipment, including expediting and delivery risk management. Working command of commercial terms: Incoterms, freight terms, payment milestones, and warranties. Strong Excel and tracking discipline; able to maintain accurate delivery and status data across a large book of open POs. Bachelor's degree in supply chain management, engineering, construction management, or business — or equivalent experience. Preferred Qualifications Experience in data center, mission-critical, semiconductor, or other heavy industrial construction environments. Familiarity with OFCI/CFCI delivery models and working alongside EPC or GC partners. Exposure to factory witness testing and factory acceptance test coordination. Ability to read mechanical equipment schedules, specifications, and submittals. Microsoft Dynamics 365 or comparable ERP experience. APICS/ASCM (CPIM, CSCP) or ISM (CPSM) certification. description: By living according to a common set of values, we create a culture that unifies, embraces the uniqueness we all bring to the company, and positions Integer for long-term success. At Integer, our values are embedded in everything we do. Customer We focus on our customers’ success Innovation We create better solutions Collaboration We create success together Inclusion We always interact with others respectfully Candor We are open and honest with one another Integrity We do the right things and do things right What You’ll Do In This Role In this role, you will perform standard work assignments while developing proficiency. You typically need a college degree or equivalent work experience, providing exposure to fundamental theories and concepts. Your role requires conceptual knowledge within Purchasing and involves applying general business knowledge. You will receive guidance and direction from others and be accountable for technical contributions to your team. You will seek to identify innovative approaches to solve standard problems, analyze information, and utilize standard practices to make informed judgments. Your work will impact your own tasks and contribute to the achievement of team goals and objectives. Additionally, you will exchange information, ask questions, and check for understanding to ensure effective communication. You will adhere to Integer’s Values and all safety, environmental, security, and quality requirements including, but not limited to: Quality Management Systems (QMS), Safety, Environmental and Security Management Systems, U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations, company policies and operating procedures, and other regulatory requirements. You will analyze basic requirements to place, cancel, and/or reschedule purchase orders with approved suppliers. You will evaluate changes in demand, design, and supplier-driven factors to ensure appropriate supply to production. You will request and evaluate quotes from suppliers that meet cost, delivery, quality targets, and specifications. You will analyze, report, and forecast purchase price variance. Participate in the annual budget process for purchases and standard costing. Maintain material flow in the supply chain, assuring that priorities are clearly identified to import, receive, inspect, and release raw material. You will manage and forecast inventory levels to optimize raw material availability and working capital strategies. You collaborate with team members to understand and evaluate supplier capabilities and performance. Develop and support initiatives for cost reduction and savings opportunities. You will collaborate with Quality for the resolution and closure of corrective actions (CAPA), nonconforming material (NCMR), and return to vendor (RTV). You will initiate and coordinate the loading of new suppliers in the ERP system, as well as update changes to existing suppliers. You will collaborate with the Finance department to resolve issues of accounting, payment terms, AP holds, and resolution of payment to suppliers. You may perform other duties as needed and as directed by your leadership How you will be measured ? The specific measures listed below may be subject to change and are not intended to be an all-inclusive list: Safety is our highest priority; you will be an active supporter of the Integer Environmental, Health & Safety programs. Supply Chain – Achievement of site Supply Chain KPI’s; PO without Promise Date, PO Status Approval, Past due PO’s, AP Hold You will have defined Goals and Objectives specifying key projects and expected milestones to achieve. Innovation and ideation are critical aspects of your role, and you will be expected to generate continuous improvement suggestions and support the implementation of them. What sets you apart ? A Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, or a related field is desired; however, if you do not meet the education requirement, you may be considered with two years of relevant experience in purchasing. You will have strong PC literacy skills (eg Excel, Word, PowerPoint, ERP) While you will have regular support and guidance from more experienced buyers, supervisors or managers, you will demonstrate the ability to work independently as well as collaboratively with other associates and cross-functional teams. You demonstrate a solid technical aptitude with the ability to be an effective contributor to a team or produce results of a technical nature as an individual. You demonstrate competencies in both written and oral communications. You maintain a calm demeanor that transcends the high energy, constantly changing production environment. You possess a positive, can-do attitude with an underlying belief that failure is not an option. Our total rewards program is designed to attract, retain, and motivate associates to contribute to Integer’s success. Our compensation program includes base salary and a cash-based incentive program supporting our pay-for-performance philosophy. We provide a comprehensive benefits package with immediate eligibility including medical, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, and adoption benefits. Parental leave is available after one year. Optional employee-paid programs include supplemental life insurance, critical illness, hospital indemnity and accident insurance. Employees are immediately eligible to participate in the 401(k) plan with company matching contributions. We provide 80 hours (10 days) of company designated holidays per year plus an annual allotment of paid time off. U.S. Applicants: Equal Opportunity Employer. In addition, veterans and individuals with disabilities are encouraged to apply.

description: Job Description The Procurement Coordinator supports the day-to-day purchasing and vendor management functions across our construction projects. description: Job Description: The Procurement Coordinator is responsible for the procurement of quality spares and supplies for the Company and shall be knowledgeable of Company suppliers and shipping methods. The Procurement Coordinator will have full ownership of their generated purchase orders from initiation to closure and shall aggressively ensure need dates are maintained and estimated arrival dates are continually updated. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Ethically utilizing Company funds when purchasing goods and scheduling shipments; Making the most economically sound decision to purchase, rent, or exchange parts to properly fill needs; Sourcing vendors for New Parts Creations, taking into account cost, part condition and warranty, and time constraints; Sourcing alternative vendors when the initial vendor cannot meet the required need date; Coordinating primary components and the related parts resources from a single vendor whenever possible or practical; Coordinating the delivery of parts purchased on non-PBH exchanges directly to the needed base and facilitating the return of the core part by the remote employee to the vendor; Adjusting PO need dates or ship-to locations when directed to do so by the Planning group; Communicating with the Quality Control Department about the paperwork required for life limited and overhaul parts; and, Performing other duties as assigned by the Procurement Supervisor. Support procurement activities across global operations and diverse project portfolios, coordinating sourcing, documentation, and vendor engagement for both ongoing and ad‑hoc international assignments. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Solid understanding of how procurement principles, planning, transportation cost structures, and negotiations techniques impact purchasing required; Excellent verbal and written communication skills required, as well as proficiency in MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) required; Ability to adapt to changing priorities in a high-paced environment required; Ability to work weekend AOG support on a rotational basis with other members of the Purchasing and Planning Team required; One to Five years procurement/sub-contracts execution experience including materials management and supply chain environment preferred; Working knowledge of ERP and purchasing software preferred; Solid understanding of general accounting principles and the financial impact of inventory transactions preferred; Familiarity with supply chain management, inventory control, Just-in-time (JIT) preferred; Proficiency in RAMCO and Oracle preferred. description: Description Founded in 1986, Sterling Commercial Roofing, a Tecta America company, is the trusted choice for businesses across Northern Illinois, Eastern Iowa, and Southern Wisconsin. As the largest commercial roofing business in Illinois, we put people first—ensuring employee safety and delivering exceptional service and quality to our customers. We are looking for an Inventory & Purchasing Coordinator to join our team. In this role, you will manage inventory, place material orders, work with vendors, and support our Project Managers and Accounting team. Your work will help ensure materials are ordered accurately, delivered on time, and properly tracked. This position is ideal for someone who is organized, detail-oriented, and enjoys working with inventory, purchasing, and data. Job Functions Inventory Management Maintain accurate inventory records. Track materials coming in and going out of inventory. Research and correct inventory discrepancies. Perform inventory counts and cycle counts. Work with warehouse staff to verify inventory levels. Monitor stock levels and help prevent shortages or excess inventory. Purchasing & Vendor Support Create and enter purchase orders. Track orders and delivery dates. Follow up with vendors on order status and shipments. Help resolve delivery issues and pricing discrepancies. Maintain part numbers, product information, and cost data. Support Project Managers with updates on open orders. Documentation & Reporting Maintain organized purchasing and inventory records. Scan and file project documentation. Track vendor returns, credits, and refunds. Prepare inventory and purchasing reports. Use Excel and business systems to analyze inventory data. Year-End Inventory Support Assist with annual inventory counts. Help track obsolete or unused materials. Support inventory audits and provide documentation when needed. Knowledge Skills & Experience Experience in inventory control, purchasing, supply chain, or a related role. Strong attention to detail and accuracy. Good organizational and problem-solving skills. Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities. Strong communication skills. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel. Experience working with inventory or purchasing software. Experience with Navision a plus. Experience in construction, manufacturing, distribution, or a similar industry. Understanding of inventory control and purchasing processes. Sterling Commercial Roofing, aTecta America company, offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company match, paid time off, paid holidays, etc.

description: TITLE: Maintenance Procurement Coordinator REPORTS TO: Maintenance Parts and Purchasing Lead FLSA STATUS: Non-Exempt SHIFT: 8:00am to 5:00pm This position is open to any qualified INDIVIDUAL regardless of sex, race, age, color, religion, national origin or disability. Position Purpose The Purchasing Agent supports maintenance, engineering, production, and MRO operations by sourcing materials and services, managing purchase orders from request through receipt, resolving discrepancies, and maintaining accurate purchasing records. The role uses MVP, Jazz, Coupa, P4K, Excel, Power BI, and eBusiness platforms to support timely and cost-effective purchasing decisions. Essential Functions/Major Responsibilities Create, review, and maintain purchase requisitions and purchase orders in MVP, Jazz, Coupa, and P4K in accordance with approval requirements and company procedures. Purchase stock and non-stock maintenance parts, production supplies, repair services, chemicals, lubricants, adhesives, and other assigned materials. Obtain and evaluate vendor quotations based on price, quality, availability, lead time, freight, payment terms, and service; identify alternate suppliers and hard-to-find items when needed. Place orders, document confirmations, track promised delivery dates, and follow up on late, delayed, backordered, or unshipped items. Maintain accurate vendor, item, equipment, order, receipt, delivery, quote, and supporting documentation in applicable systems and files. Reconcile purchase orders, receipts, packing slips, invoices, and system records; investigate and resolve quantity, price, tax, freight, duplicate receipt, and payment discrepancies. Manage capital and non-capital purchasing activity, including required project, work order, asset, equipment, and capital authorization references. Coordinate returns, repairs, exchanges, warranties, credits, reclaimed parts, and freight claims through final resolution. Communicate order status, shortages, substitutions, shipment details, and purchasing issues to vendors, requestors, receiving, accounting, and management. Generate and monitor open purchase order, past-due, receipt, exception, spend, vendor performance, and reconciliation reports. Use Excel and Power BI to clean, compare, analyze, and present purchasing, inventory, delivery, receipt, and supplier performance data. Support standard operating procedures and provide backup assistance for procurement, parts, tool crib, and receiving functions as assigned. Maintain a safe, clean, organized, and professional work environment; comply with company policies and perform other duties as assigned. , Preferred Systems Experience Hands-on experience with MVP, Jazz, Coupa, and P4K for purchasing, approvals, order management, receiving, or reconciliation. Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including formulas, lookups, pivot tables, sorting, filtering, data cleanup, comparisons, and report preparation. Experience with Microsoft Power BI, including importing data and building reports, dashboards, and supplier performance visuals. Heavy eBusiness experience with vendor portals, electronic ordering, order confirmations, shipping notices, invoicing, document retrieval, and online account management. Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Word, Teams, and related business applications. Education/Experience/Skills Required High school diploma or GED required; associate degree in business, supply chain, procurement, accounting, or a related field preferred. Three or more years of purchasing, procurement, MRO, maintenance, inventory, receiving, accounts payable, or related experience preferred. Experience working with vendors and internal business partners in a fast-paced operational or manufacturing environment. Equivalent combinations of education, training, and relevant experience may be considered. Strong purchasing judgment, attention to detail, organization, follow-through, and problem-solving skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities, urgent orders, deadlines, interruptions, and changing operational needs. Ability to identify root causes and coordinate practical resolutions across departments and suppliers. Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work independently within a collaborative team. Ability to handle pricing, supplier, financial, and company information with appropriate confidentiality. An Equal Opportunity Employer including Disabled/Veterans

description: Position Summary The Purchasing Coordinator is responsible for supporting purchasing activities and ensuring ingredients and products are ordered from approved suppliers to meet production needs. This role works closely with internal teams, vendors, and suppliers to support inventory flow, resolve issues, and contribute to cost-effective purchasing practices. Key Responsibilities Purchase ingredients, raw materials, and products from approved suppliers to support scheduled production. Monitor production schedules and ensure materials arrive on time to prevent shortages, delays, or overstock. Maintain accurate purchase orders, including quantities, pricing, delivery dates, and supplier information. Monitor raw material inventory levels using ERP/MRP systems and purchasing tools. Maintain purchasing attributes such as safety stock, lead times, reorder points, and purchasing recommendations. Identify opportunities for adjustments and communicate those with the supervisor. Daily review for purchasing and inventory reports, including but not limited to the General Item Status Report, Reorder Report, Negative Item Report, and MRP outputs. Any discrepancies or issues should be independently researched and assessed prior to escalating to additional stakeholders. Communicate professionally with internal departments, vendors, suppliers, and other stakeholders regarding purchasing needs, order status, shortages, supply constraints, and issue resolution. Collaborate with Customer Service, Inventory, Receiving, Strategic Procurement, Logistics, Planning, and other teams to support purchasing, inventory flow, and production requirements. Support company profitability through cost-effective purchasing, supplier collaboration, cost reduction, cost avoidance, and value-added procurement practices. Maintain a strong understanding of manufacturing capabilities, business processes, supply chain operations, and the raw materials used in production. Complete other duties and projects as assigned by management. Qualifications High school diploma or equivalent required. Associate degree or bachelor’s degree preferred. Experience in food, ingredient, manufacturing, or distribution purchasing preferred. Experience using ERP/MRP systems or purchasing tools preferred. Strong communication, analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with internal teams, suppliers, vendors, and stakeholders. Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Quality and Food Safety Requirements Follow all Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs). Follow all Safe Quality Food (SQF) guidelines. Maintain awareness of Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) and its importance. Ensure all products and ingredients are purchased only from approved suppliers. Immediately report food safety problems or concerns to a person with authority to initiate action, as indicated on the organizational chart. Safety Requirements Follow applicable OSHA regulations related to job tasks. Remain aware of surroundings, including forklift traffic and trip hazards such as pallets or cords when entering production areas. Wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) when entering production areas. Participate in monthly safety engagement activities. Excited about this role but don’t think you meet every requirement listed? We encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this role or another one of our openings. ADM requires the successful completion of a background check. REF:113836BR

Position Overview The Purchasing Coordinator I role is a key operational role within Spirit’s Purchasing department. This position is responsible for executing day-to-day procurement activities for microelectronics, semiconductors, EEE components, and engineering services. The Purchasing Coordinator I plays a crucial role in maintaining efficient purchasing processes, managing supplier relationships, and ensuring timely delivery of materials to meet Spirit’s needs. The role serves as an escalation point for complex issues and works closely with Sales to optimize the purchasing process and enhance customer satisfaction. PC1 provides customer communication on purchase orders, including supporting for order expedites, monitoring, data reporting, and supply chain updates. Communicate with suppliers regarding order details, pricing, delivery schedules, and quality requirements. Monitor, maintain, and track order status, purchasing records, supplier information and pricing within ERP system – ensuring accuracy, transparency, and on time delivery for internal stakeholders and customers. Support supplier-managed inventory programs and inventory-related initiatives, including cycle counts and reconciliations. Provide proactive order status communication to internal teams and customer-facing departments. Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, reduce response time, and improve the overall customer-support experience. Stay informed about market trends, pricing fluctuations, and industry developments affecting purchasing and customer support operations. Support logistics coordination for incoming shipments, ensuring proper receiving through Warehouse collaboration. Assist in supplier evaluations and performance reviews, incorporating customer impact and service quality considerations. Collaborate with the Purchasing Manager and department leads to develop and implement customer service strategies and process improvements. description: Reports to – Procurement Manager Organization Overview Baby2Baby is a non-profit organization that provides children in need with diapers, formula, clothing, and the basic necessities that every child deserves, serving more than one million children across all 50 states. The organization has distributed over half a billion items in the past 14 years to children in homeless shelters, domestic violence programs, foster care, hospitals and school districts as well as children who have lost everything in the wake of disaster. The organization’s success has been propelled forward by its industry-leading model that is redefining what it means to operate a non-profit with a seamless integration of impact, innovation, and influence, which earned them praise from TIME Magazine as one of 2023’s most influential companies and recognition as the #1 non-profit on Fast Company’s World’s Most Innovative Companies List. Position Overview Reporting to the Procurement Manager, the Procurement Coordinator will support the day-to-day execution of Baby2Baby's procurement function by coordinating purchasing activities, maintaining procurement systems and documentation, tracking orders and vendor information, and ensuring accurate reporting and data management. Working closely with departments across the organization, this role will help streamline procurement operations, support strategic sourcing initiatives, and contribute to the continued growth and efficiency of Baby2Baby's procurement function. The Procurement Coordinator will work Monday–Friday. The work is performed in an office setting and is currently in office or on site 3–5 days per week. The primary office location is 5830 W. Jefferson Boulevard, Los Angeles, CA 90016, with potential on-site responsibilities at Baby2Baby's warehouse located at 16333 Raymer Street, Van Nuys, CA 91406, as well as the future headquarters in Santa Monica, CA. Duties and Responsibilities Supports the day-to-day administration and execution of Baby2Baby's procurement activities, ensuring purchasing processes are organized, efficient, and accurately documented. Coordinates the full procurement lifecycle, including purchase requests, purchase orders, vendor confirmations, production schedules, shipments, deliveries, and invoice reconciliation. Owns the maintenance and accuracy of procurement databases, trackers, dashboards, and reporting tools to provide visibility into purchasing activity, vendor performance, budgets, inventory risks, and cost savings. Maintains centralized procurement records, including vendor contact information, pricing history, lead times, minimum order quantities, payment terms, contracts, and product specifications. Supports vendor management through onboarding, ongoing communications, documentation collection, and follow-up to ensure timely execution and strong working relationships. Conducts supplier and product research, prepares comparison analyses, and assists with sourcing initiatives, benchmarking, and evaluation of new products and vendors. Assists in developing and maintaining procurement reporting, dashboards, and metrics that support forecasting, leadership visibility, and operational decision-making. Coordinates closely with the Warehouse team to align purchasing timelines with receiving capacity, inventory management, and distribution schedules. Partners with internal departments to track purchasing requests, communicate order status, and ensure procurement priorities are executed effectively. Identifies opportunities to improve procurement processes through better documentation, workflow management, technology, and data organization. Supports cross-functional procurement initiatives and strategic projects as assigned. Onsite involvement at Baby2Baby events and distributions across Los Angeles, as needed. Other duties as assigned. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. 2+ years of experience in procurement, purchasing, operations, logistics, supply chain, administration, or a related field. Highly organized with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to organize, interpret, and maintain accurate data. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and build positive working relationships with vendors. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines and maintaining accuracy. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Google Workspace, particularly Excel and Google Sheets. Comfortable learning new systems and technology platforms, with an interest in leveraging tools to improve operational efficiency. Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and proactively identify and resolve issues. Strong commitment to Baby2Baby's mission and values. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting procurement, purchasing, supply chain, inventory management, or warehouse operations. Experience maintaining reports, dashboards, or operational data used to support business decisions. Experience researching suppliers, comparing products, or coordinating vendor relationships. Experience working in a nonprofit, humanitarian, or mission-driven organization. Familiarity with AI tools or technology platforms that support process improvement, reporting, or operational efficiency. Other Baby2Baby is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to fostering diversity within its staff. We have made diverse thinking a priority in order to keep our organization in touch with the needs of families in our program and to help hold us accountable to those we serve. Our organization strives for diversity, from the children we serve to our board and staff, not only in race, age, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, and religion but also in cultural background and life experiences.
