description: Are you interested in being part of an innovative team that supports Westinghouse’s mission to provide clean energy solutions? At Westinghouse, we recognize that our employees are our most valuable asset and we seek to identify, attract and recruit the most qualified talent while recognizing and encouraging the value of diversity in the global workplace. About The Role The Lead Procurement Engineer is a key leadership role responsible for executing procurement and delivery activities for Westinghouse new-build projects, with a primary focus on AP1000® nuclear power plants in North America. This role leads the end-to-end procurement lifecycle for auxiliary equipment, from sourcing and purchase order placement through supplier execution, delivery, and customer turnover. The successful candidate will ensure project objectives are achieved across safety, quality, cost, schedule, and contractual requirements while partnering with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Project Management, Commercial teams, suppliers, and customers. You will report to the Manager, APX WBS-7 Auxiliary Equipment and be expected to work hybrid out of Cranberry Township, PA . Relocation assistance is not provided. Approximately 20–25% travel to supplier facilities is expected. Key Responsibilities Drive localization/regionalization efforts to identify and develop suppliers in North America to support new AP1000 projects. Develop and implement the appropriate program management model, complementary to global execution models to profitably ensure Westinghouse's participation and leadership in the APX Supply Chain Portfolio. Forecast program performance, including identification of risk areas and development of mitigation strategies to ensure overall program meets safety, quality, and financial goals. Be a trusted business partner to the Delivery Stream project procurement leader for each major customer project. Lead and provide oversight to Delivery Stream teams across all Westinghouse, supplier, and customer sites. Lead decision-making, strategy development, and implementation for procurement of components and equipment. Work with APX Supply Chain partners to develop and provide strategic sourcing strategies and execution plans focused on delivery and implementation of products that exceed incremental profitable growth for Westinghouse. Oversee training and mentor new hires and existing employees working on customer projects for the first time. Serve as primary project interface for project management, status, and responsibility for delivery of components and equipment within Westinghouse scope of supply. Support development of Delivery Stream project management staffing forecast. Participate in bid opportunities/meetings. Once projects are secured, serve as the primary project interface, providing status and taking responsibility for the delivery of components and equipment within Westinghouse scope of supply. Collaborate with design engineering and quality to develop appropriate document submittal and witness and hold point (W&HP) requirements. Provide supplier strategy and procurement planning by guiding supplier Identification and down selection, technical evaluations, quality audits and request for quotation package creations. Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Engineering Discipline or higher in Engineering. 5 plus years of relevant experience in project delivery to major technical design projects. Project Management Professional (PMP) is a plus. We are committed to transparency and equity in all of our people practices. The base salary range for this position, which is dependent upon experience, qualifications and skills, is estimated to be $116,800 to $146,000 per year. Why Westinghouse? Benefits Our benefits package is tailored to meet the diverse needs of our employees, while also promoting wellness and career growth. The following are representative of what we offer: Comprehensive Medical benefits which could include medical, dental, vision, prescription coverage and Health Savings Account (HSA) with employer contributions options Wellness Programs designed to support employees in maintaining their health and well-being including Employee Assistance Program providing support for our employees and their household members 401(k) with Company Match Contributions to support employees' retirement Paid Vacations and Company Holidays Opportunities for Flexible Work Arrangements to promote work-life balance Educational Reimbursement and Comprehensive Career Programs to help employees grow in their careers Global Recognition and Service Programs to celebrate employee accomplishments and service Employee Referral Program Westinghouse Electric Company Is The Global Nuclear Energy Industry's First Choice For Safe, Clean, And Efficient Energy Solutions. We Enable Our Delivery Of This Vision By Living Our Value System Safety and Quality Integrity and Trust Customer Focus and Innovation Speed and Passion to Win Teamwork and Accountability While our Global Headquarters are located in Cranberry Township, PA, we have over 11,000 employees working at locations in 19 different countries. You can learn more by visiting http://www.westinghousenuclear.com . Westinghouse is an Equal Opportunity Employer including Veterans and Individuals with Disabilities Get connected with Westinghouse on social media: Twitter | Facebook | LinkedIn | YouTube

description: Open the Door to Your Future with Clopay Corporation & CornellCookson At Clopay Corporation, we are more than just North America’s largest residential and commercial garage door manufacturer—we are a powerhouse of innovation, safety, and design. Through our premier brands, we lead the industry in providing groundbreaking high-performance closure solutions for both the places people call home and the spaces where the world does business. Headquartered in Mason, Ohio, and operating state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities in Troy, Ohio, Mountaintop, Pennsylvania, and Goodyear, Arizona, we are a proud American-owned company and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Griffon Corporation. Our reach extends across 55+ distribution centers and thousands of retail locations in the U.S. and Canada, ensuring that we deliver the right door for every opening – from homes to businesses and beyond. By joining our team, you become part of a legacy that blends the residential elegance of Clopay, known as "America’s Favorite Garage Doors," with the industrial strength and 180-year heritage of our rolling brands, Cornell and Cookson. Together, we secure everything from family garages to the world's most iconic stadiums and skyscrapers. We have an excellent opportunity for a New Product Procurement Specialist in our Mason, Ohio location. In this position, the successful candidate will perform the following job responsibilities: Early Supplier Involvement (ESI) and Engineering Collaboration Partner with Design Engineering teams during early stage concepts to recommend supplier technologies, materials, and manufacturing methods. Facilitate Early Supplier Involvement (ESI) workshops to optimize part designs for manufacturability, quality, and cost efficiency. Challenge design specifications that risk creating unnecessary sole-source constraints or proprietary lock-ins, advocating for standard industry alternatives where appropriate. Prototyping and First-Article Sourcing Manage rapid-turn quotation, bidding, and purchase order execution for prototype tooling and sample parts. Coordinate sample submissions, tooling builds, and first-article inspection reports (FAIR) with Quality Assurance and Product Engineering. Track and expedite critical-path tooling and prototype deliveries to align with strict project milestone schedules. Target Costing and Financial Analysis Conduct target costing assessments and cost modeling for newly designed components. Perform total cost of ownership (TCO) analysis, factoring in unit costs, tooling, freight, duties, scrap, and inventory holding costs. Lead supplier price negotiations to ensure the final Bill of Materials (BOM) meets corporate gross margin targets prior to product release. Supplier Selection and Risk Mitigation Identify, evaluate, and qualify strategic suppliers capable of supporting new technology platforms and volume scale-ups. Conduct supplier risk assessments (capacity, financial stability, geographic vulnerability) and establish dual-sourcing strategies where required. Negotiate and finalize non-disclosure agreements (NDAs), master service agreements (MSAs), and initial development contracts. Production Transition and Phase-In Establish stable, production-ready supply chains prior to commercial launch gates. Coordinate seamless transfer of finalized tooling, part numbers, pricing, and master contracts to the sustaining Buyer/Planner team. Monitor initial mass-production runs to ensure ramp-up stability, resolving early supply chain bottleneck. Required Or Essential Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Industrial Engineering, or a related field. 3 – 5 years minimum experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, or supply chain, with an emphasis on new product introduction (NPI) or engineering sourcing. Ability to interpret engineering drawings, CAD files, component specifications, and complex Bills of Materials (BOMs). Hands-on experience with ERP/RP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle), PLM software, and advanced Excel modeling. Proven ability to build consensus and communicate effectively across Engineering, Operations, Finance, and external vendor partners. Demonstrated track record in cost reduction, tooling agreement negotiation, and contract structuring. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent product launch timelines under tight deadlines. Proactive mindset focused on mitigating supply chain risks early in the design cycle. Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and Power Point) is a must. Why Choose a Career with Us? We don't just manufacture doors; we engineer the "front door" of the American dream and the security of global commerce. At Clopay, we believe our strength lies in our people. From our design engineers to our manufacturing associates and delivery drivers, every member of the team plays a vital role in our success. Our Team Members Thrive Because We Prioritize Unrivaled Scale: Work for a market leader with a massive manufacturing footprint and a reputation for excellence that spans nearly two centuries. A Culture of "What’s Next": We invest heavily in automation, sustainable materials, and smart-home integration to stay ahead of the curve. Commitment to People: As a Griffon Corporation company, we provide the stability of a large organization with the tight-knit, collaborative feel of a specialized craft team. A Legacy of Expertise: Join our "Pioneer Club"—a group of over 440 employees who have been with us for 20 years or more. We offer the stability of a market leader and a place where you can truly grow a lifelong career. Commitment to Innovation: We aren’t just keeping up with industry trends; we’re setting them. Whether it’s our exclusive WINDCODE® technology or our award-winning designs, we provide the tools for you to do your best work. Community Focused: Our success is linked to the well-being of our neighbors and communities. Through our partnership with Habitat for Humanity, Clopay employees help provide homes and security to families in the communities where we live and work.

description: At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit www.bwxt.com . Follow us on LinkedIn , X , Facebook and Instagram . Welcome to BWXT We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference. Position Overview The Technical Procurement Engineer provides specialized technical expertise in support of strategic sourcing, supplier development, and the procurement of complex, highly engineered materials and services. As a key technical resource within BWXT Supply Chain, this position partners closely with Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, and Program Management to ensure all procured materials, components, and services meet technical, quality, regulatory, cost, and schedule requirements. The role primarily supports BEO and contributes to broader Tennessee Operations initiatives as business needs evolve. Location: On-site in Oak Ridge, TN Your Day-to-Day As a Technical Procurement Engineer Support strategic sourcing, negotiation, and procurement of materials and services, including raw materials, machining, fabrication, forgings, welding materials, and other technical commodities. Conduct supplier assessments such as audits, competency evaluations, qualification activities, and ongoing surveillance. Develop, review, and issue procurement specifications, technical packages, statements of work, subcontractor submittal requirements, and inspection and testing plans. Review supplier proposals, technical exceptions, manufacturing plans, inspection results, calibration records, and certifications to ensure full compliance with requirements. Serve as the primary engineering interface with suppliers for subcontracted components, ensuring fabrication processes meet all technical and quality standards. Lead and contribute to internal technical teams evaluating supplier performance and resolving issues involving discrepant or degraded materials. Collaborate with engineering, purchasing, and quality teams to identify, evaluate, and qualify new suppliers. Support the development of cost estimates and contribute to program efficiencies through process improvements. Apply independent judgment to resolve complex technical procurement challenges while meeting cost, schedule, and compliance expectations. Required Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree. At least 5 years of experience in technical procurement, materials management, or purchasing. Experience with supplier qualification, ASME NQA-1, FAR/DFAR/DEAR regulations, and DOE facility operations. Strong technical understanding of engineering principles, manufacturing processes, quality control, and failure analysis. Strong negotiation, communication, collaboration, and interpersonal skills. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple tasks, interpret complex technical requirements, and prepare detailed procurement documentation. Must be a U.S. citizen. Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Q clearance. Preferred Qualifications Engineering degree Candidates without an engineering degree but with demonstrated technical competency and direct experience supporting engineering, supplier qualification, or technical procurement will also be considered. What We Offer Competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans. Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance. Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs and sponsorship for continuing education. An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations. The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy. Opportunities for continuous learning and training to grow throughout your career! Pay: $70,000 - $103,000 The base salary range for this position in Tennessee (US-TN) at the start of employment is expected to be between $70,000 and $103,000 per year. description: Description Amazon is seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager to join the Global Corporate Procurement (GCP) Team. This is an exciting opportunity to be a part of a team that has a meaningful and measurable impact on Amazon’s success. At Amazon, our vision is to be Earth's most customer-centric company. Our passion for invention leads us to pioneer and globalize new businesses and customer offerings daily. As we rapidly become the world’s largest consumer of services in many categories, the Corporate Procurement team is fueling our explosive growth by identifying innovative sourcing strategies and negotiating sustainable, long-term partnerships. We are seeking a skilled Strategic Sourcing Manager with experience leading complex sourcing initiatives across Employee Services. Key leadership traits required include the ability to influence and form partnerships with business leaders, and operational excellence in managing multiple complex and competing priorities simultaneously. Strategic Sourcing Managers are expert practitioners in the tools for creating competitive environments and have a bias for decision-making rooted in data and analytics. They routinely influence vendor relationships by advising Amazon leaders across multiple stakeholder groups on the direction of sourcing projects in support of business goals. If you are looking for a new challenge in a fast-paced, innovative company, come make history with Amazon’s Global Corporate Procurement department. At Amazon, we believe that in-person collaboration is essential to our culture and innovation. While we allow flexibility for personal circumstances, we generally expect employees to work from our offices five days a week. This approach has consistently shown that spontaneous interactions, rapid problem-solving, and the energy of in-person teamwork led to better results for our customers. Our data shows that teams working together in person are more effective at making complex decisions, onboarding new team members, and fostering the kind of creative collaboration that has driven Amazon's success. The serendipitous hallway conversations and impromptu whiteboarding sessions that happen naturally in an office environment have proven invaluable to our invention process and maintaining our high bar for excellence. Key job responsibilities Establishing strong relationships with internal business stakeholders; building a strong understanding of strategic business direction, requirements and priorities across assigned suppliers and/or spend categories Dive deep across multiple business units to leverage our supplier base with the goal of optimizing performance, quality, and cost Evaluate supplier core competencies and competitive positioning using industry cost models and benchmarking; leveraging key-insights to inform and support the strategic sourcing strategy development process Managing the fundamentals of sourcing and supplier engagement activities including RFx, spend pattern analysis, contract analysis, bid evaluation, negotiations, and supplier consolidation Identifying sourcing opportunities by leveraging spend analysis tools and engage with stakeholders to consolidate requirements over categories, suppliers and geographies Work with business and finance leaders to identify and drive savings and controllership improvements, optimizing the return on investment and total cost of ownership Providing guidance to internal stakeholders on procurement processes and best-practice tools, such as category management, supplier evaluation and supplier diversity A day in the life Your morning might start with a cross-functional alignment call for an upcoming RFP involving three business units, followed by analyzing bid responses and building a recommendation deck for senior leadership. After lunch, you're on a negotiation call with a strategic supplier's C-suite to finalize contract terms, then pivoting to a spend review with Finance to validate savings actuals against targets. You'll close the day by coaching a business partner through the supplier evaluation framework for an upcoming engagement. No two days look the same — you'll balance long-range strategic planning with hands-on execution, often managing five or more active sourcing engagements simultaneously across different stages of the lifecycle. About The Team Global Corporate Procurement (GCP) manages Amazon's indirect spend across Employee Services, Marketing, Professional Services, Technology, Logistics, and Real Estate & Facilities. We're a global team of sourcing professionals who combine analytical rigor with creative problem-solving to deliver sustainable value at scale. Our culture values deep ownership, intellectual curiosity, and a bias for action — we move fast, but we move smart. You'll be joining a team where your work is visible to senior leadership and directly tied to Amazon's bottom line. Basic Qualifications Experience in an indirect procurement function at a multinational corporation Proficiency in best-in-class procurement processes, including category management, benchmarking, should-cost modeling, RFx, reverse auctions, and contract development Experience managing multiple indirect spend categories, some of which may include the following: IT Software, IT Services, Corporate Services, Marketing, Contingent Labor, Facilities and Real Estate, Capital Expenditure, and Human Resources/Employee Services 5+ years of experience developing, leading, negotiating, and executing end-to-end sourcing engagements Demonstrated experience in Employee Services and HR-related procurement, including sourcing and managing spend in areas such as HR Services, Employee Benefits, and/or Pharmacy/Drug Programs, with a track record in vendor strategy development, competitive bidding, and contract negotiations Preferred Qualifications Experience in project management Bachelor's degree or equivalent Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. description: About Fluidstack We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI. We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply! How We Operate Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role. Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible. Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins. Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward. Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world. The Supply Chain Team Examples of key problems the team is working on Supply compute at a scale of 10s to 100s of GWs, the largest build out of compute in history. Qualify and dual-source across every critical equipment category, with lead-time and capacity thresholds tied directly to the forward build pipeline. Make supply chain the reason we build faster than anyone. Our modular build redefines speed in this industry, and it lives or dies on supply chain. Keep procurement permanently off the critical path so schedule compression stays our advantage, not our constraint. Build the most accurate supply chain prediction modelling that exists. Use the frontier of AI to forecast lead times, demand, and disruption with a precision the industry has never had, and turn that foresight into a structural edge. Role Scope Own sourcing for everything a new site needs to go live: site services, temporary power and water, security, waste, and facilities support. Build the site readiness sourcing playbook so each new site procures its full service stack in weeks, not months. Negotiate regional and multi-site agreements that new sites inherit on day one. Coordinate need-by dates with construction and operations so no service gap ever idles a site. What We're Looking For The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. You've sourced site services or indirect categories for multi-site industrial operations. You've stood up procurement for a greenfield site and know every category that gets forgotten. You build playbooks that make the second site faster than the first. You negotiate rate cards that hold across geographies. Bonus: Data center or construction site services. Utility coordination. Security services contracting. Facilities management agreements. We are committed to pay equity and transparency. Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law. You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch. Compensation Range: $175K - $250K

This position will set the standard for leadership and the sharing of Logistics best practices across the various business units by demonstrating in-depth knowledge of the industry. Role will require development of RFIs and RFPs as well as leading negotiations and execution of contracts. description: Job Summary: The Manager, Sourcing & Procurement, is responsible for leading sourcing, procurement, supplier management, and contract negotiation activities that support manufacturing, commercial, clinical, and corporate operations. This is a hands-on leadership role for an experienced procurement professional to oversee the development of all Requests for Quotes and Proposals, Capital Projects, support award selection, lead purchase negotiations and complete contract commitments. The role drives process and budget improvements through continuous improvement incentives and enforces ethical and effective procurement practices within the buyer team. This position is ideal for a collaborative, business-focused procurement leader who thrives in a fastpaced biotechnology environment and enjoys rolling up their sleeves to solve problems, build supplier relationships, and drive results. Key Responsibilities: Strategic Sourcing & Procurement • Lead sourcing activities for goods and services that support manufacturing, laboratory, facilities, corporate, and commercial operations. • Develop and execute sourcing strategies that balance quality, service, risk, and cost considerations. • Lead supplier selection initiatives, including RFIs, RFQs, and RFPs. • Evaluate supplier capabilities and participate in supplier qualification activities. • Identify opportunities for cost savings, process improvements, and supplier consolidation. Contract Negotiation • Lead negotiations of supplier agreements, service contracts, Statements of Work (SOWs), Master Service Agreements (MSAs), and other commercial contracts. • Partner closely with Legal, Finance, Quality, Operations, and business stakeholders to negotiate favorable commercial terms while mitigating risk. • Ensure contracts align with company policies and business objectives. • Manage contract renewals, amendments, and supplier performance obligations. Hands-On Procurement Leadership • Personally perform sourcing and procurement activities when needed to support business priorities. • Balance leadership responsibilities with direct execution of procurement initiatives. • Support day-to-day purchasing operations and assist with escalations as necessary. • Foster a culture of accountability, responsiveness, customer service, and continuous improvement. Team Leadership • Lead, coach, and develop procurement personnel. • Establish goals, priorities, and workload distribution across the procurement function. • Provide guidance and support on sourcing strategies, supplier negotiations, and procurement best practices. • Promote a collaborative and service-oriented team culture. Cross-Functional Partnership • Partner with Manufacturing, Quality, Technical Operations, Facilities, Finance, Clinical, and Commercial teams to understand business requirements. • Communicate effectively with internal stakeholders regarding sourcing strategies, supplier performance, and project status. • Support capital projects and strategic business initiatives through procurement expertise and supplier engagement. • Works directly with VMI contact for ensuring adequate levels of inventory. • Other duties as assigned. Requirements: Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, Procurement, Operations, Finance, or a related field. • 5+ years of progressive sourcing, procurement, or supply chain experience. • 2+ years leadership experience with direct reports. • Demonstrated experience negotiating supplier agreements, service contracts, and commercial terms within the United States. • Experience managing vendor relationships and supplier performance. • Experience leading RFIs, RFQs, RFPs, and supplier selection processes. • Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills. • Proven ability to effectively interact with vendors, service providers, and cross-functional business stakeholders. • Experience working with ERP systems and procurement tools. • Strong organizational, negotiation, and problem-solving skills. Preferred • Experience within biotechnology, pharmaceutical, life sciences, medical device, CDMO, or other regulated manufacturing environments. • Previous people leadership, supervisory, or team lead experience. • Knowledge of GMP-regulated manufacturing environments. • Experience supporting manufacturing, facilities, laboratory, engineering, capital equipment, or professional services procurement. • CPSM, CPM, APICS, or other relevant procurement certifications. • Experience working in small-to-mid-sized biotechnology or pharmaceutical organizations where procurement leaders are expected to balance management responsibilities with hands-on execution. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements: • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, stand, walk, and use hands to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and mobile phone. • Ability to use computer, to read written materials and to complete paperwork activities; • Ability to communicate well with individuals by telephone and in person.

description: About KARL STORZ From the operating room to surgery centers—and everywhere in between—KARL STORZ North America is a global leader in medical technology and advanced visualization solutions. We design specialty innovations, smart instruments and devices, integrated ecosystems, and intelligent imaging—to build a more connected, software-enabled operating room. As an independent, family-owned MedTech company, we ambitiously think in generations instead of quarters to improve patients’ lives around the world. About The Role KARL STORZ is seeking a Senior Project Buyer to lead end-to-end procurement activities across key projects and purchasing categories. This role will develop and execute sourcing strategies while balancing cost, quality, delivery, technical requirements, and long-term supply continuity. As a senior commercial partner, you’ll work closely with Engineering, Project Management, Quality, Operations, and our global procurement network to lead supplier selection and negotiations, manage commercial and supply risk, and ensure materials are ready for a successful transition into production. This role requires up to 20% travel . What You’ll Do Lead competitive sourcing processes, including RFPs, RFQs, and RFIs, for complex project and material requirements. Develop and execute project and category sourcing strategies focused on total cost, quality, delivery, capacity, compliance, and supply continuity. Identify, evaluate, qualify, onboard, and develop suppliers in partnership with Engineering, Supplier Quality, Legal, Risk, Master Data, and Operational Procurement. Lead supplier negotiations, commercial bid evaluations, cost breakdowns, benchmarking, and total-cost-of-ownership analyses. Manage contracts, NDAs, supplier agreements, purchase orders, and other commercial documentation in accordance with procurement and legal requirements. Build strategic supplier relationships and lead supplier performance, risk, capacity, and continuity discussions. Develop mitigation strategies for supplier risks, including alternate sourcing, capacity planning, inventory strategies, and recovery plans. Partner with Engineering and project teams to translate technical, electrical, mechanical, and quality requirements into actionable sourcing plans. Lead procurement activities throughout prototyping, design transfer, product release, and sustaining phases. Lead make-versus-buy and buy-versus-buy assessments and present data-driven recommendations to senior leadership. Develop procurement schedules, identify critical-path materials, monitor supplier commitments, and proactively escalate project risks. Oversee key Material Requirements Planning and demand forecasting activities, including inventory analysis, backorder mitigation, PO reporting, and inventory turns. Collaborate with Marketing and Product Management to develop demand and supply plans. Maintain accurate SAP purchasing records, supplier confirmations, pricing conditions, purchase orders, and material data. Track and report procurement KPIs, including savings, cost avoidance, supplier performance, lead times, sourcing progress, and project risk. Coordinate the hand-off of released materials, supplier agreements, sourcing documentation, and open actions to Operational Purchasing. Mentor Project Buyers and provide onboarding, coaching, and practical guidance without direct supervisory responsibility. Identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities across sourcing, procurement processes, supplier collaboration, and data quality. What You Bring 5+ years of relevant procurement, sourcing, supply chain, or transferable experience. Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Finance, Business, Accounting, Manufacturing, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant work experience. Demonstrated experience with strategic sourcing, supplier selection, contract negotiation, commercial analysis, and supplier risk management. Strong SAP or comparable ERP/MRP experience, including purchase orders, supplier data, pricing, and material master management. Experience developing and executing material group or category sourcing strategies. Experience managing projects and partnering with cross-functional teams. Strong analytical skills with the ability to review large amounts of data and translate findings into actionable recommendations. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong organizational, problem-solving, and time-management skills. Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing business needs. What Will Make You Successful Master’s degree in Supply Chain or a related discipline and/or certifications such as CPSM, CPIM, CSCP, or equivalent credentials. Experience creating and presenting make-versus-buy, buy-versus-buy, supplier selection, and commercial recommendations to senior leadership. Advanced Microsoft Excel and broader Microsoft Office Suite skills. Strong knowledge of Material Requirements Planning, demand forecasting, inventory management, and SAP. Ability to combine financial and business acumen with strong supplier negotiation and relationship-management skills. Experience working across global, multicultural, and cross-functional teams. Ability to constructively challenge sourcing assumptions and identify opportunities for value engineering, standardization, cost reduction, and supply-chain improvement. A results-oriented, self-motivated approach with the ability to work independently while effectively influencing stakeholders across multiple functions. Strong knowledge within assigned purchasing categories and the ability to serve as a procurement subject-matter expert. Why KARL STORZ? Join KARL STORZ and be part of a team creating medical innovations that truly make a difference. Beyond technology, you’ll be part of a culture that values talent as its greatest asset, empowering you to contribute to a mission that improves patient care worldwide. Ready to make an impact? Apply to be our next Senior Project Buyer and help us build the future of MedTech together.

job_title: Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager - Supplier Development
description: Your role The Strategic Sourcing role is accountable for developing and executing a sustainable procurement strategy within their assigned commodity area. This includes establishing and managing long‑term agreements and service‑level commitments, optimising and rationalising the supplier base, and ensuring effective supplier onboarding. A key focus of the role is strengthening supply chain resilience by building. As Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager - Supplier Development, you will execute sourcing strategies that secure qualified capacity for production ramp-up and build a competitive, resilient supply base. You will lead supplier selection, negotiation, onboarding, qualification coordination, launch readiness, and performance, with particular focus on new product introduction, dual sourcing, and continuity of supply. This is a senior individual-contributor role with no direct reports. Manager reflects accountability for sourcing strategies, supplier relationships, spend, contracts, risk, and results. What You Will Do Develop category and supplier strategies aligned with growth, NPI, production ramp-up, cost, capacity, quality, and supply-resilience priorities. Lead market analysis, RFIs, RFQs and RFPs, total-cost evaluation, negotiations, supplier selection, awards, and agreements. Assess suppliers for capability, capacity, processes, quality systems, financial health, scalability, compliance, and risk. Coordinate supplier onboarding and qualification across Engineering, Supplier Quality, Operations, Planning, Finance, and other functions, with clear milestones, owners, risks, and escalations. Facilitate product and part qualification, including specifications, samples, tooling, first articles, validation, deviation closure, approvals, and production release. Engineering and Quality own technical requirements, validation decisions, and formal approval; you drive supplier response, timing, commercial readiness, escalation, and completion. Secure capacity and launch readiness through reviews, forecasts, lead-time and flexibility commitments, inventory plans, and commercial agreements. Build dual-source and continuity plans for critical parts and single-source risks, coordinating alternate-source qualification with technical and quality teams. Lead supplier reviews, performance improvement, and recovery plans covering quality, delivery, capacity, cost, compliance, and risk. Deliver savings, cost avoidance, working-capital improvement, productivity, and total-cost benefits without compromising quality or continuity. Develop supplier relationships that improve access to capacity, technology, and innovation while meeting legal, ethical, sustainability, and Atlas Copco requirements. To succeed, you will need Typically 5-8 years of experience in strategic sourcing, category management, supplier development, procurement, or supply chain, preferably in engineered products or manufacturing. Success sourcing, negotiating with, qualifying, onboarding, and ramping suppliers for NPI or production growth. Experience coordinating suppliers and cross-functional teams through qualification and production release. Strong negotiation, contract management, cost analysis, total-cost, supplier-performance, and risk-management capabilities. Ability to interpret technical drawings, specifications, bills of material, manufacturing processes, and supplier-capability information. Strong communication, influence, judgment, analytical problem-solving, and project leadership without formal authority. Bachelor's degree in supply chain, engineering, business, operations, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Location and travel: This position may be remote within the United States or hybrid; residence near Saugerties, New York, is not required. Approximately 40% travel is expected, primarily to supplier sites for qualification, launch readiness, business reviews, improvement, and issue resolution, and to company locations. Travel will be mainly within North America, with international travel as needed. Arrangements are subject to company policy, employment eligibility, payroll and tax requirements, and business needs. In return, we offer Culture of trust and accountability Lifelong learning and career growth Innovation powered by people Comprehensive compensation and benefits 401k Automatic Company Contribution and match Generous PTO package Annual Variable Compensation Program Salary: $125,000-$150,000/yr Job location This position may be remote within the United States or hybrid; residence near Saugerties, New York, is not required. description: Job Summary The Senior Buyer is responsible for the strategic sourcing, negotiation, and procurement of fabricated and machined aerospace components. description: At DuPont, our purpose is to empower the world with essential innovations to thrive. We work on things that matter. Discover the many reasons the world’s most talented people are choosing to work at DuPont. DuPont's Global Procurement team is looking for a Senior Project Buyer – Operating Materials & Services to lead procurement for capital and operational projects across the company. This is a visible role with real influence. You'll be the main procurement contact for capital and site teams and represent the team to internal business groups. You'll also guide other project buyers and work closely with the commodity buy team. Your sourcing, contracting and negotiating will directly affect project cost, schedule and success. What You'll Do Shape sourcing strategy from the start Build and carry out sourcing strategies that fit each project's scope, schedule and budget. Get involved early in the project lifecycle to shape procurement and contracting decisions. Assign projects to other buyers based on buy type and team workload. Lead high-value sourcing and contracting Run the full sourcing process for major packages: RFI/RFP/RFQ, technical and commercial bid evaluation, and award. Structure and negotiate complex contracts (lump-sum, reimbursable, unit-rate and hybrid), balancing risk and value. Design contracting strategies that fit each project's risk profile and current market conditions. Negotiate and deliver measurable value Negotiate pricing, payment milestones, warranties, liquidated damages, retention and performance guarantees. Drive cost savings, cost avoidance and value engineering without compromising safety, quality or schedule. Manage currency, escalation and commodity-linked pricing on long-duration contracts. Build strong supplier and contractor partnerships With the commodity buy team, qualify, evaluate and manage OEMs, fabricators, EPC contractors and engineering firms. Manage supplier performance through expediting, inspection and progress monitoring until delivery. Manage risk and governance Find and reduce schedule, quality, financial and single-source risks on the critical path. Ensure compliance with capital approval (AFE) processes, delegation of authority, safety rules and regulatory standards. Work Across Functions And Keep Leaders Informed Work with Engineering, Business, Legal, Finance and Operations to keep procurement in step with project milestones. Prepare executive-ready updates on capital commitments, savings, cash flow and procurement risk using Power BI and Excel. Support project audits, cost forecasting and closeout. Lead Strategic Sourcing activities for designated sites by competitive bidding process and contract negotiations. Leverages area vendor base to lower TCO identifying aggregated spend benefits opportunities across the region. Negotiate with support from Category Management for local volumes, processes, quality levels, and prices. Negotiates regional area purchasing contracts. Manage and develop Buyers where required. Ensure procurement policies and procedures are conveyed to end users in the Procurement of goods and services. description: Our Sensors Division in Tempe, AZ is seeking a Senior Buyer to join our dynamic team! The Senior Buyer will take a lead role in procurement activities for complex and technical materials and services. This individual will be responsible for managing supplier relationships, driving cost reduction strategies, and ensuring optimal inventory levels to support production schedules. This position works cross-functionally with manufacturing, engineering, planning, and quality teams to ensure timely and cost-effective purchasing decisions in alignment with business goals. Location: Tempe, AZ Salary Range: $67,400 - 90,000 per year plus bonus Please note that the salary range information provided is a general guideline only, reflecting a position based in Arizona. Criteria such as the candidate’s qualifications and relevant experience, the scope of the specific position, as well as market and business considerations will be evaluated when extending an offer. Develop and implement sourcing strategies, vendor selection processes, and cost-saving initiatives. Coordinate purchasing activities with manufacturing, planning, and engineering departments to meet production needs. Negotiate pricing, terms, and conditions with suppliers to secure favorable agreements that align with company objectives. Track and expedite complex purchase orders; update shipping and delivery schedules proactively. Resolve supplier-related issues including claims, rejections, over/under shipments, engineering changes, and cancellations. Analyze supplier performance metrics and conduct site visits to evaluate production capabilities and compliance. Collaborate with Accounts Payable to address and resolve invoicing discrepancies. Monitor market trends, perform make-versus-buy analysis, and evaluate alternative sourcing opportunities. Provide guidance and mentorship to junior buyers or procurement staff as needed. What You Bring Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field. 7+ years of progressive purchasing or supply chain experience in a manufacturing or technical environment. Proficiency in MS Office and experience with ERP/MRP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle). Strong knowledge of engineering drawings, technical specifications, and manufacturing processes. Demonstrated ability to perform price/cost analysis and contract negotiations. PMAC, ISM, or APICS certification preferred (e.g., CPM, CPSM, CPIM). Familiarity with Lean manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies is a plus. Excellent communication, negotiation, and analytical skills Who We Are With over 50 years of experience in aviation technology, Curtiss-Wright's Sensors & Controls Division is continuing the legacy of flight innovation, providing critical components on a variety of commercial, defense and industrial platforms. Curtiss-Wright's Sensors & Controls Division is a key partner to major commercial aerospace original equipment manufacturers, including Boeing and Airbus. The Division includes businesses that produce high performance electro-mechanical actuation, precision position sensors, fluid controls and motion control subsystems, as well as complex structural components for aerospace applications. description: 7-Eleven is an iconic family of brands with over 86,000 locations, surpassing every retailer in the world. We revolutionize convenience, restaurants and fuel through cutting edge innovation — working hard to be the customer's first choice. 7-Eleven empowers our employees to "activate awesome" and make a meaningful impact in their stores and communities every day. If you're ready to grow, lead and make a difference, come join our team and help shape the future of convenience. Job Summary As the Associate Sourcing Manager, you will be responsible for sourcing/procurement related activities and processes associated with the acquisition of products and services, which will include store equipment (store fixtures, food & beverage equipment, refrigeration, HVAC, signage, parts and building materials) as well as related services, including Asset Protection This includes requirements gathering, creating and issuing Request for Proposal (RFP), proposal evaluation, contract negotiations, contract drafting and administration with the goal to improve spend and quality performance. This role supports Sourcing Managers or Directors and ensures compliance with 7-Eleven sourcing policies and processes. As an Associate Sourcing Manager, you will partner with business stakeholders and suppliers to execute procurement/sourcing activities while building collaborative relationships to deliver improved cost and service levels. KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITES Executes 7-Eleven sourcing processes which include data/spend analysis, strategic planning and market research, scoping, bidding, contract negotiations and execution, compliance, and supplier management activities for assigned categories. Build and maintain collaborative relationships with cross functional stakeholders to develop and execute sourcing processes that support business goals Build and execute various RFx/sourcing events, performing bid analysis and providing feedback to stakeholders and collaborate on negotiation strategies. Manage suppliers/contractors based on specifications and contractual requirements to ensure effective execution, implementation and prompt resolution of any issues that may arise. Negotiate contracts and contract renewals with suppliers to source/procure products or services needed for categories to optimize spend, reduce risk, achieve favorable terms and drive towards optimized total-cost-of-ownership. Identify/interview potential suppliers and evaluate supplier capabilities to determine if supplier is qualified to produce and/or supply products or services. Perform market research in applicable areas. Ability to support legal in key contract negotiations such as pricing, performance measures, and breach of contract remedies and termination options. Participate in cross-functional discussions with stakeholders. Provide clear and concise progress updates. Demonstrate ability to build and analyze financial models to evaluate proposal scenarios and present recommendations in a clear and concise format. KEY LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES Ability to work well with both business stakeholders and suppliers, in a fast-paced, self-directed environment. Understand leaders’ intent and strategic goals and how to translate that into actions that needs to be taken Ability to provide suggestions and collaborate with team and stakeholders to solve problems by assessing the situation, leveraging and analyzing relevant data, identifying root cause and developing potential solutions. Adapt to change, ability to quickly learn details of new business challenges and identify dependencies and impacts of other key initiatives. Education And Experience EDUCATION: Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent experience) strongly preferred. YEARS OF RELEVANT WORK EXPERIENCE: Minimum of 3+ years required Specific Knowledge And Skills Demonstrate ability to build and analyze financial models to evaluate proposal scenarios and present recommendations in a clear and concise format. Strong organizational skills, understanding of legal aspects, negotiating skills, purchasing terminology, cost analysis, and legal compliance regulations Experience and background in store equipment (store fixtures, food & beverage equipment, refrigeration, HVAC, signage, parts and building materials) as well as related services, including Asset Protection in retail, food service or restaurants and sourcing/procurement of products/services in this space strongly preferred. Forecasting and Demand Planning: Coordinate demand forecasting efforts and support day-to-day business as needed. Supply Chain Issue Resolution: Troubleshoot and resolve operational and supply chain challenges to ensure timely product availability, consistency and performance. Supplier & New Item Setup: Support onboarding of new suppliers and product setups, ensuring compliance and efficient integration. Proficient with MS Office suite – including MS Excel, Outlook, and Powerpoint. Location: Dublin, CA (Hybrid: in-office collaboration with remote flexibility) Base Salary Range: Up to $150-175k +Bonus Key Responsibilities Strategic Sourcing & Execution ● Develop and execute multi-year sourcing strategies for Industrial Construction (e.g., steel structures, concrete, MEP systems) and Facilities Maintenance (e.g., conveyor systems, forklifts, racking). ● Lead analytics to identify high-risk and high-cost categories, creating multi-year sourcing roadmaps. ● Partner cross-functionally with Property Development, Engineering, Project Management, Legal, Risk Management, and Finance to align on project requirements and milestones. ● Manage end-to-end competitive sourcing events (RFPs), vendor evaluations, clean sheet analysis, market index analysis, and total cost of ownership (TCO) modeling. ● Onboard qualified suppliers and contractors, monitoring performance via key metrics, quarterly business reviews (QBRs), and executive supplier meetings. ● Drive bottom-up cost estimation and cost-saving initiatives through value engineering and competitive bidding. ● Facilitate seamless operational handover from Property Development to Facilities Maintenance upon site go-live. description: The Company Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Dexcom began as a small company with a big dream: To forever change how diabetes is managed. To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We are broadening our vision beyond diabetes to empower people to take control of health. That means personalized, actionable insights aimed at solving important health challenges. To continue what we've started: Improving human health. We are driven by thousands of ambitious, passionate people worldwide who are willing to fight like warriors to earn the trust of our customers by listening, serving with integrity, thinking big, and being dependable. We've already changed millions of lives and we're ready to change millions more. Our future ambition is to become a leading consumer health technology company while continuing to develop solutions for serious health conditions. We'll get there by constantly reinventing unique biosensing-technology experiences. Though we've come a long way from our small company days, our dreams are bigger than ever. The opportunity to improve health on a global scale stands before us. Meet The Team The Direct Materials Sourcing team is a group of category experts responsible for building resilient supply networks, securing capacity, managing total cost, enabling new product introduction, and reducing supply risk. As the Staff Strategic Sourcing Manager, you will lead sourcing strategy across Mechanical Assembly and key material categories, partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Quality, Finance, Legal, and external suppliers to deliver business results. Where You Come In Develop and execute short- and long-term category strategies for mechanical assemblies, molding, metal stamping, needle manufacturing, converting, adhesives, and resins. Own the supplier relationship for assigned categories and serve as the primary commercial leader across Tier 1 suppliers and critical sub-tier suppliers. Lead supplier selection, sourcing events, negotiations, contracting, cost improvement, capacity planning, and business continuity initiatives. Build strategies that extend through the full value chain, including raw materials, tooling, manufacturing processes, contract manufacturers, Tier 1 suppliers, and sub-tiers. Partner with R&D, Sustaining Engineering, Operations, Quality, and NPI teams to ensure supplier readiness, manufacturability, continuity of supply, and successful product launches. Develop supplier relationship management plans, assess commercial and operational risk, and implement practical mitigation and second-source strategies. Use market intelligence, should-cost analysis, total cost of ownership, and fact-based business cases to influence decisions and secure leadership alignment. Position Strategic Sourcing as a competitive advantage for Dexcom by bringing external innovation, supplier capabilities, cost leadership, resiliency, and speed to the business. What Makes You Successful Proven strategic sourcing or category management experience supporting mechanical assemblies and related direct materials in a regulated manufacturing environment. Working knowledge of molding, metal stamping, needle manufacturing, converting, adhesives, and resins, including key manufacturing processes, cost drivers, capacity constraints, and supply market dynamics. Demonstrated ability to manage Tier 1 and sub-tier supplier relationships, including performance, commercial strategy, risk, capacity, quality, and continuity of supply. Strong negotiation, contracting, supplier relationship management, and stakeholder influence skills. Credible, engaging, and knowledgeable communication style, with the ability to build trust across technical, operational, and executive stakeholders. Ability to become a trusted business advisor for assigned categories by translating market, supplier, technical, and financial insights into clear recommendations. Ability to develop quantitative and qualitative business cases, communicate tradeoffs, and gain support from senior leadership. Proven record of delivering results in a matrix organization while leading cross-functional initiatives with clear ownership and follow-through. Strong financial analysis, market analysis, strategic planning, project management, and problem-solving capabilities. High proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint, with the ability to extract insights from complex data and communicate them with executive-level clarity. Preferred Qualifications Experience in medical device, life sciences, or another highly regulated manufacturing industry. Knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, value engineering, should-cost, and total cost of ownership principles. Experience supporting new product introduction, supplier transitions, tooling, capacity expansion, and business continuity planning. Practical knowledge of eProcurement, spend analytics, supplier performance, and contract lifecycle management systems. Leadership Impact Success in this role means creating category strategies that the business trusts, suppliers understand, and cross-functional teams can execute. The Staff Strategic Sourcing Manager is expected to bring informed judgment, strong commercial leadership, and a collaborative presence that elevates supplier relationships and positions Strategic Sourcing as a source of competitive advantage for Dexcom. Access to career development through in-house learning programs and/or qualified tuition reimbursement. An exciting and innovative, industry-leading organization committed to our employees, customers, and the communities we serve. At this level a graduate degree may be desirable with 4 years of related experience. description: About Fluidstack We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role. Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible. Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins. Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. Job Title: Strategic Sourcing Manager, New Product Development Location : Mocksville, NC About Us Imagine a company with technology leadership of over 160 years, yet it operates with the energy of a startup. Ingersoll Rand has dedicated itself to Making Life Better for its employees, customers, shareholders, and planets. We produce innovative and mission-critical flow creation and life science technologies – from compressors to precision handling of liquids, gasses, and powers – to increase industrial productivity, efficiency, and sustainability. Supported by over 80+ brands, our products are used in various end-markets including life sciences, food and beverage, clean energy, industrial manufacturing, infrastructure, and more. Across the globe, we’re driving growth with an entrepreneurial spirit and ownership mindset. Learn more at irco.com and join us to own your future. Job Overview : Lead the team. Shape the products. Influence what comes next. Ingersoll Rand is evolving its compressor portfolio, and sourcing will help determine how that future takes shape. As a Sourcing Leader within the Compression Systems & Services Americas Sourcing Organization, you’ll lead the people and supplier decisions that bring new products, redesigns, and Innovate to Value (i2V) initiatives from concept through launch. Your greatest impact starts with the team. You’ll develop an established group of sourcing professionals, giving them the coaching, tools, and confidence to make sound decisions and take ownership of their work. Through clear priorities, thoughtful delegation, and meaningful accountability, you’ll strengthen the team’s capabilities while removing barriers and keeping sourcing commitments aligned with project milestones. You’ll also lead selected projects yourself, combining people leadership with hands-on sourcing execution. Working closely with engineering, project and product management, operations, quality, finance, commodity teams, and suppliers, you’ll guide direct-material sourcing across an industrial compressor portfolio. The work spans components such as motors, drives, electronic controls, and heavy castings within a global supply base. You’ll set sourcing direction, develop supplier strategies, lead complex negotiations, and advance dual-sourcing and risk-mitigation efforts suited to a manufacturing environment with a broad product mix and lower production volumes. You’ll also help define how the team measures success: making progress visible, identifying schedule risks early, and connecting sourcing decisions to cost savings, product margins, quality, and supply assurance. As legacy products evolve and new platforms move toward production, your leadership will help turn sourcing strategy into measurable results. For a sourcing professional who enjoys developing people, solving complex supplier challenges, and seeing decisions take shape in real products, this is an opportunity to influence both how the team performs and what Ingersoll Rand brings to market next. Responsibilities : Sourcing Strategy and Project Leadership: Lead sourcing strategy for NPD and I2V initiatives from early concept through launch and stabilization. Align sourcing resources and deliverables with business objectives, project gates, commodity strategies, supplier rationalization, plant needs, localization objectives, and regional priorities. People Leadership and Team Development: Lead, coach, and develop sourcing professionals supporting NPD, value engineering, localization, supplier transitions, and productivity projects. Set goals, prioritize assignments, balance workloads, conduct performance discussions, and support career development and succession planning. Build capability through best practices, collaboration, barrier removal, and a culture of ownership and accountability. Supplier Selection and Commercial Management: Lead supplier selection, sourcing decisions, RFPs, RFQs, and negotiations, balancing cost, quality, delivery, lead time, capacity, risk, and long-term supplier capability. Oversee pricing, payment terms, tooling, inventory programs, capacity commitments, and supplier development needs. Cost Management and Value Improvement: Own sourcing cost models, business case inputs, and project cost tracking for legacy-to-new product comparisons, productivity targets, and launch readiness. Drive I2V and VAVE workstreams to identify cost reduction, design-to-value, supplier optimization, localization, and specification improvement opportunities. Project Governance and Performance Tracking: Establish standard work, reporting cadence, and performance measures that provide visibility to sourcing milestones, risks, savings, cost avoidance, and launch readiness. Represent Sourcing in product gate reviews, plant reviews, VAVE events, MMR events, and leadership operating reviews, ensuring actions are documented, assigned, and completed. Risk Resolution and Supplier Recovery: Identify gaps to project goals and lead cross-functional countermeasures addressing cost, supplier readiness, part qualification, capacity, delivery, and quality. Manage supplier escalations and recovery plans when issues threaten launches, customer commitments, warranty performance, or project timelines. Cross-Functional Partnerships and Continuous Improvement: Build strong relationships with engineering, product management, operations, quality, finance, commodity leaders, plant teams, and suppliers to align priorities, resolve conflict, and maximize value. Facilitate continuous improvement and ideation sessions to build the project pipeline and strengthen sourcing execution. Special Projects and Additional Responsibilities: Lead or participate in special projects and perform additional duties as assigned. Requirements : Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Engineering, Operations, or a related field. 7+ years of progressively responsible experience in sourcing, supply chain, engineering, operations, or project leadership, including direct-material sourcing and support for NPD, VAVE, I2V, and / or complex cross-functional programs. 3+ years of people leadership, supervisory, or team-lead experience, including assigning work, setting priorities, coaching employees, monitoring performance, and supporting employee development. 3+ years of experience coordinating sourcing deliverables with engineering and project management teams through structured development processes, including tracking milestones, resolving barriers, and addressing schedule risks. 3+ years of experience evaluating supplier quotations, selecting suppliers, negotiating pricing and commercial terms, and managing supplier development or performance issues; to include progressive experience preparing business cases and cost models, tracking savings, and analyzing sourcing data to identify gaps and recommend corrective actions. 3+ years of advanced Microsoft Excel experience, including pivot tables and macros; experience using Word and PowerPoint to communicate business information; and general knowledge of how ERP/MRP systems support purchasing, materials planning, and manufacturing operations. Core Competencies : Strategic Sourcing Leadership: Translates business priorities into actionable sourcing strategies with proactive planning and sound judgment. People Leadership and Talent Development: Coaches and empowers employees while building trust, collaboration, and accountability. NPD and I2V Execution: Align

Position Title: Buyer II Location: Irvine, CA Work Arrangement: On-Site Position Summary Buyer II is responsible for performing intermediate-level procurement activities to support organizational operations. description: Job Description Join Century A/C Supply , proudly part of Rheem , a global leader in Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) innovation! description: We're Hiring: Buyer Location : Ontario, CA Company : Pelican Products Inc. Who We Are At Pelican, we engineer products that stand up to the world’s toughest conditions—because the people who rely on us do too. For nearly 50 years, we’ve been a trusted partner for military personnel, first responders, outdoor adventurers, and innovators who push the limits. With a global presence that includes 11 offices, 4 manufacturing facilities, and 4 custom case centers, we create high-performance protective solutions that ensure our customers can focus on what matters most. Whether it’s transporting critical medical supplies, securing mission-essential equipment, or keeping expedition gear safe, Pelican products are Built to Protect to Equip for the Mission. At Pelican, your work has a real-world impact. You’ll be part of a team driven by innovation, craftsmanship, and the shared belief that when the mission is critical, failure isn’t an option. If you’re ready to build something that makes a difference, be part of a team that protects what matters most. Job Summary The Buyer independently manages purchasing activities for assigned materials, commodities, suppliers, and services to support production and business requirements. Conducts sourcing, supplier evaluation, negotiations, and purchasing analysis to optimize cost, quality, delivery, and inventory performance. Works cross-functionally to resolve supply issues, mitigate risk, and support continuous improvement within the Supply Chain organization. Primary Duties And Responsibilities Independently manages purchase orders and material requirements for assigned suppliers, commodities, or product categories. Reviews production requirements, inventory levels, lead times, and demand to ensure material availability and support appropriate inventory levels. Conducts sourcing activities, including RFQs, supplier evaluations, bid comparisons, and supplier recommendations based on cost, quality, delivery, capability, and business requirements. Negotiates pricing, lead times, delivery terms, minimum order quantities, and other commercial terms within assigned authority. Monitors supplier performance and works with suppliers to resolve delivery, quality, cost, capacity, and service issues. Identifies potential material shortages and supply disruptions and coordinates recovery or mitigation actions with suppliers and internal stakeholders. Investigates and resolves purchasing, inventory, invoice, receiving, and supplier-related discrepancies. Partners with Production Planning, Operations, Engineering, Quality, and other departments to support production requirements, new products, engineering changes, and business priorities. Identifies opportunities for cost savings, inventory optimization, lead-time reduction, and supplier performance improvement. Maintains accurate purchasing data, supplier information, pricing, lead times, and documentation within the ERP system. Supports supplier development and continuous improvement initiatives within the Supply Chain organization. Ensures purchasing activities comply with applicable laws, regulations, company policies, ethical business practices, and ISO requirements. Actively supports and complies with Pelican’s objectives, guidelines and commitment to Safety, Environment and Quality Performs other duties as assigned. Required Skills And Qualifications High school diploma or equivalent. Minimum 3–5 years of purchasing, procurement, supply chain, or related experience, preferably within a manufacturing environment. Demonstrated experience managing suppliers, purchase orders, material requirements, and sourcing activities. Working knowledge of supplier negotiations, RFQs, cost analysis, inventory management, and supplier performance. Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and decision-making skills. Ability to independently prioritize multiple assignments and resolve purchasing and supply-related issues. Effective verbal and written communication skills with the ability to work effectively with suppliers and cross-functional teams. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word, and Outlook. Experience using ERP/MRP systems. Must be eligible to receive information controlled under the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). The employee may also be required to perform non-standard physical activities including climbing, balancing, stooping, kneeling, and crouching. The employee must have the ability to lift and/or move up to 10 pounds frequently and up to 40 pounds occasionally in accordance with job requirements. We offer a relaxed and casual work environment, a strong commitment to giving back to communities, and a focus on employee satisfaction. With regular opportunities to share feedback with leadership and structured performance evaluations, we ensure that your voice is heard and your growth is supported. Competitive paid time off plans / Holiday pay /extra vacation purchase opportunities 401k plan – with immediate match Great Benefits – several options including Pet insurance for our animal lovers Health Savings Account Contribution Wellness Discount Program Global Mental Wellness Program Quarterly Employee Celebration Days Peer to Peer Recognition Program Service Recognition Program Employee referral program Employee discount program on Pelican Products and gear And more… Compensation & Benefits Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several U.S. geographic markets. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for the job location during the hiring process. We also offer a comprehensive package of benefits, including paid time off, 10 paid holidays per year, medical/dental/vision insurance, company-paid life and disability plans, and matching 401k to eligible employees. Pelican Products, Inc. is an equal employment opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected Veteran Status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
