description: Description ABOUT THE COMPANY NaturVet has been an industry leader in the development and manufacturing of natural pet supplements and other essential solutions for over 30 years. Our competitive advantage lies with our people, and we are committed to providing a safe and inclusive workplace, opportunities for advancement, and a healthy work-life balance. Located in Temecula, California, NaturVet is one of the largest pet supplement manufacturers in the United States. Our operations span four facilities within a two-mile radius, including two manufacturing facilities where we produce Soft Chews, Powders, Tablets, and Liquids for our trusted NaturVet brand and as private-label products for several high-profile companies. About The Role We are seeking a detail-oriented, proactive Strategic Buyer to support our manufacturing operations through effective sourcing, purchasing, and supplier relationship management. In this role, you will manage assigned purchasing categories from supplier selection and negotiations through purchase order execution, delivery coordination, and issue resolution to ensure materials are available when needed, meet quality requirements, and support business objectives. The Strategic Buyer balances strategic sourcing and supplier development with day-to-day purchasing execution. You will partner closely with Production, Operations, Planning, Quality, R&D, Finance, and other internal teams to maintain supply continuity, manage costs, improve purchasing efficiency, and address changing business needs. Depending on assigned categories and business priorities, responsibilities may include packaging, labels, ingredients, raw materials, maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) supplies, and other production-related materials. This role also supports supplier qualification, onboarding, quality documentation, and continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen supplier performance and purchasing processes. Core Responsibilities Purchasing & Supply Management: Manage the end-to-end purchasing process for assigned categories, including sourcing, purchase order creation and maintenance, order tracking, delivery coordination, and resolution of purchasing issues. Strategic Sourcing & Negotiations: Identify and evaluate suppliers, obtain competitive quotes, negotiate pricing and purchasing terms, research market trends, and identify cost-saving and sourcing opportunities. Supplier Relationship Management: Develop and maintain strong supplier relationships, monitor supplier performance, address service or delivery concerns, and support ongoing supplier evaluations and improvements. Material Availability & Inventory Support: Partner with internal teams to anticipate material requirements, monitor inventory and purchasing needs, and proactively address potential shortages, delays, or excess inventory. Supplier Qualification & Onboarding: Source and qualify new suppliers and coordinate onboarding documentation and internal approvals to ensure accurate and complete setup within the ERP system. Sample & Approval Coordination: Manage sample and First Article Inspection (FAI) processes, including sample requests, supplier follow-up, testing, evaluation, status tracking, and approval documentation. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Production, Operations, Planning, Quality, R&D, Finance, and other departments to align purchasing activities with production schedules, specifications, cost objectives, and business needs. Pricing & Invoice Resolution: Investigate pricing discrepancies and coordinate with suppliers, Finance, and internal stakeholders to support accurate invoicing and timely invoice approvals. Systems, Documentation & Compliance: Maintain accurate supplier, pricing, purchase order, and product information; support audits and supplier documentation requirements; and follow company policies, quality standards, applicable regulatory requirements, and food safety and GMP requirements. Team Support & Flexibility: Provide backup purchasing coverage across categories as needed, support assigned MRO purchasing activities, maintain standard operating procedures, and participate in cross-training and knowledge sharing. Requirements KEY QUALIFICATIONS Education & Experience High school diploma or GED required; bachelor's degree in business, supply chain management, or a related field preferred. At least 3 years of experience in purchasing, procurement, sourcing, or materials management. Experience in manufacturing, food and beverage, consumer packaged goods (CPG), supplements, cosmetics, or a similar industry preferred. Experience managing multiple purchasing categories, such as packaging, labels, ingredients, raw materials, MRO, or other manufacturing-related supplies, preferred. Skills & Competencies Strong supplier relationship management, sourcing, and negotiation skills, including the ability to manage pricing, lead times, material availability, and supplier performance. Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate options, resolve issues, and make sound decisions. Demonstrated ownership, accountability, and follow-through, with the ability to independently manage priorities and proactively address risks. Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a changing operational environment. Effective written and verbal communication skills and the ability to build productive relationships with suppliers and cross-functional teams. Ability to identify sourcing opportunities, recommend process improvements, and contribute to purchasing and supplier strategies. Knowledge of FDA regulations, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), and applicable industry compliance requirements. Ability to read, write, speak, and understand English sufficiently to communicate effectively, review purchasing documentation, and use business systems. Systems & Technology Strong proficiency with ERP systems and purchasing, procurement, inventory, or purchase order tracking systems. Above-average proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams. Compensation: $75,000–$90,000 annual salary Employment Type: Full-time, exempt, on-site in Temecula, CA; not eligible for remote work Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, life and AD&D, supplemental coverage, employee product discount, 401(k) with Company match, and paid time off Recruitment Process: Applications will be reviewed as they are received, and interviews may begin before the posting closes. NaturVet reserves the right to fill the position and close the posting at any time. No unsolicited agency or recruiter submissions, please. This job posting is intended to provide a general overview of the role and is not a comprehensive or exhaustive description of all duties, responsibilities, qualifications, or working conditions, including physical demands and work environment. A complete job description is available upon request. Please contact hr@naturvet.com if you would like additional information about the position.

description: Company Overview Sarmal, Inc. is a San Diego–based biotechnology company developing next-generation genomics and molecular detection platforms. You will be the single point of contact between our scientific and operations teams and the vendors who supply them — sourcing quotes, negotiating terms, placing orders, and making sure reagents, consumables, and equipment arrive on time and in good condition. Track open orders and expedite backorders, allocations, and delayed shipments before they become bench-level problems. Serve as day-to-day point of contact for supplier representatives; coordinate vendor visits and product demonstrations. Monitor supplier performance on quality, delivery, and responsiveness; escalate recurring issues and identify second-source options for critical materials. Receiving & Inventory Receive all incoming shipments: verify contents against packing slips and purchase orders, inspect for damage, and record lot numbers and expiration dates. Route temperature-sensitive materials immediately on arrival — cold-chain reagents, dry ice shipments, and controlled-storage items — to the correct storage location. Maintain stockroom and consumables inventory; conduct cycle counts, monitor par levels, and anticipate demand against upcoming study timelines so that long-lead items are ordered ahead of need. Sound negotiation skills and the ability to be persistent with suppliers while maintaining tact and preserving the relationship. Strong proficiency with Excel and comfort learning new purchasing, inventory, or ERP systems. Excellent organization and attention to detail, with the ability to manage many concurrent orders and competing priorities. Ability to work on-site five days per week. Familiarity with cold-chain handling, dry ice, and temperature-controlled storage requirements. Hands-on experience with an ERP, inventory, or e-procurement platform (e.g., NetSuite, QuickBooks, Quartzy, Coupa). Exposure to a regulated quality environment and supplier qualification practices. Experience with capital equipment procurement, service contracts, or facilities vendor coordination. description: Welcome to Backburner Labs Backburner Labs is an engineering consultancy in St. Paul that designs and builds products our clients can't build alone: medical devices, industrial systems, robotics, things that often don't exist until we make them. That's the engineering side. None of it works without the business behind it. We've doubled revenue every year for five years and are preparing to move into a new headquarters to match. Growth like that doesn't happen without finance, operations, logistics, and salespeople who are just as sharp and just as accountable as the engineers down the hall. We're still small enough that your work is visible, not buried in a process nobody remembers building. You'll help create the systems this company runs on as it scales, not just maintain ones someone else already figured out. If you'd rather build something than babysit it, you'll fit in here. Help build the company that's building what's next. Quick Facts Founded: 2019 Company: ~50 people (full-time and contract employees) Current location: St. Paul - St. Anthony Park area Future location: Minneapolis - Prospect Park area (we have leased a 43,000 sq ft building) Revenue: doubled every year for 5 years (more details shared later) Client retention: 93% Position Overview Backburner Labs is an engineering consultancy and contract manufacturer that designs and builds products our clients can’t build alone: medical devices, industrial systems, robotics, and things that often don’t exist until we make them. That work depends on getting the right parts, from the right suppliers, at the right price, on time. We’re looking for a hands-on Buyer to own purchasing and improve how it works as we grow. Request and compare quotes on price, availability, lead time, and freight; negotiate terms and identify second sources. Source parts from China and other international suppliers, accounting for quality requirements, shipping, tariffs, and total delivered cost. Own supplier accounts and relationships, including setup, payment terms, supplier records, and tax-exemption documentation. Convert BOMs and build plans into purchase plans; flag long-lead, single-source, and end-of-life parts early. Purchase Tracking & Follow-Through Create and manage purchase orders from request through delivery; confirm acknowledgements and expedite as needed. Maintain a clear view of open orders, expected arrival dates, costs, and project assignments. Resolve delays, backorders, incorrect shipments, and returns (RMAs) before they disrupt a build, balancing fast-turn prototype buys against planned production orders. Process Improvement & Financial Coordination Build a consistent purchasing intake process: required specifications, quantities, need dates, project codes, and approvals. Work with our CFO on payment terms, invoice discrepancies, and project cost tracking. Improve purchasing workflows and records in our ERP/MRP system (Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central), using Arena PLM for BOM and item information. Inventory Management Own manufacturing inventory accuracy: on-hand balances, stock locations, and ERP transactions. Receive material against purchase orders and packing slips, verifying part number, quantity, and condition. Run cycle counts, maintain reorder points and lot/serial traceability, and support kitting and material readiness for builds. Shipping & Logistics (Secondary) Coordinate parcel (FedEx, UPS) and LTL shipments, labels, BOLs, supplier returns, and freight claims. Qualifications Required 2+ years of hands-on purchasing supporting engineering, manufacturing, or hardware products, including personally requesting quotes, issuing POs, and following them through delivery. Hands-on inventory experience: receiving, cycle counts, and reconciling ERP records to physical stock. Comfort with technical part information, clear communication, and the ability to keep many orders moving without losing details. Working with finance on approvals, payment terms, invoices, and cost tracking, and improving a purchasing process in a growing organization. We serve industry leaders across transportation, energy, medical, and defense, offering tariff-free production, open capacity, and rapid ramp-up. With in-house R&D and engineering, we help customers strengthen supply chains and build confidently in America. SUMMARY OF POSITION Under the direction of the Purchasing Director, the Buyer is responsible for contacting suppliers to procure all purchases, ensuring on-time deliveries, and supporting/mediating the resolution of any supplier-related concerns or issues. Responsible for the flow of communication cross-functionally. JOB DUTIES & ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Issue Purchase Orders and follow up with suppliers until the material is received in the system – including MRO. Coordinate material pickups from our suppliers. Request and maintain required paperwork from suppliers of raw materials and MRO (such as invoices, TDS, MSDS, COA, packing lists, and certificates) Communicate with suppliers to ensure that specified delivery dates are met on purchase orders issued by Purchasing or Supply Chain. If the supplier is unable to meet the specified delivery date, issue a Change Order showing the new agreed-upon delivery date and promptly advise the departments involved (i.e., Production Planning, Materials Management, Production, etc.). Monitors and evaluates supplier performance. Advises appropriate personnel of an impending supplier failure to fulfill contractual obligations, which may delay production or delivery. Resolves shipment quality discrepancies by mediating supplier/manufacturing issues. Facilitates inspections, substitutions, and standardization by arranging and participating in conferences between suppliers and company personnel. Negotiates and settles damage claims, rejections, losses, return of materials, over-shipments, cancellations, and engineering changes with suppliers. Prepares moderately complex reports by collecting, analyzing, and summarizing information and trends. Provides parts, equipment, and materials information by answering questions and requests. Applies continuous improvement techniques and methods to internal processes and systems to increase efficiency and customer service and to reduce costs. Understand the Automated Procurement System and its relationship to the various interfacing systems. Maintain purchasing databases to ensure dependent departments have prompt and accurate information. Use generated reports and screens for control and manufacturing decisions. Review the various databases of the Automated Procurement System daily for reschedules and cancellations and take appropriate actions urgently. Assist Production Planning in reviewing purchased parts shortages to determine if sufficient quantities are available and or in transit to allow a manufacturing schedule change if and when required. Process all Accounting tasks for price and quantity discrepancies. Post daily acknowledgements to purchase orders. Follow up on un-acknowledged orders and confirm with vendors. Review rejected material and complete disposition with corrective action. Review metrics for validity and provide daily maintenance to ensure accuracy. Determines proper quantities of materials (resins, inserts, packaging etc.) and establishes deliveries to meet the production schedule, using MRP, machine run time, and knowledge of other relevant facts. Monitor the forecast for the raw materials, including packaging. Keeps Schedulers apprised of material availability problems through daily contact and attending production scheduling meetings. Participation in these meetings should also be to find out the needs of materials and services from the Production team. Establishes and monitors inventory processes, including Kanbans, VMI, Pull/Lean and Consignment programs with vendors. Monitors inventory value and continually works to reduce levels without interrupting service to the plant. Maintains reasonable level of inventories, economical to supply parameters and production schedules. Follow the Purchasing department's increase process as is required. Participates in all functions of Physical Inventory. Contributes to the development & implementation of planning & acquisition processes as well as purchasing reqs, purchases, & procedures. Works closely with appropriate teams in the development and engagement of sourcing strategies. Knows and contributes to the objectives and goals of the Supply Chain group. Create scorecards to monitor performance. Presents and elaborates on the month PPV report and clarifies any questions. Help with audits such as IATF and ISO. This list of duties and responsibilities is not all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other duties and responsibilities, as management may deem necessary from time to time. QUALIFICATIONS (KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES): Minimum education requirement is a Bachelor’s Degree in Business, Supply Chain, or related coursework from 4-year college or university with at least 3 years of related experience (i.e., purchasing, customer service, or production scheduling). May instead have an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience; additional experience may be substituted for education. APICS certification strongly preferred. Must work fairly independently receiving a minimum of detailed supervision and guidance. Data entry experience. Able to work in a fast-paced and at time stressed environment. Intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Office products required – ie. Outlook, Excel, Word. Knowledge of the materials purchased, programs, and procedures that are related to the work of the purchasing department. Must be dependable and have an excellent attendance record. Detail-oriented accuracy in work and good follow-up skills. Effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to customers, clients, and other employees and management of the organization. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, at all levels, both internally and externally. Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists.

description: Schaeffler is a dynamic global technology company and its success has been a result of its entrepreneurial spirit and long history of private ownership. Your Key Responsibilities Support the preparation of market analyses and the implementation of category strategies for the plant. Develop and execute profitable purchasing strategies and negotiation approaches in close alignment with relevant functions and stakeholders. Monitor the supply market continuously and manage the supplier portfolio to ensure quality, cost efficiency, on-time delivery, sustainability, and compliance with contractual and legal requirements. Negotiate prices and conditions in line with internal purchasing guidelines and contractual requirements, and manage supplier contracts professionally. Coordinate the assigned suppliers, including purchase price planning and the definition and tracking of saving initiatives that support plant performance. Wellness initiatives: Employees have access to wellness programs and resources aimed at promoting physical, mental, and emotional health, fostering a supportive and thriving work environment. See all of our benefits at: Schaeffler Benefits As a global company with employees around the world, it is important to us that we treat each other with respect and value all ideas and perspectives. By appreciating our differences, we inspire creativity and drive innovation. In this way, we contribute to sustainable value creation for our stakeholders and society as a whole. Together, we advance how the world moves. Exciting assignments and outstanding development opportunities await you because we impact the future with innovation. We look forward to your application. https://www.schaeffler.us/careers/ Your contact Schaeffler Group USA Inc. Jason Gould Schaeffler is an equal employment opportunity / affirmative action employer. All qualified candidates will receive equal employment opportunities and consideration for employment without regard to unlawful consideration of race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law. description: Salary Is Based On Experience, Skills, And Education This position is 100% onsite The Marvin Group is a Strategic Partner for Global Alternate Mission Equipment and Sustainment The Marvin Group, a leading defense contractor, plays a crucial role in the development and manufacturing of various systems for military aerospace and vehicles. Based in Southern California near the Los Angeles International Airport, The Marvin Group consists of Marvin Engineering (MEC), Marvin Test Solutions (MTS) and Marvin Land Systems (MLS). Marvin Engineering designs and produces military Alternate Mission Equipment. Marvin Test Solutions designs and manufactures armament Test Equipment. Marvin Land Systems specializes in the design and build of power and thermal management systems. For over 60 years we have maintained “A Tradition of Excellence”, serving as a trusted source for our unwavering commitment to supporting all branches of the Department of Defense and our global allies. Our collaboration extends across a diverse array of programs and platforms, including major military prime contractors such as Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, and Raytheon. Position Summary Buyer IV supports Indirect Procurement and is responsible for purchases that support day-to-day operations (instead of direct material purchases for production). Indirect Procurement means the purchase of software licenses, IT infrastructure, travel, construction, leases, a wide variety of services (temps, maintenance, landscaping, cafeteria, company benefits, etc.) and capital equipment (usually large machining or quality measurement equipment but could include things like forklifts or other vehicles). These are things we need to buy that do not go into the products we manufacture. This role ensures these “indirect” items are procured efficiently, cost-effectively, and in compliance with organizational and regulatory standards. Robust negotiation, independent problem-solving, the ability to work through ambiguity to develop solutions, and clear and concise communication are all critical for this role. Marvin Engineering is growing, and our indirect procurement team needs to develop processes and expertise in all of the areas described above. The successful candidate will already have robust experience in most, if not all, of these areas. We want to leverage this experience to enable fast expansion while utilizing best practices in the industry. Essential Duties And Responsibilities Review Purchase Requests (PRs), source qualified vendors, collaborate with cross-functional customers, ensure competitive bidding, conduct analysis, ensure compliance, and negotiate best value. Develop new processes and procedures, and recommend tools and resources, for new indirect procurement activities to come under the control of the indirect procurement department. Draft and ensure approvals of purchase orders. Ensure appropriate review and negotiate contracts for indirect procurement. Track and ensure on-time delivery, completion of milestones, or activation of software. Ensure appropriate levels of support to cross-functional customers. Manage relationships and resolve disputes with vendors. Skills And Requirements Minimum of 5 years prior experience as a buyer or similar purchasing capacity, OR an AA/AS degree or higher with 2 years of experience in either a purchasing or sales capacity where negotiation was required. Strong ability to work independently to solve complex problems. Robust negotiations skills with a history of success. Purchasing experience in 3 or more of the following areas: (A) Corporate travel expenses (Hotel, airline, car rental, group events with more than 100 people, especially using third party travel services or software); (B) Software licenses, IT infrastructure or computer hardware, (C) Facilities expenses (Landscaping services, tree-trimming, on-site cafeterias, food service, or vending machines, uniform services, third party bathroom supplies, cleaning services); (D) Capital Equipment (Large machinery (especially CNC Mills and lathes), quality measurement equipment, forklifts, and other vehicles; and (E) Temp services and HR Benefits; (F) Construction and leases; OR (G) Other indirect purchases valued at greater than $50,000. Ability to analyze spending, identify trends, and create cost-saving recommendations Strong experience with Excel or another tool for data analysis. Strong experience with PowerPoint Excellent communication skills in English, both written and verbal. Experience using purchasing software. Note that SAP experience is a plus, but not required Self-starter and capable of working independently to resolve issues or concisely recommend robust plans of action for leadership. Collaborative with cross-functional customers Sound business decisions and common sense. Ability to work well under pressure and meet deadlines. Ability to communicate with General Contractors. Oversee the PO/project progress and payment process of contractor. Must be able to lift up to 35 lbs Work Environment On-site, Inglewood, California Medium-to-large, fast-paced office environment Noise level is typically moderate Occasional exposure to onsite construction or facility environments Compensation Range Salary Range (Inglewood only): $71,304 - $110,000 annually. Salary is based on skills, experience, and education. Travel Requirements May include minimal local domestic travel of <5% NOTES: This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by this position's employee(s). Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and perform any other job-related duties requested by anyone authorized to give instructions or assignments. The requirements listed in this document are the minimum levels of knowledge, skills, or abilities. This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an at-will relationship. This position must meet export control compliance requirements. All applicants must be “U.S. persons” within the meaning of ITAR, as defined: a U.S. Citizen, a lawful permanent resident, political asylee, or refugee. Interested parties please apply online and submit resume to https://jobs.marvingroup.com/ Visit us at https://http://marvingroup.com/ The Marvin Group is an EEO/Disability/Vets Employer. description: If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact. With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses (https://www.idexcorp.com/our-businesses/business-segments/) around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you. Position Summary The Buyer is responsible for sourcing, negotiating, and purchasing materials, goods, and services to meet the company's operational requirements. This position monitors supplier performance, delivery commitments, and material availability while working directly with suppliers to resolve delivery, quality, and service-related issues. The Buyer manages supplier relationships and helps ensure suppliers meet established performance expectations related to quality, delivery, cost, and responsiveness. In addition to external suppliers, this position collaborates closely with internal stakeholders including Sourcing, Planning, Engineering, Quality, Operations, Customer Service, and Product Management to support business objectives, improve material availability, and maintain continuity of supply. This critical role requires a strong sense of urgency, excellent communication skills, sound analytical abilities, and the desire to make a measurable and immediate impact on the business. This is a regular, full-time, on-site position located at HURST in Shelby, NC. Duties And Responsibilities Manage procurement activities, including issuing purchase orders, expediting orders, resolving discrepancies, and maintaining supplier commitments. Evaluate and analyze buy signals generated by the Material Requirements Planning (MRP) system; experience with JD Edwards (JDE) is preferred. Collaborate with Planning to support material availability and adjustments in production planning to meet business demands. Actively manage supplier lead times, expedite critical shortages, and support inventory optimization initiatives through effective execution of MRP recommendations. Understand procurement policies and procedures and execute job duties in alignment with those requirements. Recommend improvements that enhance operational effectiveness and efficiency. Collaborate with internal departments to understand purchasing requirements, resolve supply challenges, and improve material availability. Analyze supplier performance using quality, delivery, cost, inventory, and risk metrics to support a reliable and sustainable supply chain. Make timely, data-driven recommendations to improve supplier performance and support business objectives. Coordinate supplier quality, delivery, and nonconformance issues with internal teams and suppliers in a timely manner to minimize business disruption. Authorize payment of invoices or return of merchandise, as appropriate. Interface with vendors and build strong working relationships to maintain a high level of support throughout all aspects of the procurement process. Support sourcing, inventory management, and continuous improvement initiatives as assigned. Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor. Knowledge, Skills And Required Abilities Understanding of supply chain processes, including procurement, logistics, planning, and inventory management. Proficiency with procurement software, ERP systems, and reporting tools; experience with JD Edwards (JDE) is preferred. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to use data to support decision-making. Excellent verbal and written communication skills to effectively interact with suppliers and internal stakeholders. Ability to resolve supply chain issues and help ensure timely delivery of materials. Ability to engage and collaborate effectively with all levels of the organization. Strong attention to detail to ensure accuracy in orders, data, and compliance with specifications. Desire to learn, understand business processes, and recommend improvements where appropriate. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Education And Experience Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience, with emphasis in Business Administration, Economics, Production, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Operations Management, and/or Engineering. Two to four (2-4) years of progressively responsible purchasing and materials control experience in a manufacturing environment. Experience working with international suppliers / supply chains. PHYSICAL DEMANDS The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to sit, stand, and walk. The employee may occasionally be required to climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must be able to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds, or over 50 pounds with assistance. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus when reading printed materials and computer screens. description: A Snapshot of Your Day A typical day will include interfacing (via email, Teams, face to face) with your procurement team and other project team members from engineering, project management, supplier quality, logistics as well as with your suppliers to ensure well-managed, organized tendering and execution of projects. Using your experience in purchasing processes and supplier relationships to develop commercial expertise for your commodity and supplier network. How You’ll Make An Impact Manage all purchasing responsibilities for a defined group of commodities. Perform and execute complex buying strategies to purchase and deliver equipment and materials on time and under budget. Review and analyze requisitions and supply plans for domestic and international purchases. Participate in the negotiation of prices, terms and conditions, and quality requirements. Expedite as needed and serves as liaison between supplier and users (engineers, project managers, supplier quality & others as needed) Use problem solving skills to resolve delivery, quality, invoicing, and pricing issues Evaluate market conditions to develop risk mitigation measures for commodities. Lead initiatives for your commodities to find and develop new suppliers based on risk and capacity data. Solicit cost reduction ideas from suppliers and initiate follow-up action to implement these savings for the company. What You Bring Bachelor’s degree in related discipline and minimum 5 years of successful experience in purchasing. Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite. Ability to apply knowledge of field of specialization to the successful completion of complex assignments. Identify and resolve complex problems and issues. Ability to work independently and in a team atmosphere, using an organized and disciplined approach. Comfortable working in an international environment and willing to travel internationally. Ability to travel 10% of time both domestically and internationally. Applicants must be legally authorized for employment in the United States without need for current or future employer-sponsored work authorization. Siemens Energy employees with current visa sponsorship may be eligible for internal transfers. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, steam turbines and generators. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation. Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation. description: Job Title: Buyer Job Description We are seeking a Buyer to manage the procurement of materials used in the production of industrial machinery and related products. The individual will be responsible for processing and maintaining purchase orders, responding to MRP requirements, coordinating material deliveries, managing supplier communication, and helping to prevent production delays. The role involves working closely with suppliers and internal departments to support pricing, quality, inventory, and on-time delivery objectives. Responsibilities Process purchase orders and ensure accuracy regarding quantity, pricing, specifications, and delivery requirements. Review and respond to MRP messages to maintain a consistent flow of materials and support cost-reduction, quality, and supplier-delivery initiatives. Negotiate pricing, contracts, and business terms with new and existing suppliers. Update purchase orders with supplier-confirmed delivery dates and quantities. Coordinate incoming material deliveries to support on-time production and delivery. Monitor backordered materials and assign appropriate ship dates. Work with suppliers to expedite orders and resolve late-delivery issues. Contact vendors regularly to confirm that materials will arrive as needed. Notify the appropriate internal departments when material delays occur. Assist with analyzing supply-chain issues, work in progress, and potential production setbacks. Recommend solutions to help ensure customer and production delivery requirements are met. Participate in reviewing and adjusting inventory and planning parameters, including safety stock and lead times. Work extensively within the companys ERP system. Perform additional duties as assigned. Essential Skills 2+ years of buying or planning experience with a bachelor's degree in a supply-chain-related field, or at least three years of related experience. Working knowledge of MRP systems and functionality. Understanding of bill of materials structure. Understanding of material management and inventory flow. Experience processing and maintaining purchase orders. Experience communicating with suppliers regarding pricing, quantities, lead times, and delivery dates. Additional Skills & Qualifications Bachelors degree in supply chain or a related field with at least two years of buying or planning experience, or at least three years of relevant experience. Working knowledge of MRP systems. Understanding of bills of material and material management. Previous purchase-order and supplier-management experience. Strong communication and organizational skills. Ability to work effectively with suppliers and cross-functional internal teams. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications. Job Type & Location This is a Permanent position based out of Tecumseh, MI. Pay And Benefits The pay range for this position is $60000.00 - $67000.00/yr. Individual compensation offered for this position within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, geographic location, internal equity, and other pertinent job-related factors. full benefits, med, vision and dental. Workplace Type This is a fully onsite position in Tecumseh,MI. Application Deadline This position is anticipated to close on Oct 22, 2026. description: ARE YOU A CURRENT US FOODS EMPLOYEE? PLEASE APPLY DIRECTLY THROUGH OUR INTERNAL WORKDAY CAREER SITE Join Our Community of Food People! The Sr Produce Buyer will utilize their category expertise and vendor specific knowledge to manage inventory levels for all assigned items, suppliers and/or categories while maintaining service level and spoilage targets to our customers across multiple distribution centers. Responsible for delivering forecast accuracy and forecasting per defined goals by SKU and/or product family. Collaborate with Logistics Operations, Produce Category Management, markets and Suppliers to understand USF optimized supply chain opportunities. This role will be onsite 2 days a month. Candidates will need to reside within one of the 3 areas: Lenexa, Kansas, Grand Island, NE or Omaha, Nebraska. Job Responsibilities Delivers on KPIs for desk specific goals such as: Service Level, Days-Inventory-On-Hand (DIOH), spoilage and freight income. Proactively reviews projected out of stock report daily to ensure we deliver on customer order fulfillment. Analyzes economic order quantities, forecasts, lead times, vendor set-up, safety stock, etc., in-order to create efficient purchase orders with our suppliers. Communicates closely with our cross-functional partners to capture seasonal trends and events in the business as well as drive profitability with accurate costs. Partners appropriately with product/category management team to maintain supplier relationships and proper accountability. Cooperates with the logistics team to identify and achieve freight consolidation to maximize net income. Point person for all third party logistic managed loads. Evaluates inbound volume and purchase history to collaborate with warehouse operations on efficient receiving practices. Executes forward-buy opportunities to achieve profitability for period or year-end based on targeted goals. Confirm all purchase orders accurately using vendor confirmation as well verifying this cost using the loaded vendor price list. Clear any costing discrepancies between the received PO’s and the vendor invoice, through the Buyer Match Pay process by 8 pm each Wednesday. Work with vendors to reconcile any discrepancies. Achieve PO Cost Accuracy % on the Buyer KPI scorecard Review all daily cost exception reports and take appropriate action to insure all costing data is accurate and up to date, including: Review Last Cost Reasonableness report and resolve any issues Last Invoice Cost to Total Market Cost variances Weekly review of the Last Invoice Cost Book report and resolve issues Inventory revaluation report including auditing any inventory gains Set-up new item cost attributes to reflect accurate inbound cost Review PO timing to identify and mitigate impact of LPM / LPW costs Review PO freight costs for appropriateness and address issues with the appropriate stakeholder (ie, incorrect freight on PO, freight rate issues. Maintain up-to-date and accurate freight information and maintain control of the freight rate process utilizing the Network Strategy Rate Maintenance team and produce replenishment. Obtain current transportation market data to update rate information based on industry trends or cost increases. Proactively ensure the accurate development of demand data based upon forecast, current inventory targets, replenishment lead-time and master data settings. Interpret and report forecast implications of phasing-in/out of items. Full ownership of forecasting of your desk. Related Experience/Requirements: Minimum 4 years of purchasing, and/or related work in the procurement or logistics field, produce experience preferred. Prior experience working in a large fast paced foodservice purchasing and/or logistics environment strongly desired Knowledge/Skills/Abilities: Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills, excellent analytical skills, demonstrate a keen attention to detail, strong interpersonal skills, be able to communicate with vendors and across cross-functional. Knowledge of freight concepts and vendor pricing preferred. Must be able to manage successful relationships with product and transportation providers/suppliers. Proficiency required in the use of Microsoft Office especially Microsoft Word and Excel, as well as Microsoft Outlook. PRISM and E3/AWR experience preferred This role will also receive annual incentive plan bonus . Benefits for this role may include health insurance, pre-tax spending accounts, retirement benefits, paid time off, short-term and long-term disability, employee stock purchase plan, and life insurance. description: We are seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Manufacturing Buyer to manage the procurement of raw materials, components, and industrial supplies necessary to support our production operations. In this role, you will balance daily transactional purchasing with tactical vendor management. Your primary focus will be to ensure a reliable flow of high-quality materials to the factory floor while optimizing inventory levels, reducing lead times, and controlling overall procurement costs. Responsibilities Execute purchase orders (POs) based on Material Requirements Planning (MRP) system prompts (messages), production schedules, customer forecasts, and inventory targets. Expedite open orders and proactively resolve delivery delays, material shortages, or shipping discrepancies to avoid production downtime. Review and resolve discrepancies regarding material pricing, quantities received, and supplier invoice payments. Serve as the primary point of contact for routine supplier communication, order inquiries, and problem resolution. Monitor vendor performance metrics, focusing closely on on-time delivery (OTCS), product quality, and cost competitiveness. Partner with Quality Assurance to manage non-conforming materials (RMA process) and ensure suppliers implement effective corrective actions. Maintain accurate inventory parameters within the ERP system, including safety stock levels if needed, multiple order quantities, and supplier lead times. Collaborate with production planners and warehouse teams to monitor inventory turnover and minimize excess or obsolete stock. Solicit and analyze competitive quotes (RFQs) from existing and alternative suppliers to secure best-market pricing. Find and assist in implementing cost reduction opportunities. Qualifications Experience: 3 to 5+ years of buying or purchasing experience strictly within a manufacturing or industrial environment. Education: Bachelor’s degree in business, Supply Chain Management, Logistics, or a related field (equivalent hands-on experience will be considered). Certifications: Progress toward or completion of APICS (CPIM/CSCP) or ISM (CPSM) certification is a plus. ERP Experience: Solid proficiency working within manufacturing ERP/MRP systems (JDE a plus) Problem-Solving Agility: Proven capability to handle fast-paced changes, sudden production schedule shifts, and logistics bottlenecks. Effective Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills Organization: Highly organized with the ability to manage hundreds of active line items and open purchase orders simultaneously.

description: Procurement Specialist Location: Colwich, KS – Wichita Area | Onsite Compensation: $75,000–$95,000 base, depending on experience Relocation Assistance: Available Want to Get In on the Ground Floor? There are purchasing jobs where you inherit someone else’s processes, suppliers and “this is how we’ve always done it” playbook. This isn’t one of them. We’re hiring three Procurement Specialists to help build out a new procurement function within a growing engineering and technology organization supporting complex industrial projects across the country. You’ll still do the things great procurement professionals do — source suppliers, negotiate, manage POs, solve problems and keep materials moving. But here, you’ll also have a chance to help shape how procurement gets done. You’ll work alongside engineering, project management and operations, supporting real projects where the equipment and materials you source eventually become part of something much bigger than a spreadsheet or purchase order. If you like procurement, enjoy solving the occasional “we need WHAT, by WHEN?” problem, and want more ownership than simply pushing POs through a system, keep reading. description: Job Description Why Join Altec? COMMODITY MANAGER – MARKET PRICING & COMMODITY INTELLIGENCE Supply Chain | St. Joseph, Missouri About Altec Altec is a leading provider of products and services for the electric utility, telecommunications, tree care, lights and signs, and contractor markets. For nearly a century, Altec has been committed to helping customers safely and reliably build and maintain critical infrastructure. At Altec, our values guide everything we do: Customer First Enjoyment of Work Family Financial Stability Integrity People Are Our Greatest Strength Quality Spiritual Development Teamwork We offer a collaborative environment where associates are empowered to innovate, solve complex challenges, and make meaningful contributions to our customers and communities. About The Opportunity Altec is seeking a Commodity Manager focused on market pricing, commodity intelligence, and strategic analysis. This role serves as a key resource for understanding commodity trends, forecasting cost impacts, and supporting sourcing decisions across multiple categories. While market pricing and commodity intelligence are the primary focus of this position, the Commodity Manager may also support specific commodity categories or other sourcing priorities. Category assignments and areas of responsibility may be adjusted over time based on business needs, organizational structure, workload, and staffing. The successful candidate will partner closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Materials, and Quality teams across the organization to support both current production and future business growth. What You'll Do As the Commodity Manager for Market Pricing & Commodity Intelligence, you will: Monitor commodity markets, pricing indices, economic indicators, capacity, lead times, and supply-demand trends across multiple categories. Develop cost models, forecasts, dashboards, and scenario analyses to support sourcing and business decisions. Translate market data into actionable recommendations for Procurement, Finance, Manufacturing, Engineering, and leadership teams. Analyze commodity exposure, inflationary and deflationary drivers, and supply chain risks; identify mitigation opportunities. Establish consistent data sources, methodologies, and reporting standards for commodity intelligence. Track supplier and market cost drivers and evaluate the reasonableness of pricing changes. Support commodity managers with negotiation preparation, sourcing strategies, timing decisions, and long-range planning. Deliver recurring and ad hoc reports that clearly communicate trends, risks, opportunities, and expected financial impact. Maintain awareness of regulatory, geopolitical, logistics, energy, and technology developments that may affect commodity markets. Coach and support purchasing and materials team members in the use of market intelligence, cost modeling, and forecasting tools. What We're Looking For Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree. Six years of applicable experience in procurement, supply chain, finance, economics, business analytics, manufacturing, engineering, or a related field. Demonstrated experience analyzing market, pricing, cost, or supply chain data. Excellent analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills. Ability to translate complex data into clear, actionable business recommendations. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including advanced Excel capabilities. Knowledge of economics, finance, procurement analytics, strategic sourcing, and manufacturing cost structures. Experience using market indices, economic indicators, dashboards, or business-intelligence tools. Experience identifying cost drivers, quantifying risk, and evaluating supplier pricing changes. Experience in a manufacturing or engineered-products environment. Experience translating complex market and financial data into clear recommendations for cross-functional and leadership audiences. MBA, APICS certification, or equivalent professional certification. What Success Looks Like Successful candidates will demonstrate: A strong record of producing reliable market analysis, forecasts, and cost insights. The ability to identify emerging risks and opportunities and recommend practical actions. Skill in influencing cross-functional stakeholders through clear, evidence-based recommendations. Strong analytical judgment, attention to detail, and disciplined use of data. The ability to communicate complex information clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences. A commitment to accuracy, continuous improvement, and informed decision-making. WHY ALTEC At Altec, you'll have the opportunity to influence critical business decisions, partner with industry-leading suppliers, and help drive operational excellence across a world-class manufacturing organization. You'll join a collaborative culture that values innovation, integrity, customer service, and continuous improvement. Join us and help build the supply chain that powers the products our customers depend on every day. description: Our values start with our people, join a team that values you! Bring your talents to Ross, our leading off-price retail chain with over 2,200 stores, and a strong track record of success and growth. Our focus has always been bringing our customers a constant stream of high-quality brands and on-trend merchandise at extraordinary savings. All while providing a fun and exciting treasure hunt experience. As Part Of Our Team, You Will Experience Success. Our winning team pursues excellence while learning and evolving Career growth. We develop industry leading talent because Ross grows when our people grow Teamwork. We work together to solve the hard problems and find the right solution Our commitment to Diversity, Equality & Inclusion, and our community. We celebrate the backgrounds, identities, and ideas of those who work and shop with us because our differences make us stronger. We strive to be a positive force in our community. Our Corporate headquarters are in Dublin, CA, we have 3 buying offices in key markets in New York City, Los Angeles, and Boston, and 8 distribution centers nationwide. With 2025 revenues of $22.8 billion, we are a Fortune 500 company who is committed to providing an inclusive work environment with continuous learning opportunities and development for our teams. About This Opportunity... The Assistant Buyer is a learning role that allows you to build a foundation of skills for your future career as a merchant. As an ABI, we invest in you through structured training and one on one apprenticeship with a skilled Buyer. You will begin to build your product knowledge, operational expertise, concepts of off-price retail, personal leadership skills and understand the customer! What You Will Do And What You Will Learn... Perform support activities for the buying team, such as purchase order management and processing markdowns, while building foundational merchant skills and learning the keys to becoming a successful merchant. Provide basic analysis of key business data to the Buyer, including the use of retail math to understand the business, monitoring of regional merchandise reports, Open-To-Buy, stock analysis and other ad hoc analysis to project sales and inventory levels. Learn the elements of negotiation and how we build relationships with our vendors. Develop effective relationships with vendors by participating in in person meetings. This includes following up on shipments and resolving problems to ensure product is delivered and processed as directed by the Buyer. Begin to effectively utilize and understand the merchandising systems and warehouse process. Provide operational support by serving as the key interface between the merchant team and warehouse operations, coordinating and scheduling daily merchandise deliveries to optimize warehouse processing capacity and efficiency. Develop and demonstrate foundational product knowledge through in person shopping at Ross Stores and at the competition. Utilize product knowledge to communicate to the Buyer new resources. Track planned receipt flow on a consistent basis. Display awareness of when merchandise is being received and make call outs to Buyer. Support Buyers in preparation of key business meetings (i.e. vendor appointments, style-outs, assortment planning) including formatting of reports. What You Need To Be Successful... Strong communication skills: You can "read the situation" you actively listen, ask clarifying questions, and demonstrate the ability to build relationships. Flexibility: You can pivot, are adaptable, and receptive to feedback. Results Driven: You are tenacious, and achievement focused. You can prioritize your work and deliver it with accuracy. Intellectually curious: You can analyze and draw conclusions, are a critical thinker, and see the big picture. Resilient: You are persistent and persuasive. You stay focused on your goals and finding creative solutions to problems. Enthusiasm for the product and retail business. Product is the center of what we do.... you must have an enthusiasm for the retail business and the product. Analytical Mindset: Helping to run a business depends on analysis and retail math. Bachelor's Degree required. Perks And Benefits Of Joining Our Team... Our Associates are at the heart of everything we do and we're proud to offer a range of benefits that reflect how much we value their contributions. Here's a peek into what you can expect as an eligible Ross Associate: A broad range of affordable health insurance options & personal medical plan concierge 401(k) with employer match and Life insurance Ample PTO including accrued vacation, paid holidays, diversity day, summer Fridays and the ability to purchase additional vacation. Employee stock purchase plan* Access to health and wellness benefits such as BetterHelp and Headspace Charitable donations matched by Ross Stores Foundation And more.... benefits vary by level and position and are subject to change DISCLAIMER This job description is a summary of the primary duties and responsibilities of the job and position. It is not intended to be a comprehensive or all-inclusive listing of duties and responsibilities. Contents are subject to change at management’s discretion. Ross is an equal employment opportunity employer. We consider individuals for employment or promotion according to their skills, abilities and experience. We believe that it is an essential part of the Company’s overall commitment to attract, hire and develop a strong, talented and diverse workforce. Ross is committed to complying with all applicable laws prohibiting discrimination based on race, color, religious creed, age, national origin, ancestry, physical, mental or developmental disability, sex (which includes pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding and medical conditions related to pregnancy, childbirth or breastfeeding), veteran status, military status, marital or registered domestic partnership status, medical condition (including cancer or genetic characteristics), genetic information, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, as well as any other category protected by federal, state or local laws. The base pay range for this role $33.65 to $36.06. The base pay range is dependent on factors including, but not limited to, experience, skills, qualifications, relevant education, certifications, seniority, and location. The range listed is just one component of the total compensation package for employees. Other rewards vary by position and location.

description: The Purchasing Coordinator provides administrative and transactional support across the Purchasing function and the teams it serves. This role supports construction, special projects, manufacturing, and other operational needs through accurate data entry, supplier follow-up, subcontract administration, reporting, order tracking, expediting, and document control. The position works within established processes and approvals, escalating pricing, scope, supplier, schedule, compliance, and contract exceptions to the appropriate Purchasing Specialist. The role does not independently select suppliers, negotiate terms, approve substitutions, make award decisions, or authorize commitments. Who We Are At ColonialWebb, we are deeply committed to our people, our culture, and the continued growth of our business. As a full-service MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing) contractor, we pride ourselves on the quality and expertise of our teams, who work across a diverse range of specialties, including New Construction, Mechanical Service, Industrial Refrigeration, and Manufacturing. For over 50 years, we've been dedicated to delivering comprehensive solutions and unmatched service to our commercial customers, earning a reputation as a trusted contractor in the industry. Perks Of Joining ColonialWebb Competitive salary of $50,000 - $55,000 Career development and progression 401(k) plan with company match PTO and paid holidays Excellent medical, dental, life, vision and disability benefits Employee Assistance Program Employee referral incentives A Day In The Life Provide subcontract administrative support by reviewing request packages for completeness, preparing documents from approved templates, coordinating vendor review, tracking status, and facilitating execution after required approvals; process authorized revisions and change orders; maintain required backup, naming, routing, and records; track insurance certificates, trade-specific attachments, and project flow-down requirements; and escalate missing or nonstandard items. Provide administrative and transactional Purchasing support for construction, special projects, manufacturing, third-party welding, and other operational needs. Review purchasing requests for required job, supplier, item, quantity, pricing, delivery, and supporting information; follow up on incomplete or inconsistent requests before entering approved purchase orders, releases, acknowledgements, and confirmations in designated systems. Enter usage orders and related supplier-order data for active-job pre-buy, lump-sum, and bulk purchase orders to keep material usage and pricing trackers accurate and current. Expedite supplier submittals requested by Purchasing Specialists; track receipt and approval status, follow up on outstanding documents, distribute submittals to designated contacts, and distinguish supplier-submitted documents from technically approved submittals. Organize and maintain purchasing project folders as jobs commence, ensuring quotes, purchase orders, acknowledgements, submittals, delivery records, correspondence, subcontract documents, and supporting records are promptly saved and properly named. Expedite orders by obtaining acknowledgements, promised ship dates, backorder status, shipment details, and delivery updates; document and follow up on responses; and escalate missed dates, shortages, substitutions, quantity or price changes, damaged shipments, and issues requiring purchasing judgment or supplier negotiation. Support urgent material needs by contacting approved suppliers and, when directed, approved alternates to identify availability, lead times, and delivery options when an awarded supplier cannot meet material or schedule requirements. Support manufacturing, third-party welding, and other one-off material needs by coordinating RFQ and availability requests, entering approved orders, tracking materials and supplier commitments, following up on deliveries, and communicating open-item status. Compile recurring national and departmental purchasing reports; validate and reconcile data, maintain supporting records, distribute approved reports, follow up on missing inputs, and escalate data-quality issues. Collect supplier information and required forms and route supplier setup, update, compliance, and approval requests. Assist with routine purchase-order and invoice research by locating records, confirming available information, and routing discrepancies to the appropriate owner. Maintain purchasing checklists, templates, work instructions, and shared reference files; identify opportunities to standardize and improve repeatable administrative processes. Provide general administrative support to Purchasing leadership and the department, including scheduling meetings, coordinating supplier meetings and departmental events, preparing meeting materials, managing calendars and communications, and completing other assigned administrative duties. Protect confidential supplier, project, pricing, contracts, and company information and follow established approval, retention, and access requirements. You Should Have High school diploma or equivalent required; associate degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain, Accounting, Construction Administration, or related field preferred. Two or more years of experience in an administrative, coordinator, document-control, project-support, customer-service, or operations-support role. Purchasing experience is not required; the ability to learn purchasing terminology, systems, and documented workflows is essential. Demonstrated ability to stay organized, manage multiple competing priorities, build productive working relationships with internal stakeholders and suppliers, and maintain accuracy, responsiveness, and consistent follow-through. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including concise status updates and professional follow-up. Proficiency with standard office, spreadsheet, reporting, and business systems. Ability to follow documented processes and approval paths and escalate exceptions. Preferred Experience supporting purchasing, contracts, construction administration, manufacturing, project coordination, accounts payable, logistics, or supplier-related workflows. Experience using enterprise purchasing, order-tracking, reporting, electronic document execution, or document management systems. Experience compiling recurring reports, maintaining logs, coordinating document reviews and signatures, expediting orders, or managing controlled documents. Familiarity with construction, mechanical contracting, industrial services, manufacturing, or project-based work environments.

description: About Our Companies Corfini Meat & Seafood is a family owned & operated West Coast-based distributor with locations in Seattle, Portland, San Francisco, Sacramento, Palm Springs, San Diego, and Salt Lake City. We supply local, sustainable, and natural meats—along with locally sourced game and specialty items—to top restaurants and retail markets throughout the western United States. Chef-driven and focused on quality, education, and responsible sourcing, our team is committed to being an unrivaled leader for all proteins, nose to tail. Calvada Food Sales operates alongside Corfini as our high-volume wholesale division, with distribution hubs in Sacramento and Reno. Calvada specializes in broad-scale distribution across a wide range of commercial channels, including retail supermarkets, independent butcher shops, regional foodservice operators, hospitality and gaming venues, Hispanic and Asian culinary businesses, and regional redistributors across Northern California and Nevada. Together, our combined USDA inspected operations offer a comprehensive protein platform ranging from artisan, local-farm sourcing to high-volume commercial supply. About the Role We are looking for a detail-oriented, eager-to-learn Junior Meat & Seafood Buyer to join our Greater Sacramento team supporting both Corfini Meat & Seafood and Calvada Food Sales. This is an entry-level position designed to give you a foundational, hands-on understanding of protein procurement, inventory management, and market pricing dynamics across both specialty culinary and broadline wholesale channels. Working directly alongside the Director of Purchasing, you will start by mastering core data entry, purchase order processing, and receiving logistics. Through direct mentorship, your responsibilities will steadily expand to include product age monitoring, creating push lists, evaluating market pricing, and eventually making autonomous purchasing decisions. Key Responsibilities Phase 1: Core Operations & PO Management Purchase Order Entry: Accurately input, track, and manage daily Purchase Orders (POs) across beef, pork, poultry, and seafood lines for both specialty and high-volume wholesale accounts using Aspen Canopy ERP software. Order Tracking & Logistics: Verify vendor confirmations, monitor delivery schedules into our Sacramento and Reno facilities, update purchasing records in Aspen Canopy, and resolve basic pricing or shipping discrepancies. Inventory & Product Age Control: Monitor daily inventory levels and stock aging within Aspen Canopy to safeguard freshness and maximize product rotation across high-turnover warehouse stock. Phase 2: Expanded Analytical & Operational Support Push Lists & Specials: Collaborate daily with the Director of Purchasing to create sales push lists, move lists, and promotional specials tailored across diverse foodservice, retail, and wholesale market sectors to optimize inventory turnover and minimize waste. Cross-Department Collaboration: Partner hand-in-hand with sales, warehouse staff, and receiving teams to align incoming inventory with daily customer demand. Market & Cost Review: Assist in reviewing vendor cost sheets, tracking USDA market trends, and analyzing product pricing, yield, and quality grades across diverse customer profiles. Growth Track: Category Leadership & Independent Procurement Progressively take on direct supplier communications, evaluate local and volume sourcing options, negotiate spot buys, and execute independent purchasing strategies for designated protein categories. Qualifications Industry Passion & Knowledge: Prior experience or a strong interest in food purchasing, procurement, or supply chain for protein—including a basic understanding of cuts, species, and quality grades. Background in food service, wholesale distribution, grocery, or culinary arts is a plus. Attention to Detail: High accuracy in maintaining purchasing records, verifying product specifications, and handling high-volume numerical data. Systems & Data Skills: Proficiency in Microsoft Windows environments, Excel, and general computer systems. Experience or familiarity with Aspen Canopy or similar inventory/ERP software is a strong plus. Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills to build solid relationships with suppliers, internal procurement teams, and sales reps. Adaptability & Work Environment: Strong organizational skills to manage tight daily deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Ability to work on-site in Greater Sacramento, including spending time in refrigerated warehouse environments when inspecting inventory. Education: High school diploma or equivalent required; additional education or coursework in business, supply chain, agriculture, or culinary fields is a plus. Meat and/or seafood buying experience is a plus What We Offer Direct, 1-on-1 mentorship from the Director of Purchasing in a stable, multi-faceted business environment. Clear internal progression from entry-level PO processing to an independent Buyer role. Competitive starting compensation and benefits package. Exposure to the entire spectrum of protein distribution—from specialty chef-driven items to high-volume commercial wholesale.

description: Procurement Buyer & Operations Specialist Solon, OH — Hybrid (Tuesday & Wednesday in-office required) The Procurement Buyer & Operations Specialist owns day-to-day transactional execution across the procure-to-pay (P2P) cycle for Tarkett North America's Procurement Shared Services team. Serve as the primary point of contact for buyer-side vendor and internal stakeholder inquiries — pricing, delivery, quality, and performance concerns. Process Awareness (expected of every procurement role) Proactively identify inefficiencies in the transactional workflow and propose — and where reasonable, implement — fixes. Familiarity with procurement compliance and spend basics. description: Job Description Job Title Assistant Buyer – Gifts About the Job Books-A-Million, America’s hometown bookstore since 1917, is headquartered in Birmingham, AL, and is home to a family of brands including Books-A-Million, 2nd & Charles, Joe Muggs, and Yogurt Mountain. We’re seeking an enthusiastic and motivated Assistant Buyer to join our Merchandising team supporting our Gift business. This entry-level, hybrid role is based at our Birmingham, AL corporate office and is ideal for a recent Merchandising graduate or someone with a combination of retail store experience and strong merchandising skills. You’ll start by mastering the fundamentals of the business – purchase orders, item creation, and vendor partnerships – while building toward buying for assigned categories. • Position: Assistant Buyer – Gifts • Department: Merchandising • Location: Birmingham, AL (Hybrid) Role Summary The Assistant Buyer supports the Gift buying team by managing the operational details that keep our assortment moving – from purchase order creation and tracking to item setup, SKU management, and on-time delivery. Working closely with their assigned Buyer, as well as outside vendors, the distribution center, stores, and internal marketing teams, the Assistant Buyer builds a strong foundation in merchandising and progressively takes on category buying responsibilities. This role thrives in a fast-paced, detail-oriented, and collaborative environment and is ideal for a self-starting, flexible, organized, and results-oriented team member who is eager to learn. Role Responsibilities Purchase Order & Item Management • Execute merchandising activities including the full life cycle of purchase orders, from PO creation and order entry through tracking and receipt. • Complete item creation and SKU management, maintaining data accuracy and integrity for the company. • Ensure timely delivery of merchandise via consistent communication and follow up with vendors and the distribution center. • Use company merchandising systems and Excel according to procedures to record all transactional activity, perform processes, and complete required analyses. • Maintain logical and clear working papers, spreadsheets, and checklists/calendars, monitoring the detail and quality of your own work. • Communicate regularly with stores using appropriate communication channels. Category & Vendor Support • Learn the vendor base and take initiative to develop collaborative vendor relationships, including cost negotiation, problem resolution, and follow up. • Produce sales recaps and analysis to identify new and existing business opportunities. Communicate findings and advocate for intended purchases. • Identify patterns, gaps, or related trends when reviewing data, and provide your Buyer with suggestions drawn from your analysis. • Develop planograms for in-store merchandise sets that drive sales and fixture productivity. • As skills develop, progress into buying for assigned Gift categories, including open-to-buy management. Buyer & Division Support • Monitor the latest trends and share with the Gift team to identify sales and marketing opportunities. • Execute contracts and incentives, including promotional partnerships. • Provide organizational support for cross-functional team projects by breaking assignments into tasks and coordinating with internal and external partners. • Monitor competitor merchandising and share findings with stakeholders. • Other duties as assigned by the Buyer, Divisional Merchandise Manager, or Vice President. Role Qualifications Required Qualifications: • Bachelor’s degree in merchandising or a business-related field, or equivalent combination of work experience • 1–2 years of retail or relevant experience, which may include retail store, customer service, or internship experience • Basic retail math skills and the ability to analyze data, identify trends, and draw conclusions • High standards, accountability, and a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail • Strong prioritization and time management skills, with a sense of urgency and the ability to re-prioritize as needs change • Clear, effective written and verbal communication; listens attentively and asks questions to confirm understanding • Intellectual curiosity, personal ownership, and a drive to learn and improve processes • Collaborative team player who builds strong internal and external partnerships and stays positive and adaptable under pressure Preferred Qualifications: • Passion for the gift industry; knowledge of and interest in popular culture and online trends, with a keen eye for developing trends • Degree or coursework in merchandising • Retail internship or retail store experience • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Outlook, and Word Work Environment & Expectations • This hybrid position is based at our Birmingham, AL corporate office: 4 days in office and 1 day remote, with Monday in office preferred. • Up to 25% travel to trade shows, vendor meetings, new stores, and store visits, depending on area assigned. • PTO blackout days may apply during the peak holiday season. • Company laptop provided; reliable home internet required for remote work days. The Perks At Books-A-Million, we believe in taking care of our employees. As part of the team, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive benefits package, including: Competitive Compensation: We offer competitive pay and performance-based incentives. Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance to keep you healthy. Paid Time Off (PTO): Enjoy generous PTO and paid holidays. Employee Discounts: Get discounts on books and other products across our stores. Retirement Savings: Build your future with our 401(k) plan and company contributions. Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Statement Books-A-Million is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming workplace. We celebrate and embrace differences, and we strive to create an environment where every individual feels valued and empowered. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to their background or personal characteristics. We are dedicated to creating a culture of respect, equity, and opportunity for all employees, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply.
