description: Moog is a performance culture that empowers people to achieve great things. Our people enjoy solving interesting technical challenges in a culture where everyone trusts each other to do the right thing. For you, working with us can mean deeper job satisfaction, better rewards, and a great quality of life inside and outside of work. Job Title Sr. Buyer/ Planner Reporting To Manager, Operations Work Schedule Onsite – Sunnyvale, CA Position Summary Moog’s Space & Defense Group is seeking an experienced Sr. Buyer/Planner to support its Mountain View operation. This role owns purchasing and material-planning activities for assigned programs in a high-mix, low-volume aerospace manufacturing environment. The Sr. Buyer/Planner converts approved program demand into executable purchase and production plans, manages supplier commitments and performance, and provides accurate material status so Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, and Program teams can meet cost, quality, and schedule commitments. The successful candidate is equally comfortable working in an ERP/MRP system, negotiating with suppliers, resolving shortages, and communicating clear recovery plans. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role requiring sound judgment, strong follow-through, and regular interaction with the production floor and supply base. Key Responsibilities Material Planning and Schedule Execution Analyze program demand, bills of material, inventory, open supply, lead times, and capacity constraints to develop practical material and production plans. Maintain accurate ERP/MRP planning parameters, including lead times, order policies, lot sizes, minimums/multiples, and required dates for assigned parts and suppliers. Convert authorized demand into purchase requisitions, purchase orders, work orders, and kit requests in accordance with company processes and approval limits. Create clear material-status, shortage, line-of-balance, and clear-to-build reporting; provide reliable completion and delivery dates to internal stakeholders. Expedite, de-expedite, reschedule, or cancel supply as demand changes to protect program schedules while reducing excess, obsolete, and premature inventory. Procurement and Supplier Performance Manage the end-to-end purchase-order lifecycle for raw material, components, commercial items, tooling, outside/special processing, and other production-related goods and services. Issue RFQs, evaluate bids, document source-selection rationale, perform price analysis, and negotiate price, lead time, delivery, and commercial terms within delegated authority. Develop and execute sourcing approaches for assigned commodities or programs using approved suppliers; coordinate new-supplier evaluation and onboarding with Quality and Engineering. Obtain timely supplier acknowledgments and commitments, monitor open orders and past-due items, lead routine status reviews, and escalate risks before they affect program milestones. Monitor supplier on-time delivery, quality, responsiveness, and cost performance; coordinate recovery plans, returns, nonconformance resolution, and corrective actions with Quality and other functions. Identify long-lead, constrained, and single-source risks and develop mitigation plans, including alternate-source or schedule-recovery options when appropriate. Compliance, Data, and Cross-Functional Execution Ensure purchase orders accurately include the current drawing/specification revision, quality requirements, contractual flowdowns, delivery requirements, and required supplier documentation. Maintain complete and accurate procurement records, approvals, pricing support, supplier correspondence, and system data in accordance with company and applicable customer/government requirements. Assess the supply-chain impact of engineering and configuration changes, including cost, lead time, existing inventory, open orders, and supplier implementation dates. Partner with Program Management, Project/Program Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, Receiving/Inventory, and Finance to resolve shortages, receiving discrepancies, invoice issues, and competing priorities. Use data and trend analysis to improve supplier performance, planning accuracy, inventory health, and procurement cycle time; participate in Lean and continuous-improvement activities. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Operations, Analytics, Engineering, or a related field and at least 5 years of relevant procurement/planning experience; OR an associate degree in a related field and at least 8 years of relevant experience; OR an equivalent combination of education and directly related experience. Demonstrated experience using an ERP/MRP system to manage demand, purchase orders, inventory, planning parameters, material shortages, and/or work orders in a manufacturing environment. Working knowledge of procurement fundamentals, including RFQs, bid evaluation, purchase-order administration, supplier negotiations, price analysis, and supplier performance management. Ability to work from bills of material, technical drawings/specifications, part revisions, and quality or contractual requirements with strong attention to detail. Strong Excel skills and the ability to organize, analyze, and communicate material and supplier data clearly. Ability to manage multiple priorities, make sound decisions with incomplete information, meet commitments, and escalate issues with a clear recommended action. Strong written and verbal communication skills, professional supplier-management skills, and a consistent sense of urgency. Ability to access U.S. export-controlled information. Preferred Qualifications Experience in aerospace, defense, space, or another regulated high-mix, low-volume manufacturing environment. Experience purchasing precision-machined parts, electromechanical components, raw materials, and outside/special processes. Working knowledge of AS9100, FAR/DFARS requirements, U.S. export controls, configuration control, and supplier-quality flowdowns. Experience with Moog Business Systems (MBS), Power BI, or similar planning and analytics tools. Ability to read technical drawings and understand basic GD&T. APICS CPIM/CSCP, ISM CPSM, or similar supply-chain certification. Experience supporting Lean manufacturing and structured continuous improvement. Salary Range Transparency Sunnyvale, CA $115,000.00–$150,000.00 Annually Salary Range Disclaimer The base salary range represents the low and high end of the Moog salary range for this position in the given work location. Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to location, experience, and performance. The range(s) listed is just one component of Moog's total compensation package for employees. Other rewards may include annual bonuses, employee stock purchase plan, an open paid time off policy, and many region-specific benefits. This position requires access to U.S. export-controlled information. Contract & Risk Management Support contract lifecycle activities, including contract review, administration, renewals, and compliance monitoring. Partner with Legal and business stakeholders to facilitate contract execution and maintain required documentation. Assist in identifying and mitigating supplier-related risks, including operational, financial, and compliance risks. Ensure procurement activities comply with company policies, procedures, and governance requirements. Cross-Functional Partnership Build effective working relationships with stakeholders across business functions. Provide procurement guidance, recommendations, and analytical support to internal customers. Collaborate with Finance, Legal, Operations, and other functional teams to support enterprise initiatives. Contribute to procurement process improvements and capability-building efforts. Procurement Excellence & Continuous Improvement Support the implementation of procurement best practices, tools, and methodologies. Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve efficiency, and enhance stakeholder experience. Maintain accurate procurement and supplier information within applicable systems and reporting tools. Participate in special projects and strategic initiatives as assigned. Experience supporting sourcing events, supplier negotiations, spend analytics, and supplier management activities. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate data into actionable recommendations. Experience working with contracts, supplier agreements, and procurement processes. Ability to influence stakeholders and build effective partnerships across multiple functions. Strong communication, presentation, and relationship management skills. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, procurement systems, spend analytics tools, and reporting platforms. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. Primary Purpose Implementation of the Supply Chain Process, inventory management, and investment recovery processes and programs. Note: This is a hybrid position (in-office with remote flexibility). Employees are required to be in office at least three days per week (Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday). This position must sit out of our Baltimore - MD office. This position is not eligible for relocation assistance. Primary Duties Support quality and cost objectives by developing and implementing sourcing strategies that ensure the total cost of materials and services purchased have considerable value and minimal risk. Support and perform activities that successfully implement the Supply Chain Process. Support quality and cost objectives by developing and implementing sourcing strategies that ensure the total cost of materials and services purchased have considerable value and minimize risk. Support the implementation of inventory management and investment recovery practices; support the maintenance and analysis of inventory performance measures and the planning and forecasting of inventory levels; and support investment recovery efforts. Support Category Managers and perform activities to source, manage, maintain, and implement contracts and purchase orders and the associated databases; and with supplier performance monitoring Support and perform day to day process resolution including: un-enterable invoices, supplier changes and adds, unit of measure changes, economies of scale identification and changes. Support and implement the process that monitors and reports out on supplier performance trends, savings opportunities and achieved, discounts, and settlement agreements. description: About Vantage Data Centers Vantage Data Centers powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands. Procurement Department The team leads these efforts from conception through commissioning, working with Sales, Operations, New Site Development, and Engineering along the way. Procurement also works closely with vendor partners to come up with a vertically integrated design, and we manage these partners to deliver the projects on schedule and budget. One thing that distinguishes Vantage is that our technical staff is given the responsibility and authority to directly drive the process. When compared to external resources, our internal team can align long-term operational sustainability with value engineering and cost metrics to deliver products aligned with corporate goals. This approach empowers each member of the team to drive high- impact decisions and even more impactful results. Position Overview This position will be based on-site at our office in Ashburn, VA in alignment with our flexible work policy (3 days on site required, 2 days flexible). Vantage is looking for a self-starter in the role of a Senior Procurement Analyst to be part of a team that manages OFCI Equipment, which is the second largest individual cost within the construction process, and to become engaged in the supply chain aspects of our Data Centers. In this role, you will be responsible for record keeping, assist in obtaining vendors submittals, maintaining product specifications, working with vendors, working with the Procurement team to ensure specifications are adhered to in accordance to our company process, monitor and managing contracts, prepare status and tracking reports for the company, support the Procurement Managers and Senior Director in their daily tasks. Regular collaboration and coordination are required with our supply chain partners and internal teams such as Engineering, Operations, Legal, as well as multiple Construction Management Teams. Travel will be necessary to various factories for factory witness testing, audits, and on-boarding of new vendors. Minimal travel to Vantage Data Center sites may also be required occasionally. Essential Job Functions The individual will be continuously working with the procurement team to provide the daily assistance needed to ensure the department meets and exceeds its goals with the company. Individual will be a self-starter and with the ability to manage and assist multiple single line diagrams, product specifications and driving OFCI Equipment submittals to closure (approval). Successful candidate will understand RFIs and RFQs for the sourcing of equipment for low voltage switchgear, medium switchgear, transformers, electrical skids, CRAH’s, chillers, generators, UPS’s and other data center equipment systems as needed. Coordinate with vendors on continuous quality improvement. Manage and track equipment status with the vendors such that all scheduled dates set by the construction schedules are met. Analyze and negotiate vendor quotes, change orders and back charges. Learn and manage the financial software to enter PO’s, review invoices, track budgets, allocate equipment from purchase to the projects. Support Procurement Managers and Finance / Accounting with invoicing issues. Drive project-level tasks and milestones assigned by the project management team. Coordinates with vendors for scheduling start-up and commissioning support services from the vendors Maintain and develop supplier relationships. Help develop and maintain record keeping and reports for the business. Continue to work and help refine the procurement processes to make sure they are complying and efficient. Work with compliance to maintain the department and vendors are within guidelines. Work with operational personnel of the Vantage buildings to ensure the proper spare parts and service programs are properly in place and assist with their database. Continue safety evaluations with vendors and project sites to make compliance is met. Senior Analyst should be able to manage the full OFCI equipment package on a VDC development project with minimal support/assistance from a Procurement Manager. Duties Collaborate with stakeholders to ensure clarity of the specifications and operational requirements. Work with finance and compliance to ensure all purchases have appropriately been costed to a project. Help coordinate the approval and release of the necessary equipment per construction schedule. Continue to investigate and work with vendors to make sure their products are best suited for Vantage. Support open and transparent communication with project teams for project delivery success. Negotiate complex requests for equipment and services from suppliers and subcontractors. Manage equipment inventory planning efforts and forecasting. Additional Duties as assigned by Management. description: About Blue Bird Corporation Blue Bird (NASDAQ: BLBD) is recognized as a technology leader and innovator of school buses since its founding in 1927. description: About Us Indelco Plastics is the leading supplier of corrosion-resistant thermoplastic products for fluid control and storage. This position plays a key role in aligning procurement strategies with organizational goals, ensuring supply continuity, and supporting cross-functional business operations within a manufacturing or industrial environment. Key Responsibilities Lead strategic sourcing initiatives to identify, evaluate, and select suppliers that align with company objectives for cost, quality, and sustainability. Negotiate long-term agreements, pricing, and supply terms with key suppliers to achieve optimal total cost of ownership. Monitor supplier performance using KPIs (e.g., on-time delivery, quality, cost savings) and implement supplier development plans as needed. Collaborate with engineering, quality, and operations teams to introduce new materials, components, or suppliers. Analyze market trends, commodity pricing, and risks to proactively mitigate supply disruptions. Serve as a subject matter expert for ERP purchasing workflows, supplier management, and procurement analytics. Develop and report procurement metrics, dashboards, and improvement projects using Power BI or Excel. Ensure sufficient supply of all materials and timing of deliveries across multiple sites through robust processes for purchase orders, blanket orders, transfer orders, and manufacturing orders. Proactively communicate cross-functionally expected delays, root cause of supplier issues, and countermeasures implemented to prevent occurrences. Continually look for opportunities to increase efficiency within the purchasing organization Create and maintain documentation around current and best practices for all steps within procurement. Mentor junior buyers and provide training on purchasing procedures and supplier engagement best practices. Demonstrated success in contract negotiation, supplier performance management, and strategic sourcing. Proficiency with ERP/MRP systems (e.g., Business Central, SAP, Oracle) and advanced Excel or Power BI skills. Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities Strong analytical, negotiation, and vendor management capabilities. Ability to lead cross-functional sourcing projects with minimal supervision. Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to present to senior leadership. Familiarity with sustainability initiatives and supplier ESG data collection preferred. Training & Development: FCG University is available to all employees, offering access to more than 80,000 learning courses to help you build new skills and advance your career. Equal Opportunity Employer: Flow Control Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. description: Shape the Future of Strategic Purchasing Are you a strategic thinker who thrives on building strong supplier partnerships, driving cost improvements, and supporting world-class manufacturing operations? In this highly visible role, you'll play a critical part in developing sourcing strategies, negotiating supplier agreements, supporting new product launches, and ensuring the uninterrupted flow of materials and services that keep our business moving forward. You'll collaborate closely with cross-functional teams throughout North America while helping drive purchasing excellence across our organization. Your Role As Our Senior Buyer, You Will Develop and execute sourcing strategies for automotive components, materials, tooling, equipment, and services. Lead supplier sourcing activities, including RFIs, RFQs, supplier evaluation, and supplier selection. Negotiate pricing, contracts, and commercial agreements to improve profitability and mitigate supply risks. Drive cost reduction, value engineering, and continuous improvement initiatives across assigned commodities. Monitor supplier performance related to quality, delivery, responsiveness, and overall service levels. Support new product launches by participating in APQP, PPAP, engineering changes, and program implementation activities. Identify and proactively address supply chain risks, capacity concerns, and market fluctuations. Develop and onboard new suppliers in partnership with Supplier Development Engineering and cross-functional teams. Collaborate with Engineering, Sales, Projects, Quality, Operations, Logistics, Production, and Supply Chain teams to achieve business objectives. Manage purchase orders, delivery schedules, supplier records, and procurement documentation within SAP and approved purchasing systems. Prepare purchasing metrics, analyses, and reports that support strategic decision-making and operational excellence. Build strong supplier relationships that support long-term business success and performance expectations. What You Bring to The Table We're seeking a procurement professional who combines strong business acumen with excellent relationship-building and negotiation skills. Required Qualifications 5-7 years of Procurement, Purchasing, or Supply Chain experience within the automotive industry. Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or a related field preferred. Experience managing supplier relationships and strategic sourcing initiatives. Strong negotiation, analytical, and problem-solving abilities. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications. Ability to work effectively with suppliers and stakeholders across multiple levels of the organization. Exceptional communication, organizational, and multitasking skills. Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Commitment to continuous improvement and operational excellence. Preferred Qualifications SAP experience. Knowledge of E-Procurement systems. Experience supporting automotive new product launches and supplier development initiatives. Understanding of APQP, PPAP, and automotive manufacturing processes. German language skills are a plus. Experience working within a global manufacturing organization. At GEDIA, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while working alongside talented professionals in a collaborative environment. A challenging and rewarding role supporting North American operations. Exposure to strategic sourcing initiatives and high-impact business decisions. Opportunities to collaborate with global purchasing teams and cross-functional leaders. A culture focused on teamwork, innovation, and continuous improvement. Professional growth and development opportunities. Competitive compensation and robust benefits package. The ability to influence supplier performance, operational success, and business results every day. ARE YOU READY? If you're an experienced purchasing professional who enjoys solving complex challenges, building strategic partnerships, and driving results, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and help us shape the future of procurement excellence at GEDIA Georgia.

description: Who We Are Biofire Technologies is on a mission to give gun owners better tools for reducing preventable gun injuries and deaths, especially among children. We believe our technology, combined with a best-in-class customer experience, will define the future of firearms safety for the next generation. Our mission-driven approach has earned support from the firearm community, the tech world, and the media. Biofire employees encompass a diverse range of talents, including world-class engineers who have designed and tested firearms, medical devices, robots, cars, satellites, rockets, and supersonic jets; expert technicians from aerospace, defense tech, special forces, and gunsmithing; and elite operators from high-tech, advanced manufacturing, and regulated industries. Whether building the product or powering the company behind it, every Biofire team member is united by an obsession with safety, reliability, and operational excellence. OUR CULTURE Reducing accidental firearm injuries and deaths requires original thinking and authentic collaboration, so we’re deeply invested in building a team and culture that can achieve our mission together. Team members enjoy autonomy and flexibility from day one, so expect to be immediately tasked with solving challenging problems and building new systems that work. We’ll hold you accountable for executing audacious goals, giving and receiving honest feedback, and helping your teammates succeed. You’ll receive respect, kindness, and support from every direction while you figure out how to get it all done. About The Role As a Senior Buyer at Biofire, you’ll own material readiness for an assigned portfolio of production parts as we scale manufacturing. Success means identifying supply constraints early enough to act within standard supplier lead times, maintaining healthy inventory levels, and keeping production supplied through supplier challenges and part transitions. You will own day-to-day supply planning and purchasing for your portfolio, maintaining accurate visibility into orders, supplier performance, and emerging risks. You’ll partner closely with Production Control, Engineering, Commodity Managers, Quality Engineers, and Finance to support Clear-to-Build (CTB) reviews and turn supply risks into clear, actionable plans. This role requires strong attention to detail, sound judgment under competing priorities, and the ability to anticipate how today’s supplier performance will affect tomorrow’s production volumes. You’ll also help strengthen shared planning tools and documented processes so the team can scale and provide reliable backup coverage. Key Responsibilities Own supply planning and purchasing for your assigned portfolio, maintaining material availability and inventory within established MIN/MAX levels. Maintain accurate purchase orders, lead times, and supplier commitments, clearly distinguishing firm orders from forecast quantities. Lead category-level Clear-to-Build (CTB) tracking and support weekly executive reviews with early visibility into constraints, mitigation plans, and financial exposure. Monitor supplier delivery, quality, and capacity trends; execute supply containment actions and coordinate corrective-action handoffs with Commodity Managers and supplier engineering/quality teams. Anticipate supplier risks as production scales and prioritize competing issues based on their impact on production continuity. Coordinate part transitions and last-time buys with Engineering and Production Control, balancing remaining inventory, yield, cycle time, and excess and obsolescence risks. Request volume pricing ahead of production ramps, obtain competitive quotes, and track purchase price variance and expedite spending in partnership with Commodity Managers and Finance. Strengthen shared planning tools and documented processes, including verified lead times, replenishment timing, and cross-coverage with your peer buyer. Qualifications We understand that not all applicants will possess skills that perfectly align with our job qualifications. At Biofire, we appreciate diverse experiences from various industries, and we encourage all individuals who meet the necessary qualifications to submit their applications. While having the "desired" qualifications may strengthen a candidate's profile, we also welcome applicants with alternative experiences to apply. A Bachelor’s degree in a technical or operational field (e.g. Engineering, Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering). An MBA, Master’s in Supply Chain or APICS CPIM Certification is a plus. 3–5 years of relevant experience in production purchasing, buying, supply planning, or supply chain management within a manufacturing environment. Practical experience in functions such as military, consulting, or finance operations will also be considered. An understanding of product lifecycles, BOM development, and how upstream planning impacts downstream execution. Creating purchase orders and subcontracted work orders and processing them through procurement and planning systems. Ensuring purchased goods meet quality, quantity, and delivery standards. Building and maintaining strong relationships with key suppliers. Managing planning parameters and stock levels to ensure adequate lead time and inventory on hand while avoiding overstocking. Monitoring MRP and project plans to plan purchases and minimize stockouts. Ensuring all purchases comply with company policies and industry regulations. description: The expected hiring range for this position is: $99,500.00-$130,900.00. Please note that the pay range information is a general guideline only. Fermi Forward Discovery Group, LLC (FFDG) manages and operates Fermilab on behalf of the US Department of Energy Office of Science (DOE). Within FFDG, the Finance Division provides safe, efficient, effective financial operations in support of the Laboratory's high-energy physics program in accordance with all laws, regulations, and DOE requirements. Within the section, the Procurement Department is responsible for acquiring goods and services for the entire Laboratory. It provides helpful, professional support for all procurement requirements from the development of initial plans and requirements to subcontract closeout. This Procurement Specialist role requires a strategic thinker with an acute understanding of the market, suppliers, and products to ensure that goods and services are procured at the best possible terms for Fermi Forward. These responsibilities are accomplished in cooperation with internal customers, FRA project teams, support personnel, subcontractors, and DOE, in accordance with established procurement policies and procedures, contract law, commercial practice, and applicable federal procurement regulations. This role will execute on known or anticipated opportunities in the acquisition of constructions services while contributing to cost savings, partnerships with suppliers and other value-added activities to support the work of the Laboratory. What your day-to-day as a Procurement Specialist IV at Fermilab will look like: Serve as a procurement subject matter expert in area of capital construction, architect and engineering (A/E), and special projects. Performs subcontract administration and ensures the completeness, organization, and accuracy of the subcontract file in compliance with subcontract terms and conditions, including timely delivery of goods and services, Buy American Act, Service Contract Act, Davis Bacon Act, workplace safety, insurance, payment, socio-economic provisions, and others as appropriate. Solicits request for proposals for highly complex subcontracting requirements, determines responsiveness of subcontractors to solicitation requirements, evaluates proposals, selects qualified potential subcontractors, conducts price and cost analysis, negotiates subcontract terms and conditions, draft contractual instruments, obtains approvals, and awards procurements. Plans and develops subcontracting requirements with internal Laboratory customers. Support FFDG compliance and self-assessment activities. Support audits and assessments, contractor procurement system reviews; collaborate with the DOE Fermi Site Office (FSO); ensure team compliance with the prime contract and applicable acquisition regulations; contribute to and support Procurement metrics gathering and reporting. Skills and Attributes for Success: A Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, English, Communications or relevant experience as a sourcing or procurement professional or equivalent combination of education and experience. 9 years of procurement experience. Understanding and administration of the Buy American Act, Service Contract Act, Davis Bacon Act, workplace safety, insurance, payment, socio-economic provisions. Experience with major construction procurement awards, Cost Reimbursable, Time & Material agreements as well as IDIQs/BOAs is preferred. Proven ability to plan, develop, negotiate, administer and close large, complex, high dollar value subcontracts. Experience with electronic word processing, spreadsheets, document sharing systems, mail and other common office tools. Experience working in a matrixed project team environment. Applicable Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required: Experience with federal contracting, particularly with the Department of Energy (DOE) and working knowledge of Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR). Professional Certifications as Certified Procurement Manager (CPM), Certified Federal Contract Manager (CFCM), Certified Professional Contracts Manager (CPCM) or Master’s Degree in Business / MBA preferred. Experience handling procurements for DOE projects. DOE Order 413.3b experience is a plus. Ability to abide by all environment, safety and health regulations. Willingness to respect, understand and value individual differences that embody laboratory principles. Onsite: This is an onsite role, and the candidate must be able to work from our Batavia office. Benefits/Perks: Fermilab offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits program, including: Medical, Dental, Vision and Flexible Spending Accounts Paid time off Life insurance Short and Long-term disability insurance Retirement benefits Onsite day care Why Fermilab: Fermilab is America’s premier laboratory for particle physics and accelerator research, funded by the U.S. Department of Energy. We support discovery science experiments in Illinois and locations around the world, including deep underground mines in South Dakota and Canada, mountaintops in Arizona and Chile, CERN in Europe and the South Pole. An offer of employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a background check and drug screening. To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete and pass a federal background check investigation. This investigation includes a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture. This includes marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws. Failure to obtain or maintain such government access authorization could result in the withdrawal of a job offer or future termination of employment. Such individuals will be asked to disclose any participation for review by Fermilab's Office of General Counsel. If a candidate is selected for an interview but does not possess any of the equivalent documents, we may schedule a virtual interview. description: About The Role Keep the science moving. As a Purchasing Assistant III, you are the person who gets researchers and staff the supplies and services they need, on time, on budget, and in line with Laboratory procurement policy. This is a fully remote position at the most experienced level of the Purchasing Assistant career ladder. You will work with a high degree of independence, solve complex problems, take on special projects, and help train colleagues. You will work with a wide mix of internal customers and outside suppliers, so strong relationships and clear communication matter as much as attention to detail. This role is fully remote Salary Range: $25.34– $36.75 based on years of related experience and internal equity considerations What You Will Do Place and manage orders. Review purchase requests for completeness and accuracy, prioritize them, and choose the best way to process each one based on cost, timing, and competitive bidding. Place orders with vendors, including orders for controlled substances, prescription drugs, and radioactive items, and confirm prices, availability, and delivery. All work follows Laboratory procurement policies and local, state, and federal guidelines. Keep accurate records. Update purchase orders in the computer system with a high degree of accuracy. Maintain records of supplies, amounts ordered and received, and actual sales for items and vendors. Follow through on delivery. Track orders so materials and services arrive on the promised dates. Work with vendors and end users. Coordinate, facilitate, and resolve day-to-day procurement issues. Coordinate on-campus vendor shows. Support and advise colleagues. Give routine advice and support to end users on the procurement process and documentation. Help with user training and problem resolution as needed. Find better sources. Seek new sources of supplies and services and secure favorable terms for the Laboratory. Support daily operations. Perform other duties as required, such as scheduling equipment maintenance and services, adjusting grant encumbrances and rolling them into the next year, maintaining the catalog library, and filing. Assist in the operation of a maintenance stock room and receiving dock. Requirements Education: High school diploma or GED. A combination of education and experience may be considered. Associate or bachelor’s degree preferred. Experience: 5 + years in the same or a similar role. Ability to draw solutions from a wider range of experience, adapt methods to solve complex problems, and resolve them in a timely manner. Demonstrated ability to guide and train others. Ability to negotiate the best price and service while working within Laboratory procurement policies and procedures. Proven ability to organize time, work under time constraints, meet deadlines, and prioritize work. Demonstrated ability to take over special projects and follow through to completion. Ability to perform basic information research, gather and compile data, and prepare reports. Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and accurate data entry. Effective interpersonal skills for working with a wide variety of people and personalities, including internal customers and external suppliers. Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing. Ability to operate computer hardware and software applications normally found in a business setting. Team player with positive and professional behavior, and the judgment to recognize the limits of your responsibility and direct issues to the appropriate people. Ability to lift a minimum of 50 pounds when assisting in the maintenance stock room or receiving dock. About JAX The Jackson Laboratory is an independent, nonprofit biomedical research institution with a National Cancer Institute-designated Cancer Center and nearly 3,000 employees in locations across the United States (Maine, Connecticut, California, New York, Florida), Japan and China. Its mission is to discover precise genomic solutions for disease and empower the global biomedical community in the shared quest to improve human health. Founded in 1929, JAX applies over nine decades of expertise in genetics to increase understanding of human disease, advancing treatments and cures for cancer, neurological and immune disorders, diabetes, aging and heart disease. It models and interprets genomic complexity, integrates basic research with clinical application, educates current and future scientists, and provides critical data, tools and services to the global biomedical community. For more information, please visit www.jax.org . EEO Statement The Jackson Laboratory provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment in all job classifications without regard to race, color, religion, age, mental disability, physical disability, medical condition, gender, sexual orientation, genetic information, ancestry, marital status, national origin, veteran status, and other classifications protected by applicable state and local non-discrimination laws.

description: Job Summary General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), an affiliate of General Atomics, is a world leader in proven, reliable remotely piloted aircraft and tactical reconnaissance radars, as well as advanced high-resolution surveillance systems. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: This position is responsible for supervising the process of procuring materials, parts, components, services, and equipment under government or commercial contract(s). This includes activities such as: Review of work statements Preparation of solicitations Conducting of bidder conferences Proposal analysis and evaluations Terms and Conditions negotiations Coordination with Engineering, Manufacturing, Programs and other internal stakeholders Contract award review and approval Contract administration including oversight of supplier deliveries and quality throughout the period of performance, as well as change management Act as primary contact for purchasing activities with management and internal stakeholders. Provide advice relating to issues with government and commercial purchase orders. May represent the company with customers, potential customers and suppliers. Support production schedules by assisting in planning activities and monitoring buys. Interpret and execute Supply Chain policies and procedures for the compliant operation of Procurement activities. Recommend modifications to operating policies as needed. Keep abreast of best practices in supply chain and materials management. Coordinate and review confidentiality agreements, non-compete justifications, commercial item determinations, price analyses, terms and conditions, license agreements and other documentation for conformance to business objectives and company policies. Assign tasks, review work, and provide direction to staff while ensuring purchasing processes are met within established timelines. Assist with challenges and help to develop innovative solutions to resolve complex issues. Lead and participate in customer proposal efforts by obtaining supplier quotes and proposals, which may include subcontractor costs and pricing data. Perform price analysis and negotiations as appropriate, provide all supporting documentation to proposal team. Participate in various internal and external audits, including government and customer audits. Manage and actively participate in the planning, attraction, selection, retention, and development of human resources to ensure the availability of required management and professional talent. Maintain the strict confidentiality of sensitive information. Responsible for ensuring all laws, regulations and other applicable obligations are observed wherever and whenever business is conducted on behalf of the company. Responsible for ensuring work is accomplished in a safe manner in accordance with established operating procedures and practices. Perform other duties as assigned or required. We recognize and appreciate the value and contributions of individuals with diverse backgrounds and experiences and welcome all qualified individuals to apply. Job Qualifications Typically requires a Bachelor's degree in business administration or a related discipline and nine or more years of progressive experience interpreting, awarding and administering contractual agreements. May substitute equivalent experience in lieu of education. Must have demonstrated experience in the concepts, principles, and standard practices of supply chain management and purchasing and an extensive knowledge of contract construction, Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), FAR supplements, and the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC). Must be capable of coordinating inter-organizational activities and recommending creative solutions to complex issues. The ability to document, investigate, advise, interpret and explain complex issues or technical information to internal staff at all levels throughout the organization as well as external customers and suppliers is also required. Must have experience negotiating complex purchases and subcontracts and conducting briefings while having a detailed and comprehensive understanding of materials requirements planning. Job Type: Full-Time Salary Salary range: 90,500 - 155,375

description: St. Louis, MO | Full-Time | Non-Exempt WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT Most procurement postings read like a checklist: process POs, chase vendors, update spreadsheets. This one isn't that. You'll be the person who decides how materials actually get where they need to be - negotiating with vendors, allocating stock against real project deadlines, and catching problems before they become someone else's emergency. We're less interested in whether you've used a specific ERP system before and more interested in how you think when something doesn't add up: do you dig in, or wait to be told what to do? What Makes This Opportunity Different Real ownership from day one - you'll manage vendor relationships and purchasing decisions, not just process paperwork someone else decided on A steep, fast learning curve across fire/life safety, security, and AV systems - genuinely interesting products, not commodity parts Direct visibility into how your work affects project timelines and customer commitments - you'll see the impact of a good (or bad) sourcing call A small, family-owned company where you're not a cog - leadership knows your name and your work Room to grow into senior procurement, category management, or supply chain analytics based on where your strengths take you About Tech Electronics Tech Electronics is a St. Louis-based, employee-focused technology services company specializing in low-voltage life safety and communication systems - fire alarm, security, video surveillance, and AV - across the education, healthcare, construction, government, commercial, and worship sectors. We've been doing this for nearly 60 years, with nine offices across the Midwest and Colorado, and we still run like a family business because we are one. The Role - What You'll Actually Do This role blends hands-on purchasing execution with the judgment calls that keep material flowing. Roughly: Purchase Order Execution & Vendor Negotiation (40%) Place and manage purchase orders with vendors across our supplier network Negotiate pricing, discounts, and terms - this directly affects our margins and project profitability Build real working relationships with vendor reps so you're first in line when something's tight or short Spot and resolve pricing discrepancies, lead-time issues, and order problems before they escalate Inventory Allocation & Delivery Management (35%) Allocate stock to the right due dates, balancing internal project needs against external customer commitments Track orders proactively - catch delays early and coordinate corrective action with vendors and internal teams Work across branches to resolve shortages, transfers, and urgent material needs Reporting & Continuous Improvement (25%) Maintain accurate, useful inventory, usage, and quality/failure reports Use data to spot patterns - which vendors are reliable, where costs are creeping, what's about to run short Bring ideas for doing this better - we're not precious about "the way it's always been done" What We're Looking For We hire for how someone thinks before we hire for what they already know. In order of what actually matters to us: Intangibles - this is what we can't teach Grit - you follow through on the unglamorous parts of a job, not just the interesting ones Curiosity - you ask why a process works the way it does instead of just running it Flexibility - you can shift from a vendor negotiation to a shortage crisis to a report, all in one afternoon Independent thinking - you make a reasonable call when the answer isn't written down, and you know when to ask Analytical Comfort - how you use tools and logic Comfortable working with numbers, spreadsheets, and systems to make decisions, not just record them Can look at a report and notice what's wrong or what's changing, without being told to look for it Picks up new software quickly - we use Acumatica ERP; you don't need to know it already, but you should be the type who figures systems out fast Domain Knowledge - the part we're happy to teach Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, or related field - or equivalent experience that tells the same story Two or more years working with computer systems, including MS Office Procurement, purchasing, or vendor-facing experience is a real plus, but we'll hire the right thinker over the right resume keyword WORK ENVIRONMENT & SCHEDULE Location: St. Louis office Schedule: Monday–Friday, standard business hours Travel: Minimal - occasional vendor visits possible Reports to: Supply Chain Leadership Compensation & Benefits Competitive pay commensurate with experience Health, vision & dental insurance starting day one Company cell phone Paid time off & accrued personal time Tuition reimbursement Long-term & short-term disability coverage Generous holiday schedule Teladoc, SurgeryPlus & other medical benefits Growth paths into senior procurement, category management, or supply chain analytics roles Who Thrives In This Role You're someone who: Gets restless doing the same task the same way forever - you want to find a better process, not just run the existing one Doesn't need every answer handed to you - you'll dig, ask, and make a defensible call Actually enjoys the puzzle of getting the right material to the right place at the right time Wants to be known by name, not by employee number - and is comfortable with leadership actually knowing your work READY TO APPLY? If you're the kind of person who gets curious about why something broke instead of just fixing it and moving on, we want to talk to you. description: Job Description Join Our Team! Join WAVE and play a key role in supporting the procurement activities that keep our manufacturing and business operations running efficiently. As a Procurement Specialist / Buyer I, you will work across multiple functions and locations, partnering with internal teams and suppliers to source materials and services, manage purchasing activities, analyze spending trends, and support strategic procurement initiatives. This position offers the opportunity to build relationships across Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, Engineering, Maintenance, and supplier partners while gaining exposure to sourcing, supplier management, procurement analytics, compliance, and business operations. Your work will directly contribute to ensuring the right goods and services are available at the right time, cost, and quality to support WAVE's continued success. We are looking for a proactive, analytical, and customer-focused professional who enjoys solving problems, managing priorities, and collaborating with others to deliver results in a dynamic manufacturing environment. Responsibilities Source and procure indirect materials, equipment, services, and maintenance-related purchases that support WAVE operations across multiple locations. Manage the purchasing process from supplier quotation through purchase order creation, order tracking, and delivery coordination. Evaluate suppliers and sourcing alternatives to support cost savings, quality, service, business continuity, and operational requirements. Build and maintain supplier relationships, serving as a primary point of contact for purchasing inquiries, delivery issues, and performance-related concerns. Support supplier onboarding, contract administration, and compliance activities, ensuring required documentation and records are maintained. Monitor supplier performance and open orders, expediting critical purchases and resolving supply, delivery, or service issues as needed. Partner with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Finance, and Supply Chain teams to understand business requirements and support purchasing needs. Prepare and analyze procurement data, including spend reports, supplier metrics, savings opportunities, and key performance indicators. Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance procurement processes, reporting capabilities, supplier engagement, and overall efficiency. Ensure procurement activities comply with company policies, sourcing standards, audit requirements, and regulatory obligations. Other duties as assigned. Desired Experience 2-4 years of experience in procurement, purchasing, sourcing, supplier management, supply chain, vendor management, finance, accounts payable, or related business functions. Experience working in a manufacturing, industrial, or multi-site environment preferred. Experience utilizing ERP systems, purchasing platforms, supplier portals, or financial systems. Experience managing purchase orders, supplier communications, contract administration, spend analysis, or procurement reporting. Working knowledge of sourcing methodologies, supplier management, and purchasing processes. Experience using SAP, Power BI, Power Apps, or similar business systems preferred. Professional certifications or coursework in procurement, supply chain, operations, or business disciplines are a plus. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Understanding of procurement, purchasing, supplier management, and business operations processes. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail. Effective verbal and written communication skills. Strong customer service and relationship management capabilities. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, reporting tools, and ERP systems. Ability to analyze purchasing and supplier data to identify trends and opportunities. Ability to work collaboratively across functions and organizational levels. Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on process efficiency and operational effectiveness. Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive business information appropriately. Compensation And Benefits Hiring Range: $61,583 - $75,383 annually Individual compensation will be determined based on qualifications, relevant experience, skills, certifications, internal equity, and business considerations. WAVE Provides a Comprehensive Benefits Package That Includes Medical, dental, and vision coverage Health savings and flexible spending accounts 401(k) savings plan with company contributions Paid time off and company holidays Life and disability insurance Employee assistance programs Professional development and training opportunities About Us Our Company is proud to have a dynamic and inclusive workforce where employees are empowered to innovate, thrive and grow. We believe that each employee’s unique strengths contribute to the success of our organization. This belief extends to how we consider our job applicants. Your talents may align with this position or other opportunities within our organization. Apply today to start unlocking your career potential with Worthington Enterprises. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities in the application and hiring process. If you are interested in employment with Worthington Enterprises and need an accommodation or assistance using the careers website, please contact careers@wthg.com. Worthington Enterprises (NYSE: WOR) is a designer and manufacturer of market-leading brands that help improve everyday life by elevating spaces and experiences. The Company operates with two primary business units: Building Products and Consumer Products. The Building Products segment includes cooking, heating, cooling and water solutions, architectural and acoustical grid ceilings and metal framing and accessories. The Consumer Products segment provides solutions for the tools, outdoor living and celebrations categories. Product brands within the Worthington Enterprises portfolio include Balloon Time®, Bernzomatic®, Coleman® (propane cylinders), CoMet®, Elgen, Garden Weasel®, General®, HALO™, Hawkeye™, Level5 Tools®, Mag Torch®, NEXI™, Pactool International®, PowerCore™, Ragasco®, Well-X-Trol® and XLite™, among others. Founded in 1955 as Worthington Industries, Worthington Enterprises follows a people-first Philosophy with earning money for its shareholders as its first corporate goal. Headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, Worthington Enterprises and its joint ventures employ approximately 6,000 people throughout North America and Europe.

We attribute the prominence of the Coach brand to the unique combination of our original American attitude and design, our heritage of fine leather goods and custom fabrics, our superior product quality, and our commitment to the customer experience. At Coach, we bring together strong, collaborative people in a culture of mutual respect, support, accountability, and passion for the brand and product. Primary Purpose Strategic, operational Omni channel Assistant Buyer for North America-Men's Leather Goods, Bags & Specialty Accessories. The successful individual will leverage their proficiency to… Run weekly, monthly, and quarterly selling reports to recap and analyze business, making recommendations for driving improved performance and identifying opportunities. description: About Laurel Valley Farms Laurel Valley Farms is one of the largest mushroom substrate producers in the United States. Based in southeastern Pennsylvania, our primary focus is transforming agricultural materials into over 200,000 tons of phase 2 substrate annually, supporting the production of more than 100 million pounds of fresh mushrooms each year. We combine that scale and expertise with a commitment to innovation, long-term stewardship, and continuous improvement. We believe strong products start with strong processes and strong people. Our team combines deep industry experience, quality-focused production, customer-first service, and reliable logistics. For driven employees, Laurel Valley offers an opportunity to help grow a practical, entrepreneurial business with a larger vision to be the trusted leader in premium mushroom substrate and symbiotic value-added products. Fueled by Fungi and a Force for Local Good. Position Summary The Procurement Manager serves as the primary purchaser for Laurel Valley Farms, coordinating companywide purchases of supplies, parts, fuel, and fertilizer while assisting Operations with raw material purchasing and the maintenance shop with parts sourcing and purchasing as needed. This position manages the full purchase order process, from PO creation and required approvals through ordering, delivery tracking, receiving, and accurate ERP records. The Procurement Manager develops and maintains purchasing procedures, approval workflows, and ERP purchasing and receiving processes that strengthen accountability, visibility, and cost control. Working closely with suppliers and internal departments, this role compares purchasing options, negotiates pricing and terms, and ensures purchases meet operational needs and delivery requirements. The Procurement Manager is expected to put Laurel Valley Farms’ core values into practice: Continuous Improvement, Empowered Leadership, Integrity, Sustainability, One Team, and Accountability. Key Responsibilities Serve as the primary purchaser for the company, coordinating purchases of supplies, parts, fuel, fertilizer. Manage the full purchase order process, including creating POs, obtaining required approvals, placing orders, tracking deliveries, and coordinating receiving activities and accurate ERP entries. Develop and maintain purchasing procedures, approval workflows, and ERP purchasing and receiving processes that provide clear accountability, visibility, and cost control. Assist Operations with raw material purchasing and the maintenance shop with parts sourcing and purchasing as needed. Obtain and compare supplier quotes, availability, lead times, and freight costs; negotiate pricing, payment terms, and delivery requirements. Develop and maintain supplier relationships, evaluate performance, and establish alternative sources for critical supplies and materials. Coordinate with departments to anticipate purchasing needs, monitor supply levels, and schedule deliveries to support operations and maintenance. Verify that received goods match purchase orders and specifications; coordinate resolution of shortages, damaged goods, returns, and supplier issues. Maintain accurate supplier, pricing, purchasing, and receiving records; work with Accounting to resolve PO, receipt, and invoice discrepancies. Monitor spending and purchasing trends, identify savings opportunities, and improve purchasing efficiency without compromising quality or reliability. Coordinate with departments to verify services were completed as agreed, match service invoices to approved quotes and purchase orders, and resolve discrepancies with vendors and Accounting before payment. Perform other procurement and purchasing duties as assigned. Required Qualifications Strong negotiation and supplier relationship-management skills. Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple suppliers, orders, and priorities and follow through on commitments. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and standard business software. Ability to understand material specifications, pricing structures, freight costs, and inventory requirements. Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across departments. Ability to work independently, establish structure in developing processes, and implement practical systems and procedures in a growing business, using sound judgment and escalating significant risks appropriately. Preferred Qualifications Three to five years of experience in purchasing, procurement, supply chain, materials management, agriculture, manufacturing, landscaping, horticulture, or a related field. Experience building a procurement function or implementing purchasing processes, sourcing strategies, supplier networks, or vendor-management systems. Experience purchasing agricultural inputs, bulk or organic materials, construction materials, or manufacturing inputs. Experience with ERP, purchasing, inventory, or accounting systems. This position requires working in the office 100% in Landenberg, PA and cannot be performed remotely. Salary commensurate with experience. Excellent benefits including medical, dental, vision, paid time off, and a 401k Plan with a 5% employer match.   Local candidates preferred as no relocation assistance will be provided.  ***Send your resume to: HR@LaurelValleyFarms.net, not through LinkedIn.*** Laurel Valley Farms is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace where employees can grow, contribute, and succeed.

description: Landscape Procurement Manager Job Summary The Landscape Procurement Manager is responsible for overseeing the sourcing, purchasing, and vendor management to support landscape operations. Knowledge of landscape materials, plant sourcing, and irrigation. Excellent communication skills for coordinating across field crews, vendors, and leadership. Working Conditions Primarily office-based with periodic visits to nurseries, material yards, and job sites. May require occasional travel to vendor locations or industry trade shows.
